**Here’s what you need to know about Jim Jordan’s greatest hits:**

**Backing a nationwide abortion ban.** Ohio voters protected reproductive freedom in 2023. Jordan has spent years pushing to ban abortion across the country, including right here at home.

**Serving as Trump’s chief election denier in Congress.** The January 6th Committee called him “a significant player” in Trump’s push to overturn the 2020 election. When the committee subpoenaed him, he refused to comply.

**Founding the House Freedom Caucus.** It’s a group so extreme that even Republican Speaker John Boehner called Jordan a “legislative terrorist.”

**Supporting cuts to Social Security and Medicare.** These are the programs Ohio seniors spent their whole working lives paying into.

**Leading government shutdowns.** He pushed spending cuts that hit working families hardest.

**And the cherry on top:** a nonpartisan study from Vanderbilt and the University of Virginia ranked him among the least effective Republicans in the House. Turns out all those cable news hits don’t leave much time for passing laws.

**That’s the guy who will lead House Republicans for the next two years. He’ll be fighting Sherrod Brown’s agenda in Washington, and Ohio Republicans will be taking their cues from his extremist playbook back home.**

Peter,

America was a global leader in eliminating measles. As of today, we've lost our elimination status as a measles outbreak threatens thousands of lives across our country. This dangerous setback was 100% avoidable and is the result of one person: RFK Jr.

**RFK Jr. should be immediately removed as Secretary of Health and Human Services.**

[_**I sent an official letter calling on the president to fire RFK Jr. because he is a woefully unqualified leader who is putting the lives of our people at risk. Will you add your name and join me?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143620941/660823925/372325113?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_PT_RFKJr_261117_T1_1&ms=ITT_ATA_EM_PT_RFKJr_261117_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODQ4OWIzNTMtZTNlMi1mMTExLTkxZjMtMDAwZDNhNTMzOTc4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6qJL0AxsIV51oT1ztAot6BTRHZweDVrNX1O9MHTTDHs=&emci=5b15ef13-b7e2-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=8489b353-e3e2-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=17458827) [REMOVE RFK](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143620942/660823926/372325113?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_PT_RFKJr_261117_T1_1&ms=ITT_ATA_EM_PT_RFKJr_261117_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODQ4OWIzNTMtZTNlMi1mMTExLTkxZjMtMDAwZDNhNTMzOTc4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6qJL0AxsIV51oT1ztAot6BTRHZweDVrNX1O9MHTTDHs=&emci=5b15ef13-b7e2-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=8489b353-e3e2-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=17458827) Under RFK’s watch, the worst measles outbreak in decades has topped 4,000 cases. Whooping cough, E. coli and tetanus are on the rise. Everything from baby formula to cheddar cheese has been pulled from shelves. And through it all, he keeps spreading wild conspiracy theories about vaccines. It’s crazy, and it’s dangerous.

Families across Kentucky and the country deserve better.

People should be able to buy frozen blueberries at the grocery store without worrying about getting sick. They deserve to know that their kids are protected from diseases we beat decades ago. clean_body: Sign on to add your voice to my letter now. Peter, America was a global leader in eliminating measles. As of today, we've lost our elimination status as a measles outbreak threatens thousands of lives across our country. This dangerous setback was 100% avoidable and is the result of one person: RFK Jr. RFK Jr. should be immediately removed as Secretary of Health and Human Services. Under RFK’s watch, the worst measles outbreak in decades has topped 4,000 cases. Whooping cough, E. coli and tetanus are on the rise. Everything from baby formula to cheddar cheese has been pulled from shelves. And through it all, he keeps spreading wild conspiracy theories about vaccines. It’s crazy, and it’s dangerous. Families across Kentucky and the country deserve better. People should be able to buy frozen blueberries at the grocery store without worrying about getting sick. They deserve to know that their kids are protected from diseases we beat decades ago. And they should be able to trust that our health departments are well-funded and prepared for future outbreaks. That’s just common sense and basic decency. Thank you, Andy | | Kentucky Gov. _**Amplified Here:**_
##### Russia invaded Ukraine, bombed its cities, and threatened its neighbors. So Trump's envoys asked Moscow to help design Europe's next security deal. The arsonist is now advising the fire department.
##### David's piece looks at:
##### \- what Putin actually wants from Europe
##### \- why NATO's eastern flank is alarmed
##### \- what pro-Kremlin media say Putin's Security Council just decided about Zelensky
##### \- what a real peace has to include.
##### For $70 a year, you get independent progressive media that won't confuse peace with capitulation.
##### [Upgrade now and read the rest.](https://substack.com/redirect/27bb00f0-97a5-4e5f-a12b-10b7be919c80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.VaqpwyZocM8QKuhlsW8roBpkLuC7xEb6MhTX8L6Z42I?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=225262170)
Once upon a time, American diplomats understood a basic proposition: When a thief breaks into your neighbor's house, you do not invite that criminal to redesign the neighborhood security program. You certainly do not ask what sort of alarms the burglar prefers.
Yet, this is now the governing philosophy of the Trump administration.
Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner and Trump friend/real estate developer Steve Witkoff have been leading negotiations between Russia and Ukraine and recently engaged with Vladimir Putin about the future of European security.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27bb00f0-97a5-4e5f-a12b-10b7be919c80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
According to recent reports, the Trump administration representatives sought Russian input on a new security arrangement for Europe.
The spectacle is difficult to comprehend. Russia invaded Ukraine, seized its territory, bombed its cities, murdered its civilians, and has spent years threatening the security of other European nations, especially those sending help to Ukraine. Yet now, the Trump clowns are treating Putin not just as a participant in negotiations but as an expert consultant on the proper organization of European security.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27bb00f0-97a5-4e5f-a12b-10b7be919c80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It is extraordinary. The arsonist has been invited to advise the fire department.
Kushner and Witkoff are hardly the diplomatic equivalent of George Kennan (U.S.
diplomat known for the Cold War strategy of containment) or Dean Acheson
(Truman's secretary of state who helped form NATO). The Kushner/Witkoff records
offer no evidence of experience in international security that would qualify
someone to negotiate the future of an alliance system involving dozens of
nations and the security of hundreds of millions of people. Their only
qualification appears to be their allegiance to Donald Trump. In other words,
Kushner and Witkoff aren't reassuring even to begin with.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a983dc9e-d52e-4788-845c-866f87491c88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The issue is not whether American representatives or even Trump stooges should talk to Putin. They should. Diplomacy requires talking to unpleasant people, including dictators who have demonstrated an enthusiasm for violence. The issue is whether American negotiators understand the difference between listening to an adversary and allowing the Russian tyrant to dictate the terms of the discussion.

name: Alex Padilla
subject: Priorities
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Padilla for Senate This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail
body:
#

Friends,
It’s been a few weeks since Election Day, and after the excitement of winning our new majorities, everyone is turning to the question of what comes next.
So I wanted to lay out for you a little bit about my priorities and some of what I will be pushing my colleagues to accomplish with our new majorities in the House and the Senate:
The American people spoke loud and clear in this election: they want us to act quickly and make life more affordable for working families across the country. Democrats must deliver on that mandate.
It means bringing down gas and diesel prices and ending the illegal, unauthorized war in Iran.
It means reversing Trump’s tax cuts for the ultra-rich, restoring the tax credit subsidies for people who got their healthcare through the Affordable Care Act, and undoing the massive cuts the Trump administration made to Medicaid.
And it means ending the tariffs that are driving up the price of goods for American families and making life more expensive for everyone.
The American people also want accountability. They are tired of watching Donald Trump and his administration abuse their power, break the law, and enrich themselves at our expense.
We cannot just “move on” and look the other way. We must investigate and, if we find wrongdoing, we must **hold them accountable.**
More than twice as many people have died in ICE and CBP detention since the start of Trump’s term than in the previous two years: that is not something we can let get swept under the rug. _**Justice is coming for everyone that broke the law.**_
In the midterm elections, we saw billions of dollars in Super PAC and dark money spending. Democrats must do everything in our power to overturn _Citizens United_ and get big money out of politics, including pushing for a constitutional amendment.
And it’s time to ban the President, Vice President, and Members of Congress from trading stocks in office.
Let me leave you with this: I understand that in this month’s election results, the American people have delivered a mandate for change.
This was not a small win. These were not victories that were eked out and majorities that were eked out. It was a resounding message by the people: bring down our costs, let's turn this around. We have had enough of the incompetence and cruelty of the Trump administration.
That is the work we have ahead of us. And we cannot shy away from it. Democrats must come in with big bold ideas and be ready to take big swings to improve lives across California and across the country.
Thanks and more soon.
Sen. Alex Padilla

* * *

_Wait, before you go..._
**Alex is hard at work preparing for the next Congress and making sure that Democrats use their new majorities to improve the lives of Californians and working families across the country. That work is not easy, but it is important.**
[**If you can afford it, please chip in $5 or whatever feels right to help Alex keep fighting for California in the U.S. Senate. It means a lot to Alex and to all of us to have your support. **[DONATE](https://act.alex-padilla.com/go/553?c0=padilla-em-nov26.IBznFA&refcode=em261117-1-270&t=2&akid=1949%2E159979%2ETIb6ud)**
[](https://www.youtube.com/@AlexPadillaforUSSenate) [](https://www.tiktok.com/@alexpadilla4ca) [](https://x.com/AlexPadilla4CA) [](https://www.facebook.com/alexpadilla4ca/) [](https://www.instagram.com/alexpadilla4ca/?hl=en)

Peter, From coast to coast, voters across the country delivered a historic blue wave, and some of the most remarkable victories came out of Georgia. Georgia voters elected Keisha Lance Bottoms as the state's first Black woman governor. subject: 🧡 One signature away from 218. Let's talk about the road ahead in Congress.
body:
Join us November 18 to discuss what's next in our fight for citizenship. | | | Hi Peter, 🧡 **We're just ONE signature away from reaching 218 signatures on the Dream & Promise Act discharge petition in the House!** After years of organizing, advocacy, and communities raising their voices, we're on the verge of a major milestone in our fight for a pathway to citizenship. The Dream & Promise Act would create a pathway to citizenship for more than 4.4 million people, including DACA recipents, TPS and DED holders, and immigrant youth. Young people, families, and allies have shown up again and again. We've sent over **78,000 letters and made over 2,600 calls** to Congress to demand action. **Together, we've proven that when we organize, we can make real change. Congress has heard from us loud and clear. Now it's time for lawmakers to act!** One more signature would give the Dream & Promise Act the 218 signatures needed to trigger the process to force a vote on the House floor. The American people overwhelmingly support a pathway to citizenship, and Congress must listen. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan (right) and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres welcome President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen during the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, on November 11, 2026. Photo by Rasit Aydogan/Anadolu via Getty Images.
The Trump administration decided for the second year running to ignore the annual UN climate talks, which opened last week in Antalya, Turkey. But the companies behind one of the most successful recent corporate campaigns against climate rules showed up in force, and their PR company is handling communications for host country Turkey.
At least 41 people from seven companies that participated in a secretive and ultimately successful lobbying campaign to roll back a key European climate law are registered for COP31, according to a UN list of participants reviewed by Drop Site. Most of them are not registered under their companies' names.
Back in 2024, the European Union passed a climate law--called the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD)--requiring its biggest companies, including American corporations doing business there, to do three things: adopt and follow a plan to cut emissions in line with the Paris Agreement's goal of holding the global temperature increase to 1.5 degrees Celsius, clean up human rights and environmental abuses in their supply chains, and answer to victims of such abuses in an EU-wide court.
In response, an alliance of 11 multinational corporations formed a group calling itself the "Competitiveness Roundtable." Its members included Chevron, ExxonMobil, Koch, TotalEnergies, Honeywell, Baker Hughes, Dow, Nyrstar, Enterprise Mobility and JPMorgan Chase, the largest financier of fossil fuels. Between March and August 2025, the group held 17 coordination meetings, according to leaked [documents published](https://substack.com/redirect/35271452-8028-4eff-bfb2-164423763cf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Dutch research group SOMO. Teneo, a New York-based PR and advisory firm, coordinated it.
By 2026, their mission had been accomplished and the CSDDD had been gutted.
The 41 people from Competitiveness Roundtable companies registered at COP31 are not the only industry representives at the conference. More than 100 companies and groups linked to fossil fuels were [identified last week ](https://substack.com/redirect/0a995033-7fdb-420f-a241-185c06dcced1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)by the [Kick Big Polluters Out coalition](https://substack.com/redirect/c7d62491-ec1b-4f5e-a586-badfe9ec0799?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Teneo, the Competitiveness Roundtable's publicist, currently has a $3.9 million contract to handle communications for COP31's host, the government of Turkey.
Drop Site asked the seven companies--ExxonMobile, Dow, Baker Hughes, Honeywell, JPMorganChase, Total Energy, and Chevron--and Teneo about their participation in the Competitiveness Roundtable. None of them provided comments.
## **" Divide and Conquer"**
The Roundtable's strategy was explicit. It planned to "[divide and conquer in the Council](https://substack.com/redirect/35271452-8028-4eff-bfb2-164423763cf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," the body of EU governments, by assigning member companies to work specific capitals. It aimed to sideline "stubborn" EU departments and to push the center-right European People's Party to side with the far right "as much as possible." SOMO found at least three meetings in the documents that do not appear in the EU's lobbying transparency register at all, and eight more that listed only Teneo, not the Roundtable lobbying participants, at plenary sessions in Strasbourg.
And it foregrounded Trump's tariffs on EU goods. The Roundtable discussed using European carmakers' desperation for tariff relief to get the CSDDD scrapped or diluted "as a concession in negotiations on tariffs," according to the SOMO documents. Chevron and ExxonMobil were assigned to build pressure from outside Europe by pushing climate laws up the agenda of the U.S.-EU trade talks.
Many of the companies never said a word against the law in public. Instead, they lobbied the member states behind the scenes and largely kept their opposition quiet. ExxonMobil did speak out. Chairman and CEO Darren Woods, attending COP31 under the badge of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, [told Bloomberg](https://substack.com/redirect/4a7388e2-e94f-468f-9670-1865613fa38c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2025 it was "the worst piece of legislation I've seen since I've been in this job," and [said](https://substack.com/redirect/93d68759-e67c-4aa6-8824-fc9ed7c46f2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its penalties would be "bone-crushing." In another interview, Woods [said](https://substack.com/redirect/93d68759-e67c-4aa6-8824-fc9ed7c46f2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he had spoken directly with Trump about the European law. That year, in response to criticism from companies in France and Germany, the European Commission proposed a set of changes to weaken the regulations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/52d1ea2f-ba4d-40b9-ba16-f32d5930f531?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen shakes hands with U.S. President Donald Trump during a meeting at Trump Turnberry golf club on July 27, 2025 in Turnberry, Scotland. Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images.
Within six months, the deal was done. On July 27, 2025, at Trump's Turnberry golf resort in Scotland, he and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen agreed to a 15% ceiling on most EU goods, including cars.
The fine print came on August 21, in a [joint statement](https://substack.com/redirect/bab0aecd-2b4a-4c0a-8e17-528794fc358e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published by the White House in which the EU committed to "to address U.S. concerns" about the CSDDD's reach over non-EU companies.
In short, the EU agreed to water down the climate law's emissions requirements and the rules focused on human rights abuses. The deal became law in February 2026. The climate plan requirement was deleted outright. The EU-wide right to sue was scrapped, leaving victims to each country's courts. The law now covers only companies with more than 5,000 employees and €1.5 billion in total sales, and not until July 2029.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/17ce6ce1-e860-4c08-9c74-275c4578b3c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The EU's position was that the deal reflected its own "simplification" agenda, first proposed in February 2025, before Turnberry. And that is true. The Competitiveness Roundtable had already laid the groundwork on both sides of the Atlantic. The trade deal turned a contested domestic proposal into a written commitment to Washington.
The payoff did not buy economic peace. In May 2026, Trump announced he would raise tariffs on European cars to 25%, accusing Brussels of moving too slowly. The EU completed ratification of the Turnberry deal on June 25. By then, the climate rules were already gone.
None of this proves the companies are in Antalya to lobby on any particular decision. They are doing what large companies do at every COP: meeting ministers, speaking on panels, selling technology.
Democrats sent a large delegation to COP31, led by California Gov. Gavin Newsom, that's trying hard to rehabilitate the United States' climate reputation, but they don't have a seat at the negotiating table.
The talks run until November 20. The central fight in the final-draft negotiations is over whether it will include language on "transitioning away" from fossil fuels or "phasing out" fossil fuels. But looming over the whole enterprise is September's warning from the UN Environment Program that global warming will now overshoot the Paris goal of 1.5°C within a few years, with even the best case scenario peaking at 1.7 to 1.8°C. "There are no good outcomes above 1.5 degrees C," the agency warned.
The country that has historically emitted more carbon than any other--the United States--has withdrawn its pledges and its negotiators. The companies whose coalition helped delete Europe's climate-plan requirement--call them the "Overshoot Lobby"--have registered dozens of staff at this year's talks, many as guests of the host. And the PR firm that coordinated that climate rollback has been hired to tell the world what the summit achieved and what work remains to be done.
Climatologist Michael Mann, professor of earth and environmental science at the University of Pennsylvania and author of "Science Under Siege," told Drop Site that laws "with teeth like the EU's CSDDD were moving in the right direction." But now we have "oil-soaked PR firms like Teneo running interference," he said.
"The fossil fuel lobby has filled the vacuum left behind by the U.S. government at COP31," Mann added. "Decarbonization is a NOW issue, not a transition issue, which is where the final draft is stuck."

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Whatever is next, I cannot do it alone
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
I am writing this morning to ask you to sign up to volunteer for whatever comes next for us.
Whether it's organizing to pass necessary legislation that creates a new world and a better country - one that prioritizes the dignity of all people, or whether it's a political campaign, I need you with me.
Adding your name doesn't mean I need you to go outside and knock on doors this afternoon - it just means that when meaningful opportunities to volunteer become available there's a good chance you’re willing to raise your hand.
[Use this link to say you're interested in volunteering and we'll be in touch shortly after the holidays for some initial conversations.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/volunteer_with_aoc/?source=em20261118-12508-P_ENG_VOL_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12508%2E2526796%2EBfT-MX)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/volunteer_with_aoc/?source=em20261118-12508-P_ENG_VOL_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12508%2E2526796%2EBfT-MX)**
Throughout the history of this country, the most important progress for working people has always come as a result of people standing up and organizing for change.
That is true of the civil rights movement, the women's rights movement, the labor rights movement and more.
And that is because the only way you beat a machine is with a movement.
The same is true in political campaigns.
I can tell you that from my experience, I've been outspent in races. I've had well over $20 million spent against me in my time in Congress. My first race, I had millions spent against me -- commercials running during Yankee games and all that.
But the one thing people kept seeing everyday was volunteers wearing our campaign shirts, walking around, helping people out, asking, “What matters to you?” And they saw nothing from the other side.
I think there's a weapon of cynicism to say, 'Protest doesn't work. Organizing doesn't work. Y'all are a bunch of hippies. You know, it doesn't do anything,' because, frankly, it's said out of fear, because it is a potent force for political change.
So for me, it's not just about raising money - it's about building a volunteer base that is willing to fight for change.
Because I cannot do that alone.
[Use this link to say you're interested in volunteering and we'll be in touch shortly after the holidays for some initial conversations.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/volunteer_with_aoc/?source=em20261118-12508-P_ENG_VOL_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=12508%2E2526796%2EBfT-MX)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/volunteer_with_aoc/?source=em20261118-12508-P_ENG_VOL_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=6&akid=12508%2E2526796%2EBfT-MX)**
In solidarity,
Alexandria

**[Donate](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261118-12508-P_ENG_VOL_MIS&t=1&akid=12508%2E2526796%2EBfT-MX)** | **[Merch](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/9251?utm_source=em-footer-20261118-12508-P_ENG_VOL_MIS&t=2&akid=12508%2E2526796%2EBfT-MX)**

subject: What people voted for

body:
People trusted our candidates to make a difference. Let’s have their backs as they get to work.
#
Voters sent a pretty clear message on Election Day, Peter.
They want to be able to afford their groceries, go to the doctor when they need to, and keep a roof over their heads without wondering how they’re going to cover everything else.
I think that’s pretty reasonable. Working hard ought to mean you can pay the bills, put a little money away, and give your kids a fair shot at a better life.
**Making that possible needs to be at the center of what Democrats do next.**
Small Town PAC helped elect people who understand those pressures. Now we need to have their backs as they prepare to deliver on the promises they made, and continue working to find the next generation of leaders ready to fight for their communities.
[**Will you chip in $5 or whatever works for you today to help Small Town PAC stand with the folks we just helped elect and support the next generation of Democrats who will put working families first?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261118-1.M0Ae-S&amount=5&refcode=em20261118-1358&t=1&akid=1358%2E34582%2EA-Zfa6)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261118-1.M0Ae-S&amount=5&refcode=20261118-1358&t=20&akid=1358%2E34582%2EA-Zfa6)**
People put their trust in our candidates because they believed those candidates would make their lives better. We have a responsibility to help them make good on that trust.
That means standing with them as they fight for affordable health care, good jobs, and a future where one unexpected expense doesn’t knock somebody off their feet.
When our new leaders take on powerful interests to deliver for their neighbors, I want them to know this team is still with them.
And there are more good people across this country who understand what their communities are up against and could make a real difference in office. We want to find them, encourage them to run, and give them a shot.
[**Can you pitch in $5 today to help us have the backs of our newly elected leaders and help the next generation follow in their footsteps?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261118-1.M0Ae-S&amount=5&refcode=em20261118-1358&t=21&akid=1358%2E34582%2EA-Zfa6)
Thanks for being part of this. I’m proud of what we’re building together.
Tim

name: Alia K.
subject: How we made history in Michigan
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1818?t=1001&akid=3916%2E251025%2Exr5OuP ]Abdul El-Sayed Senator-elect for Michigan [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1818?t=1002&akid=3916%2E251025%2Exr5OuP ]Abdul El-Sayed Senator-elect for
Michigan

Hey, it’s Alia, Abdul’s campaign manager.

We just shared a memo on how we won a toss-up Senate race without a dime
of corporate PAC money, and I’ve included it below. I’m really proud of
it, and you should be too,
Peter.

We couldn’t have defied the odds without you and other members of this
team on our side. Every door, every call, every $10 donation
made this possible. Thank you for being part of this.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261118-1-ak.SwDHfg&amount=10&refcode=em20261118-3916&t=1004&akid=3916%2E251025%2Exr5OuP ]Before you read on, will you chip in $10 or any amount so
that Abdul has an organized movement behind him when he gets to work in
January?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261118-1-ak.SwDHfg&amount=10&refcode=em20261118-3916&t=1023&akid=3916%2E251025%2Exr5OuP ]Donate $10 ››

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

The New Way to Win

Money out of politics. Money in your pockets. Medicare for All.

On April 17, 2025, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed launched his campaign with a
different theory of how Democrats could win. Over the next eighteen
months, he traveled to 125 cities across Michigan, held more than 750
public events, and built a grassroots army of more than 46,000 volunteers
– all while overcoming one of the most expensive and vicious opposition
campaigns in American political history.

The Many Beat The Money

A quarter billion dollars in outside money poured into Michigan's primary
and general elections from MAGA billionaires, AIPAC, Elon Musk, and
corporate interests determined to elect candidates who would defend the
status quo that had failed Michigan families. More money was spent trying
to defeat Abdul than any other Senate candidate in Michigan’s history.

The spending disparity was staggering:

* Not once in six months did Team Abdul outspend our opponents.
* In the primary, Abdul was outspent 11 to 1 by dark money groups and
special interests, which poured $70 million into the race.
* In the general election, Abdul was outspent by nearly $100 million, a
nearly 2-to-1 disparity

While Abdul’s opponents relied on billionaires, he relied on everyday
Michiganders. More than 633,000 individual donors made 1.3 million
contributions averaging just $44.17, with support coming from every single
Michigan county and every state in the country.

46,620 volunteer sign-ups built the largest volunteer base for any
Michigan midterm candidate in history.

Despite it all, Abdul won. Twice. The many beat the money.

Abdul Won Over Trump Voters, Back Young Voters And Young Men, And Made
Significant Gains In Rural Michigan And The Upper Peninsula

Abdul assembled a winning coalition that no one thought was possible.
Despite the consternation among the chattering class, Abdul outperformed
2024, 2020, and 2018 Democratic Senate margins across the board, including
a massive 15-point swing from Trump 2024 to Abdul in Wayne County. Abdul
won every precinct in Detroit, receiving nearly 92% of the votes in the
city. Rogers got just 5% and did even worse there than he did two years
ago, while Abdul improved on both Elissa Slotkin and Kamala Harris’s
performances in Detroit.

In 2024, the Democratic ticket performed poorly with Arab-American voters
in Dearborn. Abdul didn’t just make up those losses, but ran up the score.
Record-breaking turnout in Dearborn was nearly 5% above 2024 turnout.
While Harris lost the city by 6%, Abdul won by more than 65%. In Dearborn,
nearly 3,700 more voters voted in the Senate contest than in the race for
Governor. In Dearborn Heights, Abdul roughly doubled the vote share of the
2024 ticket. The Republicans made a targeted choice to use Islamophobia as
their core line of attack against Abdul, and it backfired tremendously
with one of the key constituencies that won Trump the presidency in 2024.

Abdul also made enormous gains in rural communities with Trump 2024
voters, especially across Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula. The
campaign aggressively showed up in places other Democrats don’t show up,
and talked about issues other Democrats don’t talk about—including his
plan to put Farmers Over Billionaires and earning the endorsement of the
Michigan Farmers Union.

In the counties where Abdul hosted rallies as part of his Shouldn’t Be
This Hard bus tour through the Upper Peninsula, the campaign saw strong
swings from Trump 2024 voters moving towards Democrats.

* Dickinson County—where Abdul held a rally in Iron Mountain—saw a +10
swing towards Abdul
* Delta County—where Abdul held a rally in Escanaba—went from Rogers +29
to Rogers +23
* He won Marquette County by nearly 20 points following an enormous
rally at Northern Michigan University. Kamala Harris won the county by
just 9% in 2024.

With Jewish voters, analysis shows that Abdul virtually matched Senator
Slotkin’s ‘24 totals.

Bet On Your Candidate: Let Abdul Be Abdul

The conventional wisdom was that a populist, anti-establishment Muslim
candidate couldn't win Michigan without sanding off his edges and
moderating his positions. We took the opposite approach: we bet on Abdul.

From interviews with conservative voices like Jesse Watters to hundreds of
town halls with unscreened questions, we put Abdul in front of everyone.
He took questions from the press wherever he went, embraced skeptical
audiences, never shied away from defending his beliefs. We trusted that
the more voters got to know him, the harder it would be for our opponents
to define him.

That philosophy extended to how we confronted an unprecedented barrage of
racist and bigoted attacks. To counter, we showed voters his deeply
American story: his Michigan upbringing, his grandparents Jan and Judy,
and the values that shaped him. From American flags to home-video footage
of his family, we embraced Americana to show voters who Abdul really was.

Abdul embodies what it means to be a...Millennial. Our digital team took
that and ran with it. Millennials are fans of Love Island, we grew up on
Blue's Clues, and we can sing most words to most Taylor Swift songs.
Abdul’s willingness to try a trend, lean into the right amount of cringe,
and just have fun created the perfect conditions to generate over 1
billion views on social media in the past 11 months.

Economic Populism As A Message That Resonates With The Majority

Our theory was simple: the divide that mattered wasn't Democrat versus
Republican, but working people versus the political establishment and
economic elites that had failed them.

We maintained a relentless focus on costs, corruption, and the economic
forces squeezing Michigan families. Our ads highlighted Abdul's UAW
support and drew a sharp contrast with Rogers on trade, while others spoke
to the hollowing out of the working class.

We didn't expand Abdul's appeal by moderating or softening his message. We
expanded it by connecting his populist principles to frustrations that
transcended party lines. Voters didn't have to agree with Abdul on every
issue to recognize that he was fighting for them.

Perhaps most importantly, we broadened our coalition without forgetting
where we came from. We launched our TV campaign with Chorus, an ad
featuring Bernie Sanders and the campaign's three core principles: money
out of politics, money in your pocket, and Medicare for All. Our closing
ad, Finale, kept the same core themes of Chorus with new additions of
Barack Obama and Jesse Watters. The message was deliberate: we could speak
to a broader coalition without abandoning the people, principles, or
politics that got us there in the first place.

For too long, Democrats have been afraid to embrace progressive ideas,
challenge corporate power, or engage voters outside their traditional
coalition. Abdul's campaign demonstrated a different approach: stay true
to your values, go everywhere, talk to everyone, and trust voters to
recognize whose side you're on.

Go Everywhere, Talk to Everyone

From day one of the campaign in April 2025 until Election Day, Abdul
didn’t shy away from a single interview. He talked to every single outlet,
doing sit-downs with not just Fox News, but The Daily Wire, and The
Dispatch. He went to every place Democrats aren’t willing to go and
answered questions no other Democratic candidate in the country would be
willing to answer.

Our team earned praise from the Michigan and national press corps for our
consistent media availability – at almost every public event, Abdul
gaggled with the press, taking questions from outlets ranging from The
National Review to Zeteo to NewsMax. He laid out his final closing
argument of the race in an op-ed exclusively in Fox News. He sat down with
Bari Weiss’ CBS after revelations that she was personally pushing false,
bad-faith right-wing conspiracy theories to influence the race.

Our campaign saw our biggest and most surprising victories in Michigan’s
rural counties, including the Upper Peninsula. Three rural counties saw
some of the biggest swings toward Democrats anywhere in the state,
including two of the counties Abdul visited with AOC in the UP during the
bus tour.

And every time he went into the lion’s den and went toe-to-toe with Fox
News’ biggest blowhards, the outcome was overwhelmingly positive. Even if
he got a question on tricky political terrain, the interview got historic
ratings. Donations surged, volunteer signups boomed, social media
engagement went sky-high. While calling out hypocrisy and bad-faith
questions, Abdul drove his core message in clips that reached every corner
of the Internet.

Lean Into the Tension, Unafraid To Take a Stand

Abdul never hid from his faith, even as the conservative echo chamber and
the President of the United States himself sought (and failed miserably)
to weaponize it against him. He never minced words about his views on
foreign wars, he shared his positions confidently and firmly on some of
the most contentious issues, and he never missed an opportunity to call
out hypocrisy or both political parties that have stymied change for too
long.

On digital, we proudly shined a bright light on it. It is no secret some
voters may feel uncomfortable or are simply uninformed about the Muslim or
Arab-American community. They said as much to Abdul on the campaign trail,
and we took the opportunity to showcase these important conversations
online and communicate openly about questions people may have.

BOTTOM LINE:

For years, Democrats have followed a playbook for winning elections.
Conventional, mainstream candidates pivot straight to the center after a
primary. Abdul won and won big because he was the exact same candidate on
the day he launched his campaign as he was 565 days later when he won.

He talked about big, bold solutions to get money out of politics, put
money in pockets, and pass Medicare for All. He did not cave to demands
from Washington and the establishment to become a cookie-cutter, status
quo Democrat who shied away from any environment that carried risk.

That kind of campaign would never have won the most expensive Democratic
primary in American history, and it would never have overcome hundreds of
millions in vicious, dog-whistle, fearmongering attack ads.

Abdul won because he was himself, because this campaign was unflinching in
leveraging his authenticity on every single platform and in every single
arena.

That is how the MANY beat the MONEY.

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Emails like this help us stay connected with grassroots supporters like you, so thank you for taking the time to read this message. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

Receive Fewer Emails: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=1024&akid=3916%2E251025%2Exr5OuP

Email us: info@abdulformichigan.com

Our team earned praise from the Michigan and national press corps for our consistent media availability – at almost every public event, Abdul gaggled with the press, taking questions from outlets ranging from The National Review to Zeteo to NewsMax. He laid out his final closing argument of the race in an op-ed exclusively in Fox News. He sat down with Bari Weiss’ CBS after revelations that she was personally pushing false, bad-faith right-wing conspiracy theories to influence the race. Our campaign saw our biggest and most surprising victories in Michigan’s rural counties, including the Upper Peninsula. Three rural counties saw some of the biggest swings toward Democrats anywhere in the state, including two of the counties Abdul visited with AOC in the UP during the bus tour. And every time he went into the lion’s den and went toe-to-toe with Fox News’ biggest blowhards, the outcome was overwhelmingly positive. Even if he got a question on tricky political terrain, the interview got historic ratings. Donations surged, volunteer signups boomed, social media engagement went sky-high. While calling out hypocrisy and bad-faith questions, Abdul drove his core message in clips that reached every corner of the Internet. Lean Into the Tension, Unafraid To Take a Stand Abdul never hid from his faith, even as the conservative echo chamber and the President of the United States himself sought (and failed miserably) to weaponize it against him. He never minced words about his views on foreign wars, he shared his positions confidently and firmly on some of the most contentious issues, and he never missed an opportunity to call out hypocrisy or both political parties that have stymied change for too long. On digital, we proudly shined a bright light on it. It is no secret some voters may feel uncomfortable or are simply uninformed about the Muslim or Arab-American community. They said as much to Abdul on the campaign trail, and we took the opportunity to showcase these important conversations online and communicate openly about questions people may have. BOTTOM LINE: For years, Democrats have followed a playbook for winning elections. Conventional, mainstream candidates pivot straight to the center after a primary. Abdul won and won big because he was the exact same candidate on the day he launched his campaign as he was 565 days later when he won. He talked about big, bold solutions to get money out of politics, put money in pockets, and pass Medicare for All. He did not cave to demands from Washington and the establishment to become a cookie-cutter, status quo Democrat who shied away from any environment that carried risk. That kind of campaign would never have won the most expensive Democratic primary in American history, and it would never have overcome hundreds of millions in vicious, dog-whistle, fearmongering attack ads. Abdul won because he was himself, because this campaign was unflinching in leveraging his authenticity on every single platform and in every single arena. That is how the MANY beat the MONEY.

Meet three
judges on the oligarchy’s bench.

They hold lifetime seats. They answer to no voter. And ruling after
ruling, they hand more power to corporations and billionaires, and take it
from the rest of us:

* Judge James C. Ho: The judge who attacked the campaign contribution
limits designed to prevent wealthy special interests from buying
elections.
* Chief Judge Reed O’Connor: The judge who wrote decision after decision
against the Affordable Care Act, and who repeatedly sided with efforts
to protect corporations from being held accountable for harming
people.
* Chief Judge Amos Mazzant: The judge who struck down the Biden
administration’s expanded overtime protections. He blocked a rule that
would have helped 4.2 million workers get the pay they deserve.

Three judges. Three examples of a much bigger problem.

Our courts were designed to protect the people from concentrated power.
But now they’re protecting concentrated power from the people.

This didn’t happen by accident. The oligarchy has spent
years pushing a calculated plan to take over our courts, installing crony
judges whose records made clear they’d serve the wealthy over the people.

Now those judges are delivering. When judges stop serving the law and
start serving the wealthy and well-connected, we pay the price.

Demand Justice PAC is naming these judges. We’re exposing their records
and making sure Americans know exactly who’s behind the rulings reshaping
their lives. We can’t do it without grassroots support.

## Turbulence Injures Five on JetBlue Flight
Five people aboard a JetBlue flight from Ponce, Puerto Rico, reported injuries early Tuesday after the plane [hit severe turbulence](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkD3SozAQRE8D2bgk8ScFBJuQfZtuSA1iZMYekEsSpnz7Le8VNu_q7vf-_Mw_yMLH_TfuNIYY5oOuLFQKpbng8aTkE-bNS8yUn_TJG9-32SjTg9ag7Yy-8JvmFut1HFqLaqlp1INrnXON7ept1N553w7r6jo05A06RaiMdS0FSwPVPH77tNZWq6437W1YVKMH0yln-0Z1vmoVrVxiuj0iH0E-8U0pSEy84s3HvZZxK-WVq-ZXZabKTNd13Y7F74w7fwOVmb5clZkkepTKTB34jfyTVggxAR-PMzFlwFAowYPKIidBEL5vBS4uG2R6UyIoZ1pOocMTCB5rBiwQRCBwIkiU_UmQ8fOdaqx1uusrM9VpXF8Xi3Duh6pV9x1Z_h0v_-n8PZq_AQAA__-uPpiZ) on its way to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. The plane [landed safely around 6:58 a.m.](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZB75BzAEDi4h20svRI1pg2d7bGSbQfv2J-YVNumgS6qvqv59zV8QKMTtL7zQ-uTniFchrBXzXCF-Y3YZyu4oFSzf-FP2sO2zEqrnUnI5zOBqeOPcQrNa0w4glgatNGM7jqMeuma3ZgXUeukFDKN2ruucNx5ku_S9cjDqJtjbT0o5SNH1qn2YRWhpVCfGodeic6wVuIaa8uOZQvT0k96YPaUcVni49GrI7rUehek_TE1MTdd1PSg5IClunanprsXU9HkyNd1ApiYp72OYmjp-YDoIecYj5cpDfJ45YOHgK2b-xLrQidxT2PbKMbp0xoq58IJvzMjrmZeTMDrkC_qUkRPENcSNQ-WebmaT7XpcgSiU3rBWbC8I9Ilff7n826r_AQAA__9Ysplz) and taxied to Terminal 3, where Broward Sheriff Fire Rescue crews were waiting. All five who were hurt declined rides to the hospital, and officials released no details on their injuries. Flight 1717 likely [flew through thunderstorms](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykULuOqzAU_BrojPzEULi4TbrcdktkzDF2YnBkH4Ly9ytW-wfbzUMazczXfbrbmOK-_rcbGJ_9tMNZEyBCmdDuTyiu2BpcyhXqEz41xDVMnPKeMEbYMFmH8Q2TtO1itBwsnVswTI9yHEcxqDYYD1oOo3TeC2fnfpZy1r3UbBTOKS-gjebKY4wNjKqey07PVDDNFR2HXlDlGklhiZhL98hx9-mT31B8yiUutnN5a5MJiK_aiH8NvzX8dp5n97Eh58tt-O0adclgMUAhv9QWjC7BBRWJ--MosBA8ynwk2B2QB-CcDiA-xTUgYVJpIaniXcAttcUsrzOmFGuvG0nXzcb0Uwb_-OPb8O8AAAD__0M7iGE) over the southern Bahamas, forecasters said. Tracking data shows the jet descended from 36,000 feet to 23,900 feet over the islands, but that alone doesn't show whether the descent was tied to the turbulence. [JetBlue confirmed the turbulence](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQhZ8Gd7YA_4ALijR0N21KawyDzV7WrACv5bePWCVPcJuRRnP06Zvz52v5Ah_8sf2GJyoX3XLglQOWgmkpcHxjMgnybkLMmL_xzrvf9oVTPrWMtUwuYIp_4zJAY5UYJNC1QcXEPMzz3Mux2ZWYZuMkBYv9INhaL4I5kD3i6szqGq8qjzEmGR0nPnRipT0TfKSznHo6GjJQtL7E1D2iP1y44xuTCzF5C52JzyaovZRXJv0vwjXh-rqu7sxQooW7BgjXucR0E67rf58VChKu_1EI19WBcM1YHYJw_cCyhhNbF_y2l7acaT0DHgZbfzzO5DG3LqbSBjgtJguhRv_TZi75OLKJ0opqkrKvy4fg8yTIQLcn-PAxLz8s_a343wAAAP__UqGV3g) and said medical staff checked both customers and crew members after landing. Officials reported no structural damage to the plane.
## East Coast Braces for More Rain

Maine Gov.-elect Hannah Pingree and the Democratic legislative majority will greet a $1.3 billion deficit when they ring in the 133rd Legislature this year -- which means Maine is marching inexorably toward its next round of tax increases.
The massive deficit figure comes from the state's own Bureau of the Budget. Its [Four-Year Revenue and Expenditure Forecast](https://substack.com/redirect/10af237a-4fca-41b0-b60f-b9bf8ac2101a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), revised Oct. 6, projects $12.2 billion in General Fund revenue for fiscal years 2028 and 2029. Current law requires $13.3 billion in spending. These are the kinds of math problems state lawmakers struggle with. Add the $256.7 million hole in the Highway Fund and you get $1.35 billion.
Of course, that number is based on forecasts. It could shrink or it could grow. But the Maine Constitution requires a balanced budget (or, at least, the pretense of one), and we all know the Democratic majority isn't interested in _cutting_ spending.
So the only question is: How are Democrats going to increase taxes?
Pingree has offered a few clues about the kinds of tax increases she would support, i.e., all of them. She's backed the 2% "millionaire" tax and says she wants to increase it. However, as we've previously reported, high-net-worth individuals generally avoid Maine or have already left, so covering the deficit with only the "millionaire" tax increasing would require it to increase to 17.5% or more.
So Pingree has also [said](https://substack.com/redirect/a1a21ac2-b5ba-4876-becc-22a3c3b3def6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) she wants to "export some of our tax burden" -- by which she means making non-Maine residents pay a share of tax increases. She has said she wants towns to tax out-of-state second-home owners at higher rates, but such a change would require a constitutional amendment and a two-thirds vote Democrats do not have in the House. However, she could still "export" some of the tax burden to tourists by jacking up Maine's sales tax and the meals and lodging taxes.
What follows are five ways the 133rd Legislature could raise the money. Each is priced with the state's own fiscal notes and sized to close the $1.096 billion General Fund gap. We use fiscal notes from previous attempts to raise or lower taxes to estimate the revenue impact. Similar to how the state legislature analyzes tax policy, all of this assumes that no one changes their behavior (e.g., leaves Maine, shops in New Hampshire, etc.) to avoid the higher taxes.

### Scenario 1: A broad income tax increase
Maine Revenue Services priced the entire individual income tax when Republicans proposed abolishing it. According to the fiscal note for [LD 671](https://substack.com/redirect/9fa3e0cc-e74f-42fe-9f63-a77a1076df73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the state income tax was projected to collect $5.6 billion for the General Fund in FY2028-2029.
Closing the gap with the income tax alone means raising every bracket by about 20%. The top rate would go from 7.15% to 8.55%.
That would put the top rate above the roughly 8.5% Maine charged before the cuts that began in 2013. Every income tax filer's bill before credits would rise by about a fifth. A single filer with $60,000 of Maine taxable income would pay roughly $745 more a year at 2025 brackets.
Democrats have traditionally claimed that they don't favor broad-based income taxes that also apply to the lower and middle classes.
## Scenario 2: A bigger millionaire's tax
To close the gap with the millionaire's tax alone, the surcharge would have to rise from 2% to about 17.5%. Maine's top marginal rate would be roughly 24.6%.
For comparison, California's top rate is [13.3%](https://substack.com/redirect/f3bd7455-935c-4e57-ba47-4081692c3014?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the highest in the country.
The current surcharge applies to income above $1 million for single filers and $1.5 million for joint filers and heads of household. The Office of Fiscal and Program Review and the Department of Administrative and Financial Services estimate it will raise [$96 million in fiscal 2027 and $150 million in fiscal 2028-29](https://substack.com/redirect/7910b178-bc48-487b-b50e-11813161c590?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
When the original LD 1089 proposed 4% on all income over $1 million, regardless of filing status, Maine Revenue Services estimated it would raise about [$200 million a year](https://substack.com/redirect/82916753-147e-49f5-ba67-6fff88baa041?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). At that base, a surcharge of about 13% closes the gap.
Rep. Cheryl Golek, D-Harpswell, introduced LD 1089 at 4%. Lawmakers cut it to 2%, raised the joint-filer threshold and folded it into the supplemental budget, LD 2212. Mills signed it [April 9](https://substack.com/redirect/5e6290a3-f84d-4c70-9b69-7e00798b6ceb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), retroactive to Jan. 1. Pingree supports it and wants to build on it.
(As a reminder, the idea that Maine could generate $1 billion in revenue after increasing the top marginal tax rate to 24.6% rests on the assumption that no "millionaire" is allowed to leave Maine... ever.)
### Scenario 3: A broad sales tax increase
Perhaps the most likely way to close the budget gap is through an increase in the sales tax. Yes, Maine is in the middle of a generational cost-of-living crisis and Democrats campaigned on reducing the cost of living, so jacking up the sales tax to pay for welfare fraud and teachers unions would be a counterintuitive way of keeping that promise. But the governor leaving the Blaine House campaigned on not changing Maine's abortion law and not raising taxes, so we're clearly in an era when campaign promises mean very little to politicians (or voters, for that matter).
Raising every sales tax rate by about 1.45 points would close the gap. The general rate would go from 5.5% to about 6.95%, meals from 8% to 9.45% and lodging from 9% to 10.45%. Closing it with meals and lodging alone would take rates of nearly 15% and 16%.
On the meals and lodging rate, Maine's hospitality industry will squawk and the lobbyists will get to lobbying. So in the event lawmakers raise only the 5.5% rate and leave meals and lodging alone, it takes more: about 7.36%. Either way, Maine would sit at or near the top of New England. Rhode Island's 7% is the region's highest. New Hampshire charges nothing, which could be problematic for revenue forecasts.
Based on fiscal notes for bills proposing to cut the sales tax from the last session, we can estimate $755 million per point over the biennium.
Another indicator that the sales tax is the likely route for Democrats is that they have done this before. In 2013 the Democratic Legislature raised the general rate from 5% to 5.5% and meals and lodging from 7% to 8% over Republican Gov. Paul LePage's veto. The increase was supposed to be temporary (hahaha). The 5.5% rate never came down.
One problem with a general sales tax increase: it hits low- and middle-income families hard. However, Democrats will likely consider two items that offset any concern on that front: 1) Sales taxes are not charged on EBT cards, and 2) Sales taxes can be described as exporting the burden to tourists and summer residents.
## Scenario 4: Creative tax increases and exemption eliminations
Whatever Democrats do to come up with $1 billion to take from taxpayers is going to sting, so they will likely get creative in trying to spread around the pain as much as possible. One strategy they've used in the past is to increase lots of tiny taxes and fees and to remove exemptions.
A mix of increases to the income tax, the "millionaire" surcharge, the sales tax, and the meals and lodging taxes could be complemented with an elimination of some exemptions.
In classic government fashion, the state considers any private property Mainers are allowed to keep as a "tax expenditure," as if the collective is forgoing money by letting the productive class keep it. Maine Revenue Services' [Tax Expenditure Report](https://substack.com/redirect/14e5e733-385e-4aeb-b93f-33f52bf97c3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) prices each one of the "tax expenditures," and they all could be on the chopping block once the legislature is in session.
Expanding the sales tax to cover grocery staples would raise $185 million per year. Eliminating the exemption on continuous rentals would bring in $165 million. Taxing prescription drugs would bring in $130.9 million, while ending the exemption for residential electricity would put another $46 million on the table. Collecting sales taxes on home heating oil and other hydrocarbon-based heating options could bring in $43.7 million.
Democrats have done this in the very recent past, which could mean they're likely to take this approach again. Mills closed the last budget gap (which also, funny enough, was caused by Medicaid welfare) by increasing flat-rate taxes on goods such as cigarettes, cannabis and streaming services. The adult-use weed tax went from 10% to 14% on Jan. 1. The same day, streaming subscriptions came under the 5.5% sales tax and the old Service Provider Tax was folded into the sales tax, according to the [state controller](https://substack.com/redirect/4be22b2d-d9a2-4228-aee8-05b67d8b7a4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). On the other hand, having taken this route recently could mean they've squeezed all the levers they're interested in squeezing.
The likeliest outcome is a package of tax expansions and tax increases Democrats have already supported in recent years. That would look like increasing the "millionaire" surcharge to 4% for all filers, applying a surtax on capital gains in excess of $250,000, raising the corporate rate on income, reducing the estate tax exemption, and then some broad tax increases to cover what is left. Some exemptions with constituencies who can't hire lobbyists will likely hit the cutting room floor. Fees for all kinds of licenses will go up.
### What about the Gas Tax?
All of the foregoing scenarios only covered the General Fund deficit. But the overall gap facing lawmakers will be $250 million to $300 million higher because of the Highway Fund shortfall -- a fund that is replenished with gas taxes. Closing the $256.7 million Highway Fund gap with the gas tax alone would take about 17.5 cents a gallon on top of today's 30 cents. That is a 58% increase. Yes, yes, I know: Democrats bellyached about high gas prices and Iran during the campaign. But we've already established that campaign promises really don't matter much when it comes to funding the welfare industrial complex and making sure the political class gets paid.
### Another little problem...
All of the foregoing scenarios rest on the Democrat approach to accomplishing tax increases. When Democrats propose tax increases, they do so in a static, rather than a dynamic, model. It's a lot like Bill Cosby's approach to romance: you assume your prey can't flee. Such models don't anticipate changes in taxpayer behavior resulting from tax increases.
Behavioral changes invariably reduce the forecasted revenue from tax increases, as no one changes their behavior to pay _more_ taxes. For example, if Maine raises the taxes on millionaires, you could have more millionaires pull the six-months-and-a-day trick in Florida, Tennessee, Texas, or another zero-income-tax state. If taxes go up on meals and lodging, you could see less tourism and less domestic eating out. The contrary is also true in many cases: reducing taxes can unleash economic growth and increase government revenue. (JFK was the last Democrat who understood this, and we all know how that went.)
What this means for Democratic lawmakers is that all of the modeled rate increases in this post are likely too low to generate the revenue sufficient to balance the budget -- in real terms, as opposed to Augusta terms. They might pass constitutional muster by getting a solid Democrat-style forecast, but in reality the state will be right back in the same position 2-4 years from now, with revenues falling short of forecasts.

One strategy they've used in the past is to increase lots of tiny taxes and fees and to remove exemptions. A mix of increases to the income tax, the "millionaire" surcharge, the sales tax, and the meals and lodging taxes could be complemented with an elimination of some exemptions. In classic government fashion, the state considers any private property Mainers are allowed to keep as a "tax expenditure," as if the collective is forgoing money by letting the productive class keep it. Maine Revenue Services' prices each one of the "tax expenditures," and they all could be on the chopping block once the legislature is in session. Expanding the sales tax to cover grocery staples would raise $185 million per year. Eliminating the exemption on continuous rentals would bring in $165 million. Taxing prescription drugs would bring in $130.9 million, while ending the exemption for residential electricity would put another $46 million on the table. Collecting sales taxes on home heating oil and other hydrocarbon-based heating options could bring in $43.7 million. Democrats have done this in the very recent past, which could mean they're likely to take this approach again. Mills closed the last budget gap (which also, funny enough, was caused by Medicaid welfare) by increasing flat-rate taxes on goods such as cigarettes, cannabis and streaming services. The adult-use weed tax went from 10% to 14% on Jan. 1. The same day, streaming subscriptions came under the 5.5% sales tax and the old Service Provider Tax was folded into the sales tax, according to the . On the other hand, having taken this route recently could mean they've squeezed all the levers they're interested in squeezing. The likeliest outcome is a package of tax expansions and tax increases Democrats have already supported in recent years. That would look like increasing the "millionaire" surcharge to 4% for all filers, applying a surtax on capital gains in excess of $250,000, raising the corporate rate on income, reducing the estate tax exemption, and then some broad tax increases to cover what is left. Some exemptions with constituencies who can't hire lobbyists will likely hit the cutting room floor. Fees for all kinds of licenses will go up. What about the Gas Tax? All of the foregoing scenarios only covered the General Fund deficit. But the overall gap facing lawmakers will be $250 million to $300 million higher because of the Highway Fund shortfall -- a fund that is replenished with gas taxes. Closing the $256.7 million Highway Fund gap with the gas tax alone would take about 17.5 cents a gallon on top of today's 30 cents. That is a 58% increase. Yes, yes, I know: Democrats bellyached about high gas prices and Iran during the campaign. But we've already established that campaign promises really don't matter much when it comes to funding the welfare industrial complex and making sure the political class gets paid. Another little problem... All of the foregoing scenarios rest on the Democrat approach to accomplishing tax increases. When Democrats propose tax increases, they do so in a static, rather than a dynamic, model. It's a lot like Bill Cosby's approach to romance: you assume your prey can't flee. Such models don't anticipate changes in taxpayer behavior resulting from tax increases. Behavioral changes invariably reduce the forecasted revenue from tax increases, as no one changes their behavior to pay more taxes. For example, if Maine raises the taxes on millionaires, you could have more millionaires pull the six-months-and-a-day trick in Florida, Tennessee, Texas, or another zero-income-tax state. If taxes go up on meals and lodging, you could see less tourism and less domestic eating out. The contrary is also true in many cases: reducing taxes can unleash economic growth and increase government revenue. (JFK was the last Democrat who understood this, and we all know how that went.) What this means for Democratic lawmakers is that all of the modeled rate increases in this post are likely too low to generate the revenue sufficient to balance the budget -- in real terms, as opposed to Augusta terms. They might pass constitutional muster by getting a solid Democrat-style forecast, but in reality the state will be right back in the same position 2-4 years from now, with revenues falling short of forecasts. The U.S. has no significant commercial source of natural rubber, and synthetic versions can’t match it in demanding uses like aircraft and heavy truck tires, said center director and NC State professor Gregory McKenna. ## Home Depot Names New CEO
Atlanta-based Home Depot on Tuesday [named](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O5CAQhJ_GzrBoPP6ZgOASZ3PphRZ2NzY6DAhaw-7brzyvsFmpVCrVV_9e68s478Lx11yk-bBroFo8MVO-5RkvQkqRd4pI3r0pOyqrkmoUAALmNeVYEu28Qou6l0jwmFvSMD0HKaV6QntqkJMc52nat20YDCDaGZ-wzbDhDNCPrdN3IwDMAAA9dBtuNACZ3faDtDA0D0noOOaOTzoo5sMZ67_jm3K3x6v1-mROpen_NGpp1FJr7Wz8Ggx7E9jcmUYtN1ujlhtKfKhEMBcVEaiKnaKw0ftYXTgEEwqk_T9lUZhSuj2MNbRZY6rOe1fGqXnI4zLOfxbwb997a_UTAAD__7qSh8c) chief financial officer Richard McPhail as its next CEO as Ted Decker steps aside following a medical leave. Decker will [remain chairman](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpSAQRp8GO24Y0Ou1oNjG7t92S4PwoSQoBohk337jfYVtJieZ5GTO_PlZfkyI4dx-mwO6bn450UpErcgP7umAw5WqRXKI4UYOKIsU8s2JOH2WK6dywdaFOqeVcKD-00HTOA1CCDlRt2u_vgdj0JMa3qpfyUNNRnkzKetpHU0X9GMkog8RkaLX6lYMBGO9GoSngfUCLtSUX3XHhpS3YHz8m27kl01HF_Ve61WY-sXkzOTcWnu1muyzZHJ-7EzORM8YmZyfLv4N4xaJl4qrcJfayY2vyPyAC9ZEHmFu8BPtIYdc-GkOOCbnLmt3tRBjKO-R9WI7TIjfW-r__vHW8l8AAAD__9geiLo) of the board. Ann-Marie Campbell, a 41-year company veteran, will become president and chief operating officer, and Jordan Broggi will become CFO when the changes take effect next week. The company [reported](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0c-K2zAQBvCnkW8KGjl24oMPXVp1y5JAaeluT0Z_xo5A1ghJjcnbF-cV9jYwzPD9-N4v00X74ONy1SuOdZmniFsJWCvmfbzRig4TVYvkMPg7Zo9lkkL2HIDDeUqZSkJbJ2jc2AqHcDw3OMJp6IQQcoDmNsqh7cXQH7XpZ3duu14MaHujhTg5o41p_Lh_BIAzAEALB-MMdoDazm0nZujYUaDzlfKh3nBByovXc3jQHfPB0tqE8VZrKqz9wqRiUm3bdtiKqfd9y6TaVUyqQFYHJpUlY7ilf7E-mFQ7kj-V3CLxUjEV7miL3NKadHzwjIlyLbzUTHHhqHP0cSlccuND8BR50QEL99Fm1AWZVC9_f721p58_vr28Xr9e37r3y8f3P-r14_eesMmjS9t-WvoTO4pl1T48IfWzJdxH-T8AAP__PlGfQA) third-quarter sales of $43.4 billion, up about $2 billion, or nearly 5%, from the same period last year. [McPhail](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAURE8DnZG_gWUpXKSh27QpkbHH8CWDLeOwye2jTZELpJtiNJr3Ph7zw3DgY303O3RZ_XzgeQaUgvyKW9zhkGKxiA6BL2TGOSupboJI0H1OOZ4JtsxUO91KB-ruNTQNYy-lVCPVm1ajl62HXWhxQz-oVhKG9tZDDrIbR1ezfi0S0Z2IqKVmcQt6grG-7aWnvuokHJeYm7JhRcwrGx--44Xc2LjXQW-lpLNq3yo1VWqyMaeYTUHzR_DqVWpaOFZqymw3k53YbdoMB4Ev2M_CF8TFFiJlnOxwFGE3hheeD3NYNkFE79ki11m79OQQ-LwNVSfX3XD4fVL-a_HS6icAAP__NQGLEw), who joined the company in 2005, said results exceeded the company's expectations. Decker, who [joined the company in 2000](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnDAURJ8GOiNf87NQuEhDt2lTIuM7hquYNTIOm7x9tCnyAl83xWhG5_x4Lk8nUV7bd3fAli0sL7yviFKQP3FPBxhnKh6JEeVGFlyL0WZQRIrG5czpOuHLQjXbVjOoG2tYeky91tpMVO-We91OgTqn-_BouaU18LByt3KYWA9jLfazSEQjEVFLzcoreoLzoe11oL7qNFhKyk3ZsSHlTVyIf9KN3Ph01NHupZxX1X6rzFyZ2ad8puwKmv8En15l5lVSZeYCVgz_E1n53UlWZ8YljFdRfhcEhd_wv4rcUCkE8ch1tny-JUa5hkfV6e1wEv99l696u635GwAA__9IaoZO) as director of business valuation, drew praise for his tenure as chief executive since 2022 and his prior leadership roles.
## Psychiatric Hospital Breaks Ground
Georgia [broke ground](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOiOvgQMKF2noLm1KtLYXsM5gZO8dub-PiPIH6aaYGc28r_t0Rx_8vnziRpqXedrpzIGYKV1yjRs5OiJbio6Cf1HylCcl1U0ACOinI8V8kOUJSqdr6QiaviQN3dBKKdUA5aqtwaGrjeo7Gm6dQWt7sGbuHap-BmVLr69GAOgBAGqojDPUAqGd61bO0BaNJOc5popXWiimxeMc3vFFqbJxK4NemY9c1B-FGgs1nudZzfG7RQ64M16eQo3Xt0KNf3lhEuEjiyXF5-5EI4dNHPltV4-cvBVrzIdnDMLRA4MRNj53fpdJu-P0Ifh864pGLhv68LuB_8vvpdVPAAAA___S14lo) on a $409 million, 300-bed forensic psychiatric hospital in DeKalb County, the state's first new psychiatric hospital in decades. The hospital will serve [people in the criminal justice system](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1u7CAQhZ8Gd1gM_lm7oLiNu71tSgvD2B4FGwRk0b59RJQ3SDP6pDn6dHQ-nutTk6P7-K8vVPnY1xtLcpgzxoqnv9Bi8Nmgt-johZEwrVLIkQNwmNYQfQpo8gqNVZ2wCP3UoILHPAgh5AzNqYR-mLmbZj3ofoN9NEJu876NfWfGUQrRkKpGAJgAADpoN7vhAKjN3g1ih4H1Ai1lH9t84oE-HqR39_YvjK3xV-PUmXNIrPvH5MLkUkppS7SlPplcqp3JBaCeSr8KvkXUn4kf0X_dlvdi5hc5R_7mIb3NSTpHMvz0KVDWjsmlicqGUjNpfLBeHJcm91Mh_3W-l5LfAQAA__9ICYTI) who need court-ordered competency evaluations or treatment. Kevin Tanner, commissioner of the state Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities, said more than 850 people are waiting for forensic services, many of them in county jails. Officials [expect construction](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uxCAQhJ8Gd5xY_INdUKRxd2lTWhjW9koYEJA73dtHTiLlAdKsVppPM6P5uC93Q57C_m5O1HXfloDP4rFWzNd7xBMdplgtRoeeHpgJyyKFHDgAh3FJOZaEti7QON0Kh9CNDWpQUy-EkBM0h1bSrNYNCuzWSiNanCboJtUpVNu4wtCQvhwBYAQAaOG2uhV7QGO3thcb9KwT6KjGfKsH7hjzTmbzr_jAfLPxbLw-ak2FtW9MzkzOv0hGG7P7YZicrxAmZ4DrqD-Mr7hTKNzGUGr-tJVi4DHwgE--xYyhkOWpvOxBpmay_IglUTX-UnnKVGLAXJicm6xdepL3VAbFOrGfhvx3w_rfdR9afgUAAP__V4KR-Q) to take about three years.
## Drone Deliveries Take Off
Amazon's Prime Air drones made their [first metro Atlanta deliveries](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdEZeGzBXuEhDd2lTIp-9gCXDIrMCXb4-IsofpBmNNNIbzXw9x6dPOW3zp1_R8TyNG15HRmYst11oxYg7cUCKmNOJJeExaqU7CSChH_dCx46BR6iiMyoiNH2FDuyjVUrpB1SLC2Aaa0LXt5OypnnYDq3u-8ZEFU0LukruJgJADwBgoH7FF7aAPkymVRO0olEYE1OpecEZqczJT_lNJ5Y60FpltzDvhzAfQg9CD9d11RdTuEOhh5su9ABwixV68Kv_pk3GQhvKv2Fv-cI5bYdckQtJz9lv7IUequLifqWc09FZ0ah59Sn_1vJ_Lzud_gkAAP__WMZ_ww) this past weekend from a Gwinnett County facility. The drones deliver items weighing less than 5 pounds in under an hour and [fly within a 7.5-mile radius](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2KxSAUhJ_GdAaP5scUFtuku9tuGbx6kggagzlcufv0S5Z9g22GgYFvmPl6LA8bYji2T5vQ0LYuB9YrIhGW2-45occzk8PsMYYXloDXIoUcOAAHvZwlXyc6WqDxRgmP0OkGDYxTL4SQEzS7ARzAqbHrJqv0EzQOTnovp2FSWqMemmBuIgBoAAAF7dM_sQe0blW9WKFnnUAfKJeWdtwwly3YNb7zC0vrcmqi2YnOi6kPJmcm51prW4uvd8jkfNOZnIW-ZWRytsl-54P7kg_kf8Pe3OUUjo0npJK5pWgPskzOTTH-rCHGcA0j68SWbIi_tfTfy15G_gQAAP__BpSAcQ) of the site, but not in heavy rain or strong winds. Metro Atlanta is among the areas in Amazon's [plan](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu7CAQRb_G7lgxYLApKF6z3b42pTXA2EbCBmG0m83XR47yB-nOaKSre-7HY35gTPFY_-NOtq3LfNDrTNQa1Qu3vFOgkpunHCjFJ9VI5yy40AyAwTSXms9Cvs3QByt5IBimniyMRnHOhYF-s0JrclPgwZtBLEJpkEhSeG8IxgCij_ZKBIAJAEDCzQVHCgj9IhVfQHUDpxBbrre20Uq5rhGX9M5Pqjef9z7ZrbVydvJfJ-6duGO5PK7XddQWfaKLdvzKBws1H8R-fd6MPgseZ8wHe2HasTYmeHDSGIda0eS81Dhqp4ZxMYY7gKmvNpRXTCmeeuwGvu4Y00-R9tcRn1Z8BwAA__9xW4ds) to expand drone delivery to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by year's end. The company has said the Georgia operation will create about 30 jobs.
| Flying together with our sponsor [](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0M1KxDAUxfGnaXdTcpN-LrIQtCtHwYXiqrTJaXsxbUoSZtCnl_oK7g4c-C3-H9fhOrLjfXkZN-i0zMOOe3RICeGcq99gcfhk4C0c3xAYcZBC1heiC7XDEXw8YNJAudVKWFDZ5tDUdJUQQnaUr7qtq6muqWvahkoSUlSTasnIGsYAnchZnyIRtUREiorJTqgIo5lVJWaqslLAcvKhSCsW-LDwOLtvf0MojN9yp9eUjpiph0z2meznAPzABoadAscvpMLvjnect-oD5kw99s-fr-9Pb3nQ9rizcxzrJivFso3s_tT03yI3LX8DAAD__74qdb0) **The Brisket That Kept Them Going for 21 Days After Hurricane Helene (Most Families Have Never Heard of It)** When rescuers finally reached Mary's North Carolina home, part of the roof had caved in, and the roads were washed out. Her husband David, 66, was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer. Yet Mary, 63, was standing, and David was alive.
"How did you...?" the lead rescuer asked.
Mary pointed to [a stack of blue packages](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0M1KxDAUxfGnaXdTcpN-LrIQtCtHwYXiqrTJaXsxbUoSZtCnl_oK7g4c-C3-H9fhOrLjfXkZN-i0zMOOe3RICeGcq99gcfhk4C0c3xAYcZBC1heiC7XDEXw8YNJAudVKWFDZ5tDUdJUQQnaUr7qtq6muqWvahkoSUlSTasnIGsYAnchZnyIRtUREiorJTqgIo5lVJWaqslLAcvKhSCsW-LDwOLtvf0MojN9yp9eUjpiph0z2meznAPzABoadAscvpMLvjnect-oD5kw99s-fr-9Pb3nQ9rizcxzrJivFso3s_tT03yI3LX8DAAD__74qdb0) in the corner.
Six months earlier, her friends had laughed at the boxes in her pantry. "Planning for the apocalypse, Mary?" But on day four, with no power and no running water, she boiled rainwater on a camping stove and opened the first package of freeze-dried smoked brisket. David took one bite and whispered, "That's... that's actually good."
Most people assume emergency food means chalky MREs and protein bars. It doesn't. ## Virginia Bids for U.S. Space Academy
Virginia has formally [asked NASA to build](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0bHupCAQBvCnwY4NA6xiYXGN3V57pRlhWEkQDHKSffuLm3uDfzeZfPmSX74_r-WFIYb0_o07TfXyS6J2RqqVynIeaAktOto_a3AtpErliLktUsieA3AwC9oaLlo0dm7yqAnHjiYYxqcQQmnRbZMiHI1URiplcMTVGe16s67eDuOKOHRhuvsAwACABPPohe7JPMEPWgnfI9OCXKi5POpGVyjvkAL6-MkXlYfNexenrdbjZOoXkzOTc2vtAeqmpNzuBJMzlhpsJCbnSnZjcj5toGTvB1LJXyyT89-Tf0_-H86Pko98YuQJT-QR0zvSh_tcKt9zKpn4hvtRc-IXMjnLEbhVSjnwnuPgBq61FnwE1XMEowCFeSo_dGVyRwsxhrMfmBbvHUP8YuoPd7gm-S8AAP__uYyciQ) the new United States Space Academy in Hampton, pitching a 600-acre campus anchored by NASA’s Langley Research Center and historic Fort Monroe. Gov. Abigail Spanberger [announced the bid Monday](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2uozAQBeCnMZ2RbYyBwsU2dHfbLdGAx2Ek8yM8wcrbrxLlDW45GunofOffz_QDlGh__IUNPd9x2rHkhMx4TfmEBWGBgNtrplBoZ7zOdJTJKOOk1lL3EyxMN04WquAjWIShQq-7oVVKNVZVq4-9M9gaHZzt7NCgiq2OwWjoZnAqDBX5d57WutdaG93XTlmHfatjZxsVHQirMBAfV80r3nQ9aCeI6XXceNXLsVXJr8xnFs0fYUZhxlJKXeB-vZ_CjG-TMGM6FkjyeyzHMwXJK8rnToxBZgbGLD9o-VXLGSVmhjlRXjFI2uUK28nHLsxYXT6chVKi7Dph1WMDSp86_Mslb2_-BwAA___zX4qO). Under the plan, Langley would supply the research, engineering, and flight core while Fort Monroe would handle housing, instruction, and ceremonies, with a satellite site at the [_Wallops Flight Facility_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykz7GOhCAQgOGn0W4Ng4huQXHNdnvtlWYWBp0ExQCB7Ntf9l7hyr_5kv_nuT6RA5_bNx5kSvXrSS0HKoXSmi-0hBYdHe8Xu8ZnoXSF2FYppL4B3GBZ0RautCrsnfGoCO89GZjvkxBiVKLfjQbyOFuYvPZ2nAm0A4V-El5PCvHVs_l4ALAAgIRl0EJpWibwsxqF19gpQY5LTEPZqXLa-GT04R0rpcHGow9mL-XK3fjVyUcnH6214cSMwxbrJzGEeOVOPvpk3NU4BM567pTYDuTwR5R_3lcjfwMAAP__QfhvPg) on the Eastern Shore. The academy would welcome an inaugural class of about 300 cadets by 2028 and feed graduates into NASA, the Space Force, and the commercial space industry. Virginia’s entire congressional delegation signed on in support. President Trump [_signed an executive order_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DmO4zAQheHTUBkFFkVrCRhMosyTTijUkCW5AGoBWZbat2_Y6Bv0BR7e__27T3fkxNvyF1fycs7TRldJJEJ5KgcGwoCR1td_jhdvQvlI-zVZY1sNoKGfMAifNDmsop_REQ4VeeiGmzGmcaZ6eEfQ9DC0bWccDkOgoacQLcwhQNOhqdi_9wCgBwALfd0a11J_g7lzjZlbVM5QZNlzLQ86OS-8Mc7ptZ-U67CvVfIPkaOo5o-yo7LjdV31hgXrZT-VHd9NOlMiLKTseGQqHGkTLfm5HrrwshVNXxSe7xa950hZy65DJhTSz6I_FPrHQtmxyj4eF6fEpe2UM8uKnD5X5JeKp7ffAQAA__8ziYm9) to create the tuition-free academy in August, and NASA asked interested states for proposals in September, with a deadline of this past Monday. Virginia is competing with bids from West Virginia, Nevada, and others.
## NoVa Plow Plan: Interstates First, Neighborhoods Last
VDOT’s Northern Virginia district will plow interstates and major roads to bare pavement this winter before it clears most neighborhood streets, and [won’t treat residential roads](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE9jMiPbePgJHGxC9jbdEPXYDbRkMLJbWHP7FXOFl1RUqk_1_ftZfoAindtfONDxvS4n1hKRGfNSLvAIHgIenzeFSidjvmKqi1Gml1pLPS7gmW5cLDTBrWARpgadHqaXUqqzqtkdhN6gtybYbnr59zTB2OGESo8B1BhUQ-7Z01qPWmujx7ZXtsfxpdfBdmrtQViFgTjllne8KW90Eqzxk27MrU9HE93OfBXR_RFmFmautbZX4nSAj8lDfErCzA9GmFnrJwZh5u-jwsBY5Eq5sDyRtv2d8p5SKDJCYXmHxLKcqcorwinM3GQXrkoxUukHYdV2AH0RDf9S4e3M_wAAAP__qtOG1w) until 2 inches of snow or sleet have fallen. Todd Robson, who runs maintenance for VDOT’s Northern Virginia district, told officials at a Nov. 10 briefing that crews follow a staggered priority system across 649 mapped zones. Interstates like I-66 come first, then primary and busy secondary roads, with cul-de-sacs last. On priority roads, the goal is bare pavement edge to edge, mostly with rock salt. In neighborhoods, it’s one shared lane so emergency vehicles and residents can get in and out. VDOT asked residents to park in driveways or garages, or coordinate with neighbors to park on one side of the street, so smaller plow trucks can get through. ## Virginia Leads Nation in Data Center Energy
Virginia’s data centers [_burn through more electricity_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAURp8GO04AET0FxTR2d9opzb6w1Z3Bn8A-Et9-4rzCrb9kZa3vz9f0BZRoX37Dhp6vedqxloTMmKdyQkAIEHG7vylW2hnzmY46GWWc1FrqYYLAdOFkoYl-BovwbtDr_t0ppVqrmtWbDhX2-I2uCzA7a3vVBmxhMKp3b6sb8g9Paz1orY0eXk5Zh0On5962anYgrMJIfOQXr3hRXmgnmNN9XJhf4dia5Ffms4j2lzCjMGOt9VUzhWcUZnyahBkZ_tK-yMf42IUZV8gX5CgLf-ItIzDIgE-jxISBMwW-5aegxI1KoWN_IE328ayUEhXXC6uWDSj9l-Af_nd58y8AAP__zVSHUA) than those of any other state, a new Harvard study found, drawing about a quarter of all the power used by the nation’s 403 largest facilities. The study, [_published Monday_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAYRZ9GOwwwjKMFxTbT_dtuaT7hOn4JggFG49tv3FfY-iYn95w_P9MPceD4-U0bbD2WKeIsAbUiT2UnB3LksV0z-5NjRd5DOictdS-UEmqYyFU-MBlqvV3IgMYWVr3Gp5TyYWS7WrdIYJAGGoOU42z64aXN04zDbMann1u2N08pNSiltBq6Xpoew1MtL_OQS0-NkfBcU-7qioPzhyPTEq50IHcubW2wa617aR6_Gv1u9Hst-9qtlA_KvoP_Nvp9e93LtSMXRwHCUyXhcEsVgYj8uYRLsXy3vXKKwlGeUxTYuBROsYiIM1wCpfJGFV7Ml8gooOxW5BveZuv3k0Pg0r8aIz8bcfh3sP5n28PqvwEAAP__1JSSuQ) in _Nature Sustainability_ , estimated those hyperscale centers used 68 to 99 terawatt-hours of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, and produced 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, roughly Denmark’s entire annual output. Virginia, Oregon, Ohio, and Iowa together accounted for more than half the electricity studied. Researchers said the [_real figures are higher_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDuypDAMRVcDmbpsYz4dEExC9iadkFLbgtaM-BQWuHr3U7wtvEiB6kj33D9f4xey8Dr_xoV6vaZxpZyEVOkY046BMGCk5fPimHlVOnbZ8uiMa8BasN2IQfmi0WMZ-wk94bOk3rbP2hhTeVO-e9_F-oXG-nqqu2fVTeFZYXChbbq6frW25P6-Z63trLXOdo_G-Ia62k6tr8zUYOENRdbteOibLj5mXhkn-WwXHY-wLaX0b9U9FdWvwg2FG3LOj_xXr3tZuOF2ugcqbytK4QbcIekZP0BJeUGlBAvOK-sZCbYJzgQRFSHQ7Qz7JnLeMGCCIN8EKMq_BOd6EQsEIVwBGXahONP9YtkLN5RHH_fMIpyatvBmXpDlO7P-sO6rd_8DAAD__z0jmD4) due to the industry booming since the study window closed. "How did you...?" the lead rescuer asked.
Mary pointed to [a stack of blue packages](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuqzAUgOGngS3Ix3aMGTxc6ZapaaUOrTqhE3wcjmoMMhYoffoqfYXOv_QN_8dluCBHTrcXnMmVPQyJji1SKZSHbcWRcERP8_3K_uBUKK9xOQYppDkBnMAOOBbeadBYexdQE3Y1OWi7sxBCaVFPbuyM7SwqAe25tcbrLozUdloqVHT1pmb38ADAAoAE2xihDdkzhFYrEQxWWpDnsuSmTLRzvnFiDPG-7JSbcZnr6KZS1q1S_yrZV7IPmeibfGby18zbF5VmSZETPbLqM4VK_e-fP1_fn97q7Px6cIy8mbbS4jYjx1-1_HHI7uRPAAAA___2UnTv) in the corner.
Six months earlier, her friends had laughed at the boxes in her pantry. "Planning for the apocalypse, Mary?" But on day four, with no power and no running water, she boiled rainwater on a camping stove and opened the first package of freeze-dried smoked brisket. David took one bite and whispered, "That's... that's actually good."
Most people assume emergency food means chalky MREs and protein bars. It doesn't. Fully cooked, [sliced smoked brisket can keep 97% of its nutrients](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuqzAUgOGngS3Ix3aMGTxc6ZapaaUOrTqhE3wcjmoMMhYoffoqfYXOv_QN_8dluCBHTrcXnMmVPQyJji1SKZSHbcWRcERP8_3K_uBUKK9xOQYppDkBnMAOOBbeadBYexdQE3Y1OWi7sxBCaVFPbuyM7SwqAe25tcbrLozUdloqVHT1pmb38ADAAoAE2xihDdkzhFYrEQxWWpDnsuSmTLRzvnFiDPG-7JSbcZnr6KZS1q1S_yrZV7IPmeibfGby18zbF5VmSZETPbLqM4VK_e-fP1_fn97q7Px6cIy8mbbS4jYjx1-1_HHI7uRPAAAA___2UnTv) and 99% of its taste for 30+ years, with no fridge and no power.
