## Cleveland Public Power Rates Going Up
Cleveland City Council voted 9-3 Monday to [raise Cleveland Public Power rates every year through 2029](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAQhp8GOwwzKmpBcY3dXnulQRyEBMUAu-be_uIW-wLXf5n5vv_nMT-0D_7YvvVOqkRn54OuHKgUSrMJ9KKgj_WMF6WkC-Xksz-2GQVKDsBhmM8U80mmzFCtqqUG7FiRgn7shBCd7CunJJIeacWuGRpJS2OlsAKB1mVYWtENlVf3QQAYAECKvjZ6tBaN7kfZju0ysFbQ6ktMdXEUnY82_MYXpdrEvQrKlXJm1nwxnBhO13XVH_WbYDjdVQyn-w3DCYDh9EH4-VyCN_xdyc0zl7hTytxqQ5wCmZK84Xc-94dJpDNlXlyKz81xFDjWruyhSmo9Lx-Cz7Jnrdh27cPbr_x72JfCvwAAAP__R9uQVA). Residential customers will pay [a new monthly service charge](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0bHO3CAMwPGnIZtPmA9CMmToku3r2jEijrmgcgEBd9G9fZUbqu7dLFn6Wz_51_fy7UIMx_2ne_DU0u6Xg88auTUuC0V-cXTHltPJpbjGtYQajvuipOoBEXBYckk1M7UFu23S_IV-7HhCOxoppeltt0_eeClxNJ4U2m3zo9Z2pU0bpw07b7owXUFEHBCxl_ZGbvRekbNjr0e9DkJL3kJL5dZ2TntIPr7Ti8uN0qOL095aruLrh1CzUPN5nrfz95uupVCzKy1QZKHmiybUHBO5KNT8l_fvDPm5xkDwIQM9a0sPLhUuPYSDCrvKFWq7sscdlFQWKLQ3UHoeFCK4nEt6fS6MBrTRq2T0YGizoIfBgUNtoEdn-tUq9KvsyrTlM8QYam-FlveHC_FDa__9k9ek_gQAAP__5ZijLQ) of $2 in 2027, $4 in 2028, and $5 in 2029. A new three-tier rate structure means heavier users pay more, while a typical household using 500 kilowatt-hours should see bills rise $1 to $2 a month at first. City officials say the added revenue lets the city-owned utility borrow about $30 million and back nearly $70 million in capital projects, including a substation overhaul. _"Having a plan in place to address the problems that we're facing today is all we're asking for,"_ said Ward 7 Councilman Austin Davis. Ward 10 Councilman Michael Polensek voted no, saying the city never showed which neighborhoods would get upgrades first. _"They couldn't show that,"_ he said.
## Leaked Bill Stirs Eminent Domain Fight
A [draft Ohio bill would redefine "public utility,"](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkD2PpDAMhn8NdEFJhq8UKa6hm2uvRCY4g3UeghLfoNtfv2KK1fbb2darR4_fP_f5DsS0P37DE72kLc47noVRBPMcGF_IsK9HOjFnECyZCu2P2WrbK2OUGecjp3JgkNnUq2_xZqKr0ZvBdVrrrh_qzUPQAIsbXYTeLovRLuISQnTd0nWdHmryF9AYMxpjej00AVyMNsDg-ta1y1i1GleSlBvZMG2UIv9PL8xNSM-a_SZylOr2q7JTZafzPJvri-7L_4pVdrqOlZ2OxCQUrvFCqW87I_zFVS3ErEL6x6sC5nSqd24FARVwF8xFSVIF6QPVxa-zX4-TmKn0Q9XqxxOI327y41Jf3n4GAAD__yLKkW0) which legal experts say could let transmission developers take private land to power data centers. The change would add companies holding a power siting board certificate for transmission lines or gas pipelines. It would also speed up land seizures by reworking appraisals. The Ohio Business Roundtable [backs a "deposit and build" approach](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAMhp8m6YiASUhSUFyTbq69MvKAmaAjAYFv0Lz9iSm22HY72_r867P_3Pc7-OCv5284UVM83H5hLQGJMO8m4AsDXDbFijkDYcm--Ou5Sy4VE4KJZU85loSGdtFbPeJNuLVHLeZ14pxPau4PDW51Ts7TsqB9GGVGwIlPKLhR8qGE671ugUKIRQih-DwYaBsG5lWN6_hYupGj9RTzQAfGw0cX3vGFeTDx7IM-iFLpbr86uXVyq7UO7Yrpy79hndzasJNbisGTN61sUex77yCfmAtzCJldWFnKMcUCgdX4L1gGIcTKLBAwgxc1lCIj-IsfEjO9-6xtqj4EX9Tcjfx5gg8fWfrxl19a_g8AAP__PAmYXA) used in 45 other states. Incoming Senate President Bill Reineke, R-Tiffin, said the bill "would not extend eminent domain to anyone who doesn't already have that privilege," while the [Ohio Farm Bureau opposes it](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAQRk-DOyzAvxQUadxt2pQWP-M1yqyxYLIoOX3klXKCVFM86Wm-93FbbzZiPO7v9gGG0r6tB9SCQAR59QhPQHuEM1XI2RKUHEs87qsSauRScjmvZ07lBE-rbILpoZObbsDISQ9CiGGcmt1oD92o9eC8C27opLN-dt0UAGBywnVNNJdQSjlLKUcxtd7qbVPeTnrsde9m1gsIkVJuaYe0x7Thd3pCbn16NGh2orOw7o2phaml1tpWf6YLMrVcg5haClmCv8svB1MLgv2EwF1E5D59YeAWMdUX5sGS5R4Oglw4JV4g_gC_ejTZhLNGxFjGifXi_rARX7_QvyM-jfoNAAD__wEoiy4), warning farmers could lose land and wait months or years for payment. The leak follows votes this month in 21 Ohio cities to restrict or ban data centers.
## UH Opens Lake County Cancer Center
University Hospitals [opened a $39 million cancer center](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAYhJ8Gb1j82IYwMHTxlq4dLYJ_YlQMFhCjvH3lDn2BLqcbTved7uu-3I0PPj4_zY66ps0tEVsJWCvmxQY8MZi4HqlhzqZiyb74-Fw444ICULgtR07lQFsX6FY94gBOdahBqokxNgnZbVqCcEwOj1VIZ9FJQD6aSQC362QETJ3XVyEA3ABAMNlbo5zj1kglRjU-bmRkuPqacl83TJtPLrzTibm3ae-C3mo9Chk-CJ8Jn1tr_d90UFeG8PkiED4DXHK510bTgbHQQe3UmmgxU4uxYqbBfCO16RXrm_C5y3o9mg_BFyHJyJ678eGXXP992an5TwAAAP__qkaAUg) Monday at University TriPoint Medical Center in Concord Township. The [new UH Seidman Cancer Center location](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu5CAQRE-DM0bA2MYOCDZx9jfd0OrBjd0SBgT9PTu3X3mv8OMqleq9P1_rF1CktP-GEx3nI6wJ3y0iM9bVR7wwQtpKfmOtwNgqNUr7apQZpdZST2upuRX0vOpucz0-dZg7dNrOg1JqGG13OOvxCdZomPClrJpfU1DQez2Y56CsNh25e1BrPWmtR2UfHuYQjAc7j_3cvybRK9yIc33wgfmgHOInX1gfPp9ddAdzaeL5S5hFmCXkv9MdCLPcMMIs34kurI34I4_cCjHEJnPB1KT_Zqa0S9x2lB6SxyoDeIp3GVhypZIpsTxxIw9RekyMVZilq24rb4qR2mhFr_YTKP4_xD82eTnzLwAA___iSoyo) sits inside the TriPoint Physician Pavilion in Lake County. UH announced the project in 2025 to expand cancer care in Northeast Ohio. The center has 35 infusion areas, 40 exam rooms, and two linear accelerators for on-site radiation treatment. More than 25 specialists will cover hematology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, gynecologic oncology, and surgical oncology. | Flying together with our sponsor [](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFOwzAQgOGnSbZGPseJk8EDEmSiIDGAmCLXPjcnXDs6W63g6VF5BeZf-ob_47geLUVK5xd7QVPzFtaEtxKxVuTVRbxitMnv-YbMtmJhKpTOqxRyPAAcYFp3zmVHV1dovVHYQ5hbNKDnQQgxjLrdzKTV4J0TSqMEO8FJDdapMAgXQAs_tmTuIABMADAK3Tk7hyCd1fOoZnWaGiXQU83c1Q3zRjnE73xF7ly-tNFste6l6R8auTRyCYz4g54J_YmpfGHtcoqU8J77hTE0_ePy_Pn6_vTWsvH7jWKkMupGifPFUvxT6793XI38DQAA__-rMXXk) **The Brisket That Kept Them Going for 21 Days After Hurricane Helene (Most Families Have Never Heard of It)** When rescuers finally reached Mary's North Carolina home, part of the roof had caved in, and the roads were washed out. Her husband David, 66, was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer. Yet Mary, 63, was standing, and David was alive.
"How did you...?" the lead rescuer asked.
Mary pointed to [a stack of blue packages](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFOwzAQgOGnSbZGPseJk8EDEmSiIDGAmCLXPjcnXDs6W63g6VF5BeZf-ob_47geLUVK5xd7QVPzFtaEtxKxVuTVRbxitMnv-YbMtmJhKpTOqxRyPAAcYFp3zmVHV1dovVHYQ5hbNKDnQQgxjLrdzKTV4J0TSqMEO8FJDdapMAgXQAs_tmTuIABMADAK3Tk7hyCd1fOoZnWaGiXQU83c1Q3zRjnE73xF7ly-tNFste6l6R8auTRyCYz4g54J_YmpfGHtcoqU8J77hTE0_ePy_Pn6_vTWsvH7jWKkMupGifPFUvxT6793XI38DQAA__-rMXXk) in the corner.
Six months earlier, her friends had laughed at the boxes in her pantry. "Planning for the apocalypse, Mary?" But on day four, with no power and no running water, she boiled rainwater on a camping stove and opened the first package of freeze-dried smoked brisket. David took one bite and whispered, "That's... that's actually good."
Most people assume emergency food means chalky MREs and protein bars. It doesn't. Fully cooked, [sliced smoked brisket can keep 97% of its nutrients](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFOwzAQgOGnSbZGPseJk8EDEmSiIDGAmCLXPjcnXDs6W63g6VF5BeZf-ob_47geLUVK5xd7QVPzFtaEtxKxVuTVRbxitMnv-YbMtmJhKpTOqxRyPAAcYFp3zmVHV1dovVHYQ5hbNKDnQQgxjLrdzKTV4J0TSqMEO8FJDdapMAgXQAs_tmTuIABMADAK3Tk7hyCd1fOoZnWaGiXQU83c1Q3zRjnE73xF7ly-tNFste6l6R8auTRyCYz4g54J_YmpfGHtcoqU8J77hTE0_ePy_Pn6_vTWsvH7jWKkMupGifPFUvxT6793XI38DQAA__-rMXXk) and 99% of its taste for 30+ years, with no fridge and no power.
So why is it stocked mostly by the military and the ultra-wealthy? ## National Security Agency Joins Outages
The National Security Agency's classified internal network [went offline yesterday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uxCAQhJ_G7rBYzPmnoEjj7tKmtAisfSTYe4I9o7x9RF4h1Yw00nya-bivdxtiOPd3e6DhjdYTS47IjGk9s6UX2x057JgKkc9MCfm1KqkGASBgWq3jcOEKrTcbosK-RQPjfJMS1Aztw6DS-jaM8-xvErSbx7n31m1ao-wHK7ENptYBwASgJjl16EY9OCl7DX5EOTZaog9MqfuicPIDt_hDF6bO0dFG82B-5qZ_a9TSqKWU0rnPXGfUvFFLtVWyFSdyofQtPJVTuGhzDltALzZKLA60Hhu1tMn4ZwkxhjxU9n7YEP9Y_L-HLqN-AwAA__8RBHvu), forcing staggered arrivals at its Fort Meade, Maryland, headquarters. Officials said there is no evidence of a cyberattack, and sources blamed routine system patching. It is the latest in a week of breakdowns: Microsoft's email and Teams outage last Thursday, Friday's nationwide ground stop, Monday's Chase outage that rippled to other banks, and trouble at [Apple's iCloud and App Store](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD0OnDAQhU9jOq88xstP4SIN3aZNibx4AEfGRp4BxO0jkiOkmWKe9Ol779dn_LgQQ1p-ug0tz3lMeFFEZixjIpcPdgtyWLBcOXviXJCPUSvdSAAJ3egmDieOUHk7I2qsK7TQ9m-lQPdQrdaYtzMtdN7PiKb5Qt8Y1_ZzM9eADvsq2AcHAB2A7lT3wqk1zaRUbcC3qFphFPrAubx-55B4xTne-cTymvJWRbsy7yTqH0IPQg_p3jPxEwk9PGChB4DntEIP34NCQiKhh-n-YpH_CpKM4UR57N4xknQkN5duSVjOMD2PqWQiySvKg6QrKH2-ktBDVazfrxBjoObxXDYX4l8v_r81T6v_BAAA___YcIpI) yesterday. None has been blamed on hackers. Officials have instead pointed to aging equipment. Apple said an internal update caused its outage, Microsoft cited a networking bug, and the FAA [paused new router](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFygzAQRL8GOjG6A4NcqEhD57QpGVk6gRKBPNIZkr_P4HxCyp2d2d23H7fpZkIM2_xuVtLs07TRUSIxU562YtKTzUwcZspHSq5wysTPCSX2AkCAmozlsNMEtdOeCKmtScNwvUgJeIV60bajtnVD1xFepENA2Q6qU55auF-tU3XQZxwAKABUUjVkh663UrYduIHkUHWSXOCUm88UNl7Ix5-0U25sWuuoF-ZHqdq3CscKx-M4Gp--T4zTr3CMYSdx6gpHJruIP6gi1mBzKsmzuJvtqwhvjPD38AIbBPZ11u5xhBhD6c8R82pCfJXy_67aNf4GAAD__wuzffs) installations after a faulty one triggered the ground stop. # How to Use Volume Buttons to Take a Picture on an iPhone
Did you know you can use your iPhone's volume buttons to snap photos? Learning how to get the best angle for a photo on an iPhone can be tricky. Using the iPhone volume buttons can make it easier to take a picture when holding the iPhone at an awkward angle. Here's an iPhone camera trick: how to take a photo with your iPhone's volume buttons.
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Use this iPhone camera tip to snap a selfie at a less awkward angle for your wrist.**
* **Get the feel of an old-fashioned point-and-shoot camera with a physical shutter button.**

## How to Take a Picture with the Volume Button on iPhone
### System Requirements
_This tip was performed on an iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27. Find out how to update to the_ _[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261527-8632702-9948707669-2kf3258b1f)_ _._ Want to know how to enable taking pictures with a volume button? You don't have to set the volume button to take a picture on your iPhone; it's automatic! This is one of my favorite iPhone Camera tricks; it's super simple! You might not have realized that the iPhone side buttons work with your camera. Here's how to take pictures with the volume button on iPhone:
1. Open the **Camera app**.

|
---
2. Navigate to Camera mode if you are not already there.

---
3. The volume buttons are located on the side of your iPhone. When you're ready to take a photo (or start a video if you are in video mode), press either the volume up or volume down button. It doesn't matter which one you press, but I tend to favor the volume down button, since it is usually closer to my index finger.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?
If you'd like to learn more about iPhone Life's premium paid subscription, [click here](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261527-3296969-759d538362-2kf3258b1f)

Now you know how to take a picture with the volume button on your iPhone! You can hold your phone either vertically or horizontally, whichever works best for you. If these steps didn't work for you, then you might have accidentally toggled off this Camera setting that is on by default. To toggle it back on, go to Settings, Camera, and make sure Use Volume Up for Burst is on. As the toggle implies, if you press and hold the volume up button, your iPhone will take photos in burst mode. A single press and release will still result in one photo.
Enjoy taking selfies without any more awkward finger stretching! Next, find out how to [adjust exposure on an iPhone camera](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261527-8632703-ffff16360b-2kf3258b1f) or [how to take burst photos on the iPhone](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261527-8632704-f7f4a78d39-2kf3258b1f). Also, if you're an iPhone photography enthusiast, you might want to check out our guide covering the [icons on your iPhone camera](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261527-8632705-fb56a12ed5-2kf3258b1f) and how to make the most use of these features.

## Texas to Audit Senate Election Ballots
The state will pull randomly chosen paper ballots from the Nov. 3 U.S. Senate race and check them against the machine count to confirm the outcome, [the state's first statewide audit](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDtywyAQhk8jdWhg9S4o0qhz2pQaELsWEyw8sDb27TPyFdL_z-_nsl6MD_64fpsban5RXA8sOSAzpvVhMaFh-3YpHpgZkw9I4U0rSBiEUkJNq9nYP3FVtdNWulnVqNU491K2MPX1rtGRlds4j6M0Fqa-ReoUkWznznbUDrXXZ5pSalIgFXQNzkBWOdkjzDTRWHUSneeYGt6R8WUyhXd8Ymq2eKuD3pnvuWq_KlgqWEopDcUXDHt8ZI7HKapgOW9VsHzs4u633ywyHoZRJLOhIJ8yi8yGsXiHwpoQIgvzcJ7rpN29-BB8Hs4x15vx4dPN_0T21PAXAAD__xIwg_Y) of its kind. Secretary of State Robert Howden will [draw a random 10-digit number](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2uqzAQRlcDnZE9QMCFi9fQ5bW3tPwzDpYMjuxJCLu_Ilu41TRHR2e-n7u-m5ji_vhvNlT0CVnveNSERFj0y2JBQ_b0Je9YCUtMGNIZNHC4MSGYmLVxFN-oReuV5V6KFpWY5Mh5D_PYruo29gCTtejmyUszgcTQBzlaaUGgt21Ul00IMQvgAoYOJQQrPB8RZJjD1AwcfaRcOlqR8GNqSGd-Y-lc3tqkVqJnbfp_DSwNLMdxdK7kWks2vlL25ry4BpbrswaWr4FVMoW-h_CIHhkmdBTzzszLR7pAUyi6hBp77sHPhmFwgQ0Ge2aDtExOs5S9FIN1Q7fSltqi_POIKcV6u6ofm4npG0l_3Pat4DcAAP__1VKQrQ) during a 2:30 p.m. livestream today, and that number will determine which ballots are pulled. Lawmakers ordered the audits in 2021, and 16 other states run similar checks. "_Texans deserve to know their elections are secure and their votes are counted accurately_ ," Howden said. Counties using voting machines must also [hand-count sample ballots](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAYRZ_G3ogAx38DQ5ds6drR4ufiIGGI4IsTv32VSH2Czvfo6uj8XJerDjGk9VtvUPTyeUl41ggilOVhUKDJHK7khEooIcLHwy-Sy4EJwcS0aEthxyJapwx3s2ihxDj3nHdy6tubcm6U4wSpRztI0fVDN1oY6ya4s-2EboN6vwkhJiG5kOcTZumNcLyHnP3kx-bM4QLlcqIbCC9dfTzyjnKyeWujuhHda9N9NfLSyMsHMLk4FPOoIaHWN_e3sApbQLocLHtWSROYwRpSZZtOThMcQ4SlkBPTDxeoMp9jzM-QVpbyzjq2Z0IjL21R7v4MMYY6vCXXTYf4caJ_ptyV_A0AAP__oKCNgQ) from the Senate race, the Texas Supreme Court chief justice race, and one local race of their choosing.
## Texas Ranks 14th for Credit Card Debt
Texans carried an average of $4,620 in credit card debt per person at the end of 2025, the [14th-highest balance in the nation](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAMhp8GOmUsQQIUFNfQ7bVXMsIWwbOOnbG1YfP2N95X2EIaFZpP-v5_H-sH--Dj_S8_ZNbvPa1RzhJEVfL6tUkW1u3tcopSVLIPsof3vpKhGyACjitb9S9ZsXXzZtyErcw4TFdjOhqv7TFby7dpcDzYsbM4TOOEQzf1PRnpN2u71s-VhogjkkHqLzLRvqEzV6FpH_eh6Y04rylf9BCVby57eKeX5ItNjzbMh-qzNN2fhpaGlvM8LzZ4-0lH-iqaYt1qaKleDS0hWQ4NLfVmQwtibXX6AUPm-FkAez3AR9BDILL6FGFPGWyuf4Dl7MDJpsAF-CWZ7wIbB45WCmRhe0B_IwNPybVKig0tbZ7d8_Qh-HKrSvcH-_BjoL8M_jXT_wAAAP__5eaYOA) and 6.2% above the national average, according to a study by a personal finance company. Balances in Texas rose $180, or 4.1%, from late 2024, while average balances climbed in all 50 states. Texas still [outpaces all four neighbors](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O4zAMhJ9G7hSItOKfQsU17nLtlYZ-qFg4xQokbn7efuEA-wRbECwIznwz_y7rxaac9utfeyPDr1jWnZ4tEzPV9ctRJcvuHWrZqTHVlCnmd1xR4SABJEyr9ZwetEIXjFNhho4MjPNZqR6nc7eZwUfQEa0fw6T96N0MMep5VN663vehS-ZQA4AJUAHqE80YHQR1JpzjFEehFYXEpZ54I6aXbTG_y4PqyZdbl83GfG-i_yNwEbj4Z98fB4HLEUXg8nn52bLa_X-ToHmTsVS5petGjaWvh4f0tgYZyLG0LPWASt6pHtPKLnDpqgn3Z8o5teHgut5syh8M_mV7D4PfAQAA___VB4WG), from Louisiana at $3,610 to Arkansas at $3,310. North Richland Hills resident Joni Kattau [owed about $55,000](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDmu4zAMQE8jdwpEJt4KFdO4y7RTGlqoWIBsBRKz3X6gAP8Ev2HB7T3y33W9mpjicftrdtL8Dnk96FUTMVNZH5YKGbYfX_JBlanERCF9wooKBwkgYVqN4_ikFTqvrfIzdKRhnHulzjj13aaVCmMYbD-QGcGTtzDPDtFZN479EFQXddsGABOgArycaMZgwauecA5TGMVFkY-cy4k3YnqbGtInP6mcXN67pDfmexXnPwIXgUu9k-Py2FN2JrVjWpfAhd8CF_OoHA-BSysIXBpZ4ALwEzxZlvGQvJHcyBSWOcgvU35zleNtN_IVeZOuNC3ZRrqi_f0VU4p1aL633cT01eNffvWp8X8AAAD__xlvjVg) at her peak, with credit cards her biggest burden. Counselors helped her lower her interest rates and set a strict budget. She's now debt-free, paying off her cards every month.
## Spring Gets Uber Eats Drone Delivery
Uber Eats [started delivering food by drone](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpTAQRE8DmZG7DR8cONiEbDbdEBncBksGj-we-Nx-xb_CxFUqvVf_vqYvG2I41r92J8Nvn6aDrhKJmfL0M1Mmy_PtcjqoMOUQycfbTyjxJQAEDJNdOJw0Qe3MLJ2Gmgz0upNS4dDVm6Ee_dyqVrX06nsvByWXTndW4yKdl6oO5lkDgAFQArYNafQzONkRaj_4vmolucApN7wR09sWH-90Um6WtNfRbMzfpVJ_KhwrHK_rataU3J7yEY7V7pTDYp9qheMjV-FYOOW7wvERFGS5iGh_jmWjIqCw-OgKRzGclG9RKJ9heTI1gFYa2job932FGEN5PXjrbkP80PAvTzwN_g8AAP__e12IjA) Tuesday in the Houston suburb of Spring, where Zipline aircraft hover more than 300 feet up and lower orders into yards on a tether. Customers tap a new drone icon in the app and pick a clear drop-off spot. The drones fly up to 70 mph and carry up to 8 pounds to homes within 10 miles of participating restaurants, with [no tip or extra fees](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL_GdEbexRBcuLiGLtdeiQxeE0sORPYeJH9_gl-4fjRv3vzcx7uLKa7Lt3uS5XfYxpWOkoiZ8vg7USbH08fnbaXClGOikD5hRIWdBJDQj27muNMIlbeT8gYqsnAzrVIN9m31sHoO0zQrMFoZR73vtMOu8UorpYN2VEV7tgFAD6gAdU0GwwRetYQm9OEmtCIfecs1P4jp7UpIn22nXM_bs0r2wfwqovkSOAgcjuOoaV2cX4jPgMABG-i1aQUOp5Ekx0UWdpmLvMykpxR3ypGKjKu8EAKHKlv_OmJKsXTniOXpYrqY_M-rdot_AQAA___NGn7V). Jersey Mike's, Zaxby's, Urban Bird, and Abu Omar Halal are among the first restaurants, with service from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Dallas is set to come online next, then dozens more cities, as the companies attempt to reach [1 million deliveries a day](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO4zAMRU9jdwxEjpPYhYpt3M22WxqyRI2JVaRA4jiTnH7hXGEbNh_4fO__-Vw-nSTJX7_dja3-xLJkfrTEqlyX75UrO12foZbMTblK4piecSFDF0AEHBfnVXZesA92NWHCni1ep7MxHzSe-81OuA4xeheG1UzDcDVu9IxxiHSZAvGlF3u0IeKIZJCGE08UVwzmzDTFMV67wXAQLfWkGyv_uBbTs-xcT77c-mQ31XvrPn51NHc0K_vN1-_styPuaD7aO5oRj3PtaD60wOUAL7knydzg7QeBk-xcn9C47uIZ1P3lBiVGkAzvx_AQ3SCUF-cjAC8q3EALxJJSeXQ099WG-0NSknY50L9uTtKbVP9z4N3SvwAAAP__lYGSTg) by the end of 2029. Uber says the drones fly in rain and take the quietest path. Rival DoorDash already delivers by drone around Dallas-Fort Worth. An [Amazon drone test in Richardson](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuqzAQRL8GOiPvAgkULl5Dl9feEtl4HVYyENkLJH9_RX7h1iPNmTM_j_FhOfL6_G8XMvIO27jSmSOJUBp3R4msuI9P20pZKHGkED9hRI03BaCgG-0kfNAIpTdO-x5KMnDvW61r7NpyNlQ3oKHW1LrWWaobb3Xvulq7usXgQsnmagOADlADNhX1GBx43RL2oQv3otHkWbZUyUxCb5tD_GwHpWraljKaWeSVi_pfgUOBw3me1Wta7PNKCxwunwKHy0WRlayi3ddppqy-VspT5IMSU1a8Kpk5qy9D5d3tyZXJ-NfJMXK-XUuei-X4Bcsf_zoM_gYAAP__QCOCnA) resulted in noise complaints.
| Flying together with our sponsor [](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1OwzAUxfGnSbZGvnbSOIMHJMhEQWIAMUV2fdxauEllX_rB06PwCsxH-h3p_7GbdjamOB9e7AmGb2GZZlxLAjPy9O2QYdndfV5mFEaOCSHdwySF3G6INqQnu-d4wUS1N074gWoY6odOCCV1Vx9N2LYiKN13nZOCrCZSzmnv7eB8q1VfR7NqRKRJCpJtg0EGR150kEPQoa9aAR95yQ0fwbjZEtJ9uSA3--VUJ3NkPpdKPVRyrOQYMvADnyO8y7F8gZtlTnHGOqsxI1TqcXz-fH1_equz8edrTCmW7XpzONmY_lT-Z4yLkb8BAAD__4yvdCA) **The Brisket That Kept Them Going for 21 Days After Hurricane Helene (Most Families Have Never Heard of It)** When rescuers finally reached Mary's North Carolina home, part of the roof had caved in, and the roads were washed out. Her husband David, 66, was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer. Yet Mary, 63, was standing, and David was alive.
"How did you...?" the lead rescuer asked.
Mary pointed to [a stack of blue packages](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1OwzAUxfGnSbZGvnbSOIMHJMhEQWIAMUV2fdxauEllX_rB06PwCsxH-h3p_7GbdjamOB9e7AmGb2GZZlxLAjPy9O2QYdndfV5mFEaOCSHdwySF3G6INqQnu-d4wUS1N074gWoY6odOCCV1Vx9N2LYiKN13nZOCrCZSzmnv7eB8q1VfR7NqRKRJCpJtg0EGR150kEPQoa9aAR95yQ0fwbjZEtJ9uSA3--VUJ3NkPpdKPVRyrOQYMvADnyO8y7F8gZtlTnHGOqsxI1TqcXz-fH1_equz8edrTCmW7XpzONmY_lT-Z4yLkb8BAAD__4yvdCA) in the corner.
Six months earlier, her friends had laughed at the boxes in her pantry. "Planning for the apocalypse, Mary?" But on day four, with no power and no running water, she boiled rainwater on a camping stove and opened the first package of freeze-dried smoked brisket. David took one bite and whispered, "That's... that's actually good."
Most people assume emergency food means chalky MREs and protein bars. It doesn't. body:
Our #StopNoem and #ImpeachNoemNow campaigns won Silver at the Anthem Awards.
#
We have some news to share, Peter.
**Voto Latino’s #StopNoem and #ImpeachNoemNow campaigns just won a Silver Anthem Award, presented by The Webby Awards!**
The Anthem Awards are the world’s largest social impact awards, and our campaigns were chosen from more than 2,500 entries across 43 countries in the Human & Civil Rights category. **They were recognized for uniting a broad coalition around one shared demand: accountability from DHS.**
But this award isn’t just ours; it also belongs to you and every person who has supported our work.
For the past two years, our community has lived with a target on its back, hunted and forced into the shadows by chaotic and lawless immigration enforcement. From the very start of Kristi Noem’s tenure, we knew we couldn’t sit by and watch.
So we fought back, together. Alongside faith leaders, unions, civil rights organizations, and immigrant rights groups, we armed our community with digital toolkits, filled lawmakers’ desks with petitions and letters, and put targeted ads in front of vulnerable Republicans so they had to answer to the voters they represented.
Every petition you signed, every letter you sent, and every dollar you gave helped make this campaign possible. We’re deeply honored by this recognition, but our work is far from over. **Families in our community are still living in fear, and we’ll keep fighting until DHS is held accountable.**

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

We’re proud that every newly elected Justice Democrat we helped send to
Congress voted “no” on Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker today.

[2]@DropSiteNews 🗳️ 7 of the incoming Democrats who said they voted
against Hakeem Jeffries for speaker identified themselves in a joint
statement as Darializa Avila Chevalier, Adam Hamawy, Frederick Haynes,
Melat Kiros, Donavan McKinney, Chris Rabb and Claire Valdez. They cited a
mandate on Medicare for All, 'stopping ICE terror,' money in politics and
'ending the genocide in Gaza.' They said talks with Jeffries showed
'meaningful progress' but 'there is still work to be done.'

They showed courage to fight for the agenda our communities deserve. This
is the leadership and agenda voters across the country are demanding.

Our bold new leaders aren’t going to just rubber-stamp or coronate a
speaker without knowing what their plan is to lower costs, address the
data center crisis, get big money out of politics, end funding to Israel
and so much more.

But this “no” vote will put a target on their backs from the Democratic
establishment.

name: Wes Moore
subject: Giving this up
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2313%2E1086043%2ECauG7U)
Peter,
It took 250 years for America’s states to elect three Black governors. In the 2026 midterms, they elected four more in a single night.
**Before this month, I was America’s only Black governor, and I’m happy to lose that title.**
The night before I was sworn in as the third in 2023, Deval Patrick of Massachusetts, the second African American ever elected governor, pulled me aside and told me one of his only regrets: He had waited until he left office to think seriously about who would come next. As a mentor of mine, I knew he shared that not as a throwaway line, but as a charge.
My being the third African American ever elected governor in our nation’s history was less a statement of progress than an indictment of how slowly it has come. That night, I promised to make sure America’s leadership looks like America. And I would not wait until I left office to start.
So I campaigned hard for Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, David Crowley in Wisconsin and Aaron Ford in Nevada, not just because they would make history, but because they are good public servants who understand the assignment: making child poverty and income inequality _history._
**Since Election Day, plenty of people have called this the end of an era. I am more interested in the next one.**
Voters of every party demanded a change to the status quo. They are done with a system where families do everything right and still can’t get ahead. They want their bills to be lower. They want a government that works for them.
**[We’re ready to get to work on these key priorities-- but I need you with me to make sure we’re successful. Will you chip in $5 or any amount to power our progress in Maryland today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261118-1.NzKsYa&refcode=em-20261118-1&t=2&akid=2313%2E1086043%2ECauG7U)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261118-1.NzKsYa&amount=5&refcode=em-20261118-1&t=21&akid=2313%2E1086043%2ECauG7U)**
In Georgia, Wisconsin, and Nevada voters elected governors who promised to fight for them and their families, make life more affordable, and make government deliver -- regardless of party.
After their wins, Keisha, David, and Aaron promised to govern for those who didn’t vote for them, too. That is a welcome break from a decade of leaders who treated half the country like the enemy. You cannot love your country if you hate half the people in it.
**[The next era belongs to leaders who govern for all of it. If you’re with me in that mission, please chip in $5 to support our work today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261118-1.NzKsYa&refcode=em-20261118-1&t=22&akid=2313%2E1086043%2ECauG7U)**
Come January, a total of five Black governors will serve at once, 10% of the nation’s total. And Stacey Plaskett will take office as the first Black woman elected to lead a U.S. territory. Gina Hinojosa in Texas and Amy Acton in Ohio made history of their own. **_This is an important step toward a more perfect union._**
For nearly four years, I have been the only Black governor of any state. In January, I will lose that title. I have never been happier to give something up. And I pray nobody ever has to hold that title again.
Elevate,
Wes

## Midterms Exit Poll Takeaways
Turnout, opposition to President Trump, and the left-leaning views of younger voters drove this year's Colorado election results, according to [a new exit poll](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAQhp8Gb47g7BgYGLp4S9eO1hmOGBWbyL4mzdtXRKrUvcst9-u--_6Py3TBlNN2fceVHPs4bfQ4MjHTPtF34lvJ2eOBc9kS40q7X3CbQMLQKtUqM6HndKepxya4GMHj0JBT2p6lHIyFZnG-77vOajoH4yVY7aORczQ6aDv7s5VNcvWeUsqoTiqwp4imQxhonqMKaLToJYXEZT_xQr7ksmMoMT_LnfaTL2uT3cJ8O0T3JmAUMP5mjq-t7gWMlSBgVKoO_SfSVsu2arYvqzldW8ZPwgc-DwFjs7twe6Sc0zHUR64rpvyC8j_7ujv4CQAA__9vI36c). Voters under 45 backed the [Amendment 87 graduated income tax](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOp-w4fgpXKShu7Qp0WKvYRX_IHvD5d4-IlKeIPWMRt98H4_lAeQpbu8QULNxS8Rn8ciMecFv4iN5b6DAmiIxBMxmh7ioRvVCSiHHBQzTiUsHtdXOKQN9jVoO071p-nFS9a7lCrLrm-EuLTrszGSscx1KQDW0vVxr0teelHKUbSPVdHMwtqB6XFcnLYxD1TVoiVO-8Y4m-ZTBJudf6cR8MynUXu_MR6nat0rNlZq5lL_alVdqvn4IR9EW8UpfccMszsSYiyifeDAZ8CI5YeAgBk8liCOnkyxa8aQYKW4iQN4oCpeygIDRBowsxqFSc521PZ7kPZX-gt0CkP8F4386PbX6CQAA__8iJpD6) 68% to 32%, more than offsetting voters 45 and older, who rejected it 62% to 38%. [Younger voters also backed](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuszAMhZ8mbFSxaSEMGf6Frf96R2SCUyIFUiUubd_-ikp9grt4-uTvnPNzHa8UYthu_2llK86PGz9LZBHOI7-C3FOMjgpNaQtCK2e30DaixrYGqMGM5CTsPJ6pmq336Kit2ELXX7RuTY_VYhvuph7mi-68bg30jvFicKKuPyOTxyrY4x8AGGg0YH_yZBrClqfJw0ymU2fNc5CUT7KwSzFlmpOP77RzPrm0VtEuIveimn8KB4XDl_mUCRsfkMLh0CgcAI7TKRze6bHdONdfvt6TcC610KueKMYk9cpUHpmLwqHKdr4_Q4yhtEem20ohfvzyx-l2i78BAAD__9MmhD4) Proposition NN, which effectively ends TABOR refunds to boost school funding, by 70% to 30%, while most older voters opposed it. The poll also found that 65% of voters statewide view Trump unfavorably, and 57% said their own financial situation had gotten worse over the past year.
## Polis Warns of Medicaid Costs
Gov. Jared Polis [warned state budget writers](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdER4CMQULrahy7ZborE9DiMZjOzZsPv3T0R6X_CaqY7m3Hv_PJcncuL99Rs3suLjstNZE4lQWegfy5FT8ljR5Z0FNyp-xX2BDsZW61abBb3wm5Y7NsHGCB7Hhqx-TEPXjWaCZrXTPfihH3FAZ4YA3jn9oB5wCjSY6H3D9vqntTa67zRMt4imRxjJuagDmoe6dxRYcrnJSj6nXDDkmP7nN5Wbz1uT7CpyVNX_UjArmL-ZTxne6YIUzJdGwaz1dXoF85ET1_bEstfW_Q0vkvYsLFRqu1FgjxwUzE2x4Tg5Ja7jleW1IaePV3442dvCVwAAAP__fcmB1Q) that Medicaid could soon consume all new revenue from voter-approved Amendment 87 if its spending growth is not reined in. Amendment 87 raises income taxes on households and businesses earning more than about $500,000 and [is expected to generate](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE9jMo_shgUTONiEbDbdEDV2M1jyD7J7fvb2K570TvCykqpUX6n-3tc7hhjy4w8msuz2NdO7RWKmutIn8FlidNhwKzkwJqruwLyCglFqLbVZ0XF40Tpg5-2-g8OxI6un-ZdSo5mhO-xgBuXcjMrNahonIjdOsG_G9xqM0dgFe_VprY3ulYb5tqPpEUbatl17NJMYFPnApd74IFdiqejLHv-VF9WbK6mL9mA-m-h_C1gELN-Z9syXL2C5CAIWrQUs6lKYKPtEmaWZZKX2jNzkia1Rk4-K_olMXobsSiLJ-BGwdNX68x1iDG28Nj0ShvjF5x9e97LwPwAA__9VrYNs) roughly $2 billion a year for healthcare, schools, and child care. Al Jennings of Arvada, a World War II Marine who fought in the Battle of Iwo Jima, [died Saturday night](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHS2yAQBOCnQR0eOOmXUEGRRp3TptSc4LDOQeBBBCVvn7Ff4a93Zufb_XVf78iR0-MnHmSrC2ui64xUK5WV_nJ95RgdnrjlxBUPKm7HtIKCUWottVnRVW60Dth5GwI4HDuyepq_lBrNDN1ulR6cMn5Qo6ftqwczjBNg8GYOTk1BdWzffVpro3ulYb4FND3CSNsWtEcziUGR55rLre7kcswFfQ7xX25Ubi4fXbR7ra9T9D8ELAKW3759AgHLe4-AJWaHUcCCpaFHeeUSvbywSGbZqFLBJDF5yVeWTz5Qnn9K45aLxCiflBKnxyk90ymxSq2UgKUr1r8ujpHP8W18HMjx46nfvLJZ-B8AAP__y3qKkw) at age 100. Voters under 45 backed the 68% to 32%, more than offsetting voters 45 and older, who rejected it 62% to 38%. Proposition NN, which effectively ends TABOR refunds to boost school funding, by 70% to 30%, while most older voters opposed it. The poll also found that 65% of voters statewide view Trump unfavorably, and 57% said their own financial situation had gotten worse over the past year. Polis Warns of Medicaid Costs Gov. Jared Polis that Medicaid could soon consume all new revenue from voter-approved Amendment 87 if its spending growth is not reined in. Amendment 87 raises income taxes on households and businesses earning more than about $500,000 and roughly $2 billion a year for healthcare, schools, and child care. Medicaid takes up close to 40% of the state's yearly budget, and Polis again proposed a hard cap on its growth tied to population growth and inflation. Polis presented to the Joint Budget Committee last week and will submit a revised version in early January before he leaves office. WWII Veteran Dies at 100 Al Jennings of Arvada, a World War II Marine who fought in the Battle of Iwo Jima, at age 100. Jennings landed on Iwo Jima in February 1945 and witnessed the raising of the American flag atop Mount Suribachi, a moment captured in a famous photograph. He was 20 during the battle, and one of his brothers fought in the same fight. FOX31 named him its Serving Those Who Serve in 2024. For decades, Jennings shared the lessons of the war with younger generations through , a charity founded in Denver. ## Arizona Bids for Space Academy
Arizona [submitted its application](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQhZ_GdEbMYGApXNyGbm-bEk1gvIxiwLKdRezTR6zyBmlOdfSdn4_7eCfxsj3-08o208uNGx_Jc84cx8Sb7DGR43yGyCFliinI9DViha0G0HAbacry5NFQMdu6nfrOFGyh65uq6gBNsVhqG1P30M00UeOqtnVM7dxgXwM0-AmF2IsHADeoqwaxNHOPNRi-Qe_YsFOm4lnyHsu8MEV57Rs5f-5PjuW0r4W3S84hqfqfwkHhcBxHSS9Hq_jzMigcrgSFA8AlncLhF6NJ1qTfy_QhedHfSadAE2uaaOb11CHuYU_kFQ5FtHM4xHtJbadM9VhJ_LtB_ut5T4s_AQAA__9WcYRO) to host the U.S. Space Academy, a proposed NASA training school for future astronauts, engineers, and technicians. The state's [proposal](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAUhJ8GuoPwDxgXFGm2u2lTooN9fLGuwcg-u2j36aNNIuUBbjfSaD7NzK-P5QNjisfnT9xpZnyF5aCrJmKmslQ6Yi4VA_HzLHRWxlLP6L4W2csRhAAxLeg4PmjR2PpZjc4a3dIsjB363gip2202Klh0wpB3vndilXaVhkalJlKr9WMb5zdPCDEJ1Q9SdtpbqYSmSdhAmkKje_KRc-l4IyzxlQ8M6ZkfVDqX9zbNG_NZG_WjkbdG3q7r6r4eGd9mI2_vSY28_Qv-V7BGX4EzbLky3KFCPdERoENP-xNCLnBgxQrhzvdCgJVLPvDOf3EcXaLFkh9DPwqw6-BAj97B5LQGEQbfK2PsYE238Z7aMvvziinFOppG9587xvSnP3_3-scsfwcAAP__Y2uaVQ) would place the first class of 300 students at Arizona State University's Tempe campus, with permanent sites suggested near Pulliam Airport in Flagstaff or at an ASU innovation zone next to Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport in Mesa. President Trump called for the creation of an academy in an August executive order, and Gov. Katie Hobbs later appointed [a 13-member steering committee](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkT2O2zAQRk8jdWOIQ-qHhYo06jZtSmFEjmxiKVIgJ1Z2Tx_YTQ6Q9nvAAx6-Xx_rB4UY0v0nHTwLfe9r4qtGFuGyVk4hl0o7y9dZ-KxCpZ7Bfa7Y4QBKgZpWchKevBpq_awHZ0fT8qxG23fdqNC0j9miHjwr21utzei89fvAaDbs3KYMb22YXz6l1KR01yPejLeoleFJ2Z0N743p2AfJ5SYPphK-c6I9fuUnl5vLRxvnh8hZG_2jwaXB5bqum8JXyQs3uFCR4CI3uLzGBpeYHcU3eMsaXO75CZ8kgeGRt62C0FmB_5xcpIJkiJQ8SPl9nJCL58IeElUCKRRSSHcgR56PLwgJ_lnHHnDaet37DfZh6sGoaYRN9wToB29tNwza-7bM_rxCjKEOY2O6-0EhvtPkf195zvg3AAD__xaYoms) to build the state's case. ## Senior Safety Idea Earns Honors
Arizona-based Helpany's AI fall-prevention and health monitoring device was [named](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkLuOpDAQRb_GZEYu4-YRONiErDfdEBWm3JTaPGRbIPrrV8zMH0xSSV2de3X-PYcncuD19RcXshk_fljpTIFypjgkWnmLCT3la4-0p4wx7ezeg1a6lgAS2gFd5oMGg8Vkq9p1jSnIQtM9lGpAm2K2vlbKY1W5aiIkZ3CEUflHO3ZtY5QbC7Y3DwBaqNRD69JMna7AUAudJ0NeGEUT5y2WeSaM_NlW9OHaDoql25Yi2DnnPYnqj9C90P15niV-PC4crjsgdH83CN0D3KcRuv_BSLctO65XksgyXSnTIt9EO68vGSnxRGtO8nYgv3XIwMf9nLeFktB9Ee20nxwCp7oRRr0W5PC1Kv9W6GH1_wAAAP__ZTGNJg) one of _TIME's_ Best Inventions of 2026 in the medical and healthcare category. name: Grassroots Army
subject: Here's why I'm asking you to enlist
body:
Ordinary people doing extraordinary things. Here is why I am asking you to join, and what your membership makes possible.
---
Ordinary people doing extraordinary things. Here is why I am asking you to join, and what your membership makes possible.
| Grassroots Army Here is the why.
---
Friend, I want to tell you why I started the Grassroots Army, and why I am asking you to join it. After this election, a lot of good people felt like quitting. I understand that. But I have learned something in my life: politicians in Washington and Lansing do not save a country. Ordinary people do. Parents, neighbors, church families and small business owners who decide they are done sitting on the sidelines. That is who we are. Rooted in faith, built on family, and fighting for freedom. **What we are building** We bring receipts, not rumors. And people are listening. Last week alone, November 9 to 16:
* **1,099 posts** across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, Threads and YouTube
* **Nearly 4 million** views and impressions
* More than **151,000 reactions** and more than **41,000 shares**
* One story, where I read the chart as a doctor on the "Trumpcare for All" pitch for Medicare for All, reached **more than 1.2 million** views and impressions by itself

Every one of those numbers is a real person who stopped scrolling and heard the other side of the story. That is how minds change, one honest conversation at a time. **Why membership matters** Our members are the backbone of this Army. Their monthly support is what keeps new videos coming every single day, keeps the research honest, and puts us on the air live. Here is what members already have:
* The first batch of numbered member cards has been printed and shipped
* A members newsletter from me, and a members only feed
* Signed hardcover books on the way to our Sergeants, Captains and Generals
* Our live show, starting **Thursday, November 19 at 6:00 PM Eastern** , on Facebook, YouTube and X

**Your card. Your number. For life.** Every member gets a real, hard plastic card mailed to your door, with a member number that is yours for life. It is never given to anyone else. The front of the member card. And on the back is a QR code. When you are talking with someone about what we are doing, hand them your card. They scan it and land right on our website. The back of the member card. Scan the code and it opens GrassrootsArmy.org. **That is how we grow our Army. Each one teach MANY.** **Pick your rank** | **Private** $10 a monthStep up and stand with us.
* Weekly members newsletter from me
* Your own numbered hard plastic member card
* Members only feed
* 5% off all merch

---
**Sergeant** $20 a monthLead from the front. Everything in Private, plus:
* A signed hardcover of my book, _Men Are Forged, Not Found_
* 10% off all merch

**Captain** $100 a monthJoin the officer corps. Everything in Sergeant, plus:
* Live quarterly Zoom Q&A with me, first Sunday of each quarter at 6:00 PM ET
* 15% off all merch

**General (Gold)** $250 a monthThe highest rank. Everything in Captain, plus:
* Metallic gold card design
* An exclusive Gold only shirt each year
* Early access to new merch drops
* Quarterly small group call with me
* Founding Gold wall on our website (opt in)
* 20% off all merch

Prices plus tax. Your numbered member card is a one time $15 (U.S. shipping included), ordered right after you join. Cancel any time. You must be 18 or older to join.
[Enlist today](https://9l762.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsDg0fV3Ji0XTonBupr9Lp/4D7xyjH8ZtmV)
I am not asking you to do everything. I am asking you to stand up and be counted, and to bring one more patriot with you.
**Support and join the Grassroots Army as we take back our country, rooted in faith, built on family, and fighting for freedom. 🫡🇺🇸**
For God and Country,
**Dr. Garrett Soldano D.C.**
Grassroots Army
P.S. Already a member? Thank you. Forward this to one person who should be standing with us.
**GJS Investments LLC**
8357 Barony Pt, Mattawan, MI 49071

Grassroots Army is a brand owned and operated by GJS Investments LLC, a Michigan limited liability company. Memberships are not tax deductible and are not political campaign contributions.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tammy Baldwin for Senate
body:
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5841%2E35263%2EgWLCB8)
Peter,
The same president who said there wasn't enough money to fund Medicare and child care has allotted **at least $1.6 billion in vanity projects.**
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20261118-vanity.S1XxmD&amount=10&refcode=&t=2&akid=5841%2E35263%2EgWLCB8)
Let that sink in for a second.
For years, we’ve been told by MAGA Republicans that there’s room in the budget to support working families. **But the second Donald Trump wants a new ballroom or gilded decorations and statues in the White House or massive banners with his face, suddenly hundreds of millions of dollars appear.**
This is the backward MAGA agenda: one where working families are pushed aside, and the well-connected get new marble floors. This reckless spending is exactly what voters loudly rejected when they elected a new wave of leadership to Congress.
Peter, Tammy has spent her career fighting exactly this kind of double standard. She helped cap insulin at $35 a month for seniors on Medicare. She's taken on Big Pharma and Wall Street when they've put profits over people.
**Tammy is one of the loudest voices calling out this absurdity, but she can't keep doing it without you.**

Pete Hegseth is going to be impeached.
One way or another, the House is going to vote to impeach the Secretary of Defense. But the Senate may or may not successfully vote to convict him. Doing so would require a two-thirds vote, and even next year would require Republicans to vote for it.

| | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/do-data-centers-drive-up-electricity-costs-part-2?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIxMjM1NDUzLCJpYXQiOjE3OTUwMTExNDMsImV4cCI6MTc5NzYwMzE0MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Uz1pxYPOcYuSK0GAwT9kU6zCS1uKJAH1NprtaeFUjP8&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

Before we got [distracted by the midterm elections](https://substack.com/redirect/2c66cc1f-941e-4b17-8a67-d8ac7a006af9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I'd been writing about data centers, the most prominent new political issue that emerged in this election cycle.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f7e3b249-b530-46b2-a508-6d9018c544f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Do data centers really drain America's water?](https://substack.com/redirect/f7e3b249-b530-46b2-a508-6d9018c544f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 21
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/f7e3b249-b530-46b2-a508-6d9018c544f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When asked to vote on data centers in ballot measures, voters across the U.S. overwhelmingly rejected them. By one count, [46 measures went against data centers](https://substack.com/redirect/1d36e20e-b3e1-485d-8371-a2ba7fd6f237?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); exactly one result favored data center development.
That should tell us something about where public opinion is right now. But how closely does public opinion align with reality?
I'll look specifically at two related topics in this article: the strain data centers are creating on the electrical grid, and the impact they're having on residential utility bills.
> _**Article summary:**_
> * _Data centers are exacerbating a longstanding problem: our electricity infrastructure is dangerously old._
> * _Data centers can drive up electricity bills. There are also real instances of data centers driving those costs down, but that 's dependent on the deals that governments make with data centers. _
> * _States, counties, and municipalities have real negotiating leverage over companies building data centers. They shouldn 't squander that._
>

[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjIxMjM1NDUzLCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzk1MDExMTQzLCJleHAiOjIxMTA1ODcxNDMsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.vaZFB4kpPZQpeSJBf4yZSrDWsAvhmscNwKKxjrxFZpI?)
### What concerns voters most? Should water use really be our top concern?
I used polling data to assess the top six concerns for Americans related to data centers:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a66ec59-f4af-42c4-bbca-4675b8fa57cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [Ipsos](https://substack.com/redirect/247d4546-2f1d-4747-a5c5-7dc5f8509350?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), September 9-10
It turns out that understanding the way data centers use water is _really_ complicated, which is why I [gave it a standalone article](https://substack.com/redirect/f7e3b249-b530-46b2-a508-6d9018c544f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The short answer on data centers' water use: there are real concerns, but data centers consume a tiny, tiny percentage of our water. The concerns are mostly overblown.
But I still had people asking questions about this, so it may be helpful to compare water use by data centers with other things we do in our daily lives.1
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5abc1d45-ca78-45ca-99fc-1989d72aa5db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: see footnote #1
Of course, certain high-level AI queries2 consume much more water than a standard ChatGPT query. But if you're concerned about wasteful water use, data centers are the wrong place to start.
But what about the other concerns?3
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=221235453&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIxMjM1NDUzLCJpYXQiOjE3OTUwMTExNDMsImV4cCI6MTc5NzYwMzE0MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Uz1pxYPOcYuSK0GAwT9kU6zCS1uKJAH1NprtaeFUjP8)
### 2\. Are data centers a strain on the electrical grid?
Let's start with the headline: data centers are already consuming a lot of electricity.
[Estimates](https://substack.com/redirect/02678be2-eaf0-422d-8cf3-fbde7304388a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [vary](https://substack.com/redirect/afb25985-34a9-4e9a-9d24-3bf279d350b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [slightly](https://substack.com/redirect/9dbf5b66-3e81-4294-8bf8-c4f1883fbe9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [on](https://substack.com/redirect/210811f8-aa88-4ab6-9091-d162ccf7ac2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [this](https://substack.com/redirect/9d3d2e1b-fa2d-4235-83a8-b0291e2e135d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but data centers are consuming about 5% of American electricity.4 Like everything related to data centers, this will likely grow.5
By 2030, [the](https://substack.com/redirect/af9f55e9-fd5b-43fa-976f-905218a0660f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [consensus](https://substack.com/redirect/dd4f70c9-72dc-43cb-a999-1b0beaaa30e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [projection](https://substack.com/redirect/fa79fc7a-ddb5-4e15-a059-8adcc58d1b6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is that something like half of increased electricity demand in the U.S. will be attributable to data centers.6 By 2035, they'll account for about [20% of American electricity consumption](https://substack.com/redirect/ddb3c4cb-b058-43c4-8559-25c640e92575?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
But the concern voters have isn't whether they'll be using more electricity--that seems like a certainty. The concern is whether they're a strain on the electrical grid. Those two things are obviously related, but higher energy use doesn't necessarily lead to more strain.7
We as Americans are immensely fortunate in a million ways, not least of which is that our electrical grid is generally extremely reliable. Most of us seldom face blackouts, and short of natural disasters, sustained blackouts are almost unheard of.
But we do face issues. For starters, our infrastructure is really old. In some cases, we're literally [relying](https://substack.com/redirect/5da78362-19a1-4598-89e1-7af41de3be14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [on](https://substack.com/redirect/6c00172f-3a5f-4889-8bdd-21046ffeeac2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [century](https://substack.com/redirect/63e9b374-3711-43a6-ac6e-5cab5bac57d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)-[old](https://substack.com/redirect/b9f1fc99-f2c5-490e-9d99-5ebaaeafea46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [energy](https://substack.com/redirect/9f8bbecb-7502-4e74-bef9-7658c92a3aee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [infrastructure](https://substack.com/redirect/544956fc-a071-49c2-968b-19a18429b97c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Even on average, we're using decades-old infrastructure that's operating [past its intended life](https://substack.com/redirect/f5845bf8-0da6-4f87-8565-7d23845f01be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
All of that matters because sudden increases in energy demand--like, for instance, new data centers--are poised to create strain on a system that in many cases is already past its sell-by date. That's already having a real-world impact.
One study found that counties hosting data centers experienced [6% more power outages and 23% more customers affected by outages](https://substack.com/redirect/9b3b5c83-548b-4204-a00c-fd76776f5309?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) compared to similar counties without data centers.8 Loudoun County, Virginia--a D.C. suburb which [claims the world's largest concentration of data centers](https://substack.com/redirect/bf034e31-b79b-4e7b-8f96-59d6c843258f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--[talks about this strain explicitly](https://substack.com/redirect/2abf785f-4575-411c-a5a3-372012b5be7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).9
Some data centers, either to get ahead of regulatory risk or to reduce reliance on an electrical grid that may not be able to support them in the future, are [building out their own electricity supplies](https://substack.com/redirect/2192bfb4-e392-404c-8ccc-5bd5c94e2c1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). By one estimate, data center projects [representing 25% of proposed U.S. capacity](https://substack.com/redirect/8ed1a56c-a1e3-4060-8303-6ee74c7b226f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) plan to generate their own power on site. I bet [this will become more and more common](https://substack.com/redirect/f8b7280f-aa1b-4080-9eb3-d9e8ff42124b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**Verdict: Data centers are already straining the grid, an issue that will become more acute as America builds more data centers. Regulators may need to compel data centers to generate their own power and/or make investments in the existing grid.**
### 3\. Could data centers lead to higher residential utility bills?
Of all the issues with data centers, this is the most analyzed and the most written about. People will notice higher bills long before they notice issues with water supply or energy infrastructure.
So let's start with the obvious. Energy costs--which include electricity but also transportation fuel--are way up, but that's not because of data centers. It's mostly because of the war in Iran, which has driven up the cost of gasoline:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01bb79ee-f6e6-4ce4-b1d1-753ac520f8ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics ([Midwest](https://substack.com/redirect/d31bfe0a-6601-40f2-b737-0a12803fe4d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Northeast](https://substack.com/redirect/924145d7-2bd2-4c97-9294-4843ab0c96ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [West](https://substack.com/redirect/eb019c3c-e0db-49cb-86a3-62ebf448afa9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [South](https://substack.com/redirect/132d9d96-df7a-49bb-8cab-936d2783b366?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
The distinction between electricity and energy is important. The war in Iran is driving up gasoline costs, but [unlike in Europe](https://substack.com/redirect/830d045b-fa76-4bfe-8972-5f19e1d0183e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it's not really driving up our electricity costs.10
But with electricity rates going up, are data centers responsible? In part, but they're not the primary reason why electricity costs are going up.11
A bunch of different factors are driving up electricity costs, and there's significant regional variance. In the West, wildfires (and wildfire avoidance) have necessitated [expensive investments in aging infrastructure](https://substack.com/redirect/bab860fe-9290-4e43-a388-a2104d19b23d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); the East Coast is experiencing [more frequent severe weather](https://substack.com/redirect/46652a11-5a5f-48ab-a2d4-ae6358e56436?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that is driving up costs, a consequence of climate change.
One MIT study finds that new data center development [leads to a 2.1% increase in residential electricity rates](https://substack.com/redirect/11d1e97d-37e5-4867-b9dd-56a1bfc5659c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is a big deal. But once again, there's a ton of regional variance.
On the one hand, in Ohio, [the typical household pays $15 per month more](https://substack.com/redirect/fba3b348-60d1-4b12-bcc1-1685e396d3bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for electricity because of the state's data centers.12
On the other, there are actually examples of data centers driving _down_ residential electricity bills:
* In Oregon, data centers are charged at a different rate than residential consumers, and as a result, electricity bills for [certain Oregon households](https://substack.com/redirect/d4527778-7901-4e74-8815-c741ebacfa06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)13 have very modestly declined ($1.91 per month).
* In North Dakota, a data center project drove down electricity costs for the customers of [Montana-Dakota Utilities](https://substack.com/redirect/1bbb5387-c1e3-4118-a7d6-092b4d95bada?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by [about $6 per month](https://substack.com/redirect/b1a745bb-51c5-4c71-ac22-88d8a0db81ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Those savings stem from energy credits and regulatory mandates from the [North Dakota Public Service Commission](https://substack.com/redirect/541e4177-e0a5-4c47-ae22-71da4595cdfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

And then there are the in-between cases: [energy companies in Mississippi are claiming](https://substack.com/redirect/79382eb1-6fe8-4390-9820-1961c9347897?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that they're driving down utility bills, but because of statutory confidentiality agreements, [there's no easy way to corroborate that](https://substack.com/redirect/ed76514f-0bcc-4614-a911-f9b668eaa010?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A similar dynamic is playing out in Georgia: [promises of substantial savings](https://substack.com/redirect/e1133474-8e56-4171-9f72-e59e7efc9c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that [can't be corroborated](https://substack.com/redirect/0a706665-925c-408c-b21d-8731d5a62e6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) because of confidentiality agreements.

This is a promise--and a dynamic--that's playing out across the country. Of course everyone likes to promise lower energy bills!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d0a2c5ea-74c4-4963-9e27-f34be5a450d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Source: [Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory](https://substack.com/redirect/15f413ae-44e4-4915-bfcc-d85b170cf884?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Yes, this is motivated by a need for good PR. But it doesn't mean it's wrong, and new data centers--and the energy infrastructure that comes with them--can [avoid rate increases](https://substack.com/redirect/cb8d104f-999b-4e4d-8b6a-6cd7f2e35701?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and potentially even lower rates, if appropriately regulated.
**But that will not happen on its own**. Electricity costs are a life-and-death matter for a lot of lower-income Americans, [especially in hot climates](https://substack.com/redirect/bf3484bf-4430-4bab-90e4-29cd5fc7d851?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and the regulatory framework around new data centers is an essential part of keeping them from driving costs up.
In practice, that can take a lot of different forms:
* Using the taxes generated from data centers as rebates for residential electricity consumers.
* Charging data centers a different per-unit electricity rate than residential consumers.
* Mandating that data centers subsidize new electricity production and/or investments in and upkeep of aging electricity infrastructure.
* Ending the confidentiality agreements that make it impossible to hold data centers, energy companies, and tech companies accountable for their practices and their promises.

There is a viable path here, but it involves smart, thoughtful policy--not empty promises and the limitless construction of data centers.
Last point: [electricity rates are not the same as utility bills](https://substack.com/redirect/22f043fb-95a6-4c0f-8fae-67f4c21fa22a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Even if rates go up, more efficient appliances can mean lower monthly bills, because they consume less energy. What's more, some states that have [low electricity costs have high utility bills](https://substack.com/redirect/27ec966c-b17f-415d-ae68-c43206371ca1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), especially in warmer places where you have to run the air conditioning all summer.14
Focusing on driving down electricity costs on a per-unit basis is important. But the goal is to lower electricity bills, not per-kWh electricity costs. They're related but they're not the same thing.
**Verdict: Without the proper guardrails, data centers likely drive up residential utility bills. But there are real examples of places where that isn 't happening.**
**With the right regulatory framework, states can keep data centers from driving up residential utility bills, and maybe even help bring them down. But that will not happen on its own.**
### A fork in the road for Democratic majorities in Congress
I had aspirations of covering this in one article. That became two, and now it's three. This is a complex topic without easy answers, but I'm not interested in the simple answers.
If nothing else, data centers and AI generally [have a growing PR problem](https://substack.com/redirect/1a93a1da-6502-4205-95a0-1ebc9e3b5b4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one that politicians across the ideological spectrum are happy to exploit. That makes it more important than ever to understand what's really going on.
In Part 3, I'm going to write more about two things:
* Continuing to understand where public concern is justified, and where it's not.
* Understanding what policymakers, at the state and federal level, can and should be doing. What are the concrete policies they should be implementing?

I'll repeat [what I said last time](https://substack.com/redirect/b3a3508a-ba6c-410b-b64a-39eedb10e3c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): AI is here to stay, and if America cares about global competitiveness, we must be making investments in it--and, by extension, data centers.
**Left unchecked, data centers will create real, growing hardships for Americans. But if we block them entirely, we cede technical supremacy to our adversaries abroad. Neither option is acceptable.**
The mandate that swept Democrats into control of Congress wasn't about data centers, but it's a concern for voters and a pressing policy issue. That gives Democrats a choice: continue to amp up fear around data centers for political gain, or do the important and hard work of lawmaking.
I hope they choose the latter.

Crypto mining, for instance, also uses a ton of energy. We can--and should--argue about the applications of AI, but there's clearly some merit and some value. With crypto, it's still unclear what the value really is, and whether energy expenditures this intensive are really worthwhile.
7
More electricity use isn't inherently a bad thing, by the way. A rise in the adoption of electric vehicles would lead to more electricity use, but for a variety of reasons, that'd be a positive development. But you have to make sure that the electricity-generating infrastructure is ready for that.
8
Other studies, including a report from the nonpartisan [Congressional Research Service](https://substack.com/redirect/5d3b7c1e-55a7-4272-aaf0-dea0cceada7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), have said that new data centers haven't caused blackouts yet but rather that they're likely to increase the odds of blackouts going forward. But it's a problem that's either here or about to be here.
By the way: when I [spotted an error in a CRS report](https://substack.com/redirect/dd6acecb-0d01-4302-b578-4b6f669faa98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in my last data center article, I emailed them and they were quick to correct it. I trust their work, and the fact that they corrected the error so quickly speaks to their professionalism.
9
What they say [on the county website](https://substack.com/redirect/2abf785f-4575-411c-a5a3-372012b5be7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> Large concentrations of data centers, like those in Loudoun County, heighten the demand for electricity and can contribute to concerns about grid reliability across the region. In northern Virginia, the regional power grid has become strained in large part due to increased electrical demand from data centers over the past 20 plus years. PJM, the SCC and the utilities serving Loudoun County are charged with planning for the long-term reliability of power and are working to address concerns about grid reliability by proposing new high-voltage transmission lines in, around and through the county to address local and regional demand.
10
On an inflation-adjusted basis, electricity prices have risen over the last 25 years, but [not by much](https://substack.com/redirect/802cf1b0-6722-4efc-a48d-16e32fa1add8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
11
This chart is one illustration of that:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bc45e78f-26a4-4fb9-a48f-fdfd75e7d545?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [USAFacts](https://substack.com/redirect/802cf1b0-6722-4efc-a48d-16e32fa1add8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's not like states that have the most data centers necessarily have the largest electricity price increases. But this doesn't tell us that data centers have no impact; it just tells us that there are other factors that go into electricity costs, not just the presence (or absence) of data centers.
12
There's a reason this was [such a big issue](https://substack.com/redirect/6b9587dc-49a3-4a05-89f2-bf5e68de7a69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the [Ohio U.S. Senate election](https://substack.com/redirect/cc278500-5acb-41d0-9aec-636c783bb4d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Given the magnitude of Democratic wins, it may not have been the difference-maker for Sherrod Brown, but it certainly didn't hurt.
That same _New York Times_ article [references a projection](https://substack.com/redirect/fba3b348-60d1-4b12-bcc1-1685e396d3bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that by 2030, data centers and cryptocurrency mining could drive up electricity generation costs by more than 25% in parts of Virginia. Those projections are invariably going to change over the coming months and years, but it's nonetheless a big increase.
Virginia announced a year ago that a typical household consumer would pay [$11 more per month](https://substack.com/redirect/0eba577c-f100-43c1-a0b6-9ffbda3f3a62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2026, though again, that's not entirely attributable to data centers.
13
Specifically, for customers of [Portland General Electric](https://substack.com/redirect/4cf200f0-12c8-4726-8a6e-bad66df210fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
14
It might be a worthwhile experiment to see if tax revenues from data centers could be used to subsidize more efficient in-home appliances as a way to drive down utility bills. I'm not sure if that's been tried or researched at all.

* **White Front Pocket T-Shirt ($34):** 100% pre-shrunk American cotton with left chest pocket print and full back artwork.
* **White Crewneck Fleece Sweatshirt ($45):** Heavy-weight, pre-shrunk fleece crafted for Montana winters.
* **White Mesh Trucker Hat ($27):** Premium 6-panel structured snapback.
* **Lapel Sticker 9-Pack ($11):** High-gloss white paper stickers featuring the emblem.

Whether you wear your gear around town, to local precinct meetings, or as an add-on to your Statesmen's Ball ticket order, it shows the world that you stand for freedom. We only produced a limited run of this collection. Visit our official storefront now to claim your gear before sizes sell out!

#### From Our Partners
## **Democrats Control Congress. What It Means for Your Savings.**
The votes were counted. It was a landslide.
Democrats won control of the House and the Senate.
Here is what that means.
**Starting in January, every bill, judge, and cabinet member the President wants has to pass a Congress controlled by the other party.**
That door has shut.
President Trump's signature tax and spending bill passed with his own party's votes alone.
That window has closed.
What comes next is a standoff. Congress can send the President bills he will not like and will veto. And nothing moves.
**That is what J.P. Morgan calls "a period of policy gridlock."**
The last time a sitting president lost both chambers in a midterm was 2006.
In 2007, the new majority opened investigation after investigation into the White House, from the firing of US attorneys to the conduct of the war.
**And the first test comes fast.**
The funding deadline is coming on December 11. A government shutdown is not theoretical
Now look at your own savings.
Your 401k, your IRA, your bank account. All of them are held in dollars, inside a government now split in two and headed for gridlock.
Gold has its own record. The last time a sitting president lost both chambers in a midterm, [gold's price rose the following year](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/839ae693-6cc7-4d30-bdaf-8fcc77027324?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
You could not choose the outcome of the elections.
You can choose what you hold.
More than 60 million Americans qualify to move a portion of their savings into physical gold. Tax-free. Penalty-free.

#### The Cautious Shopper
## **The American shopper just blinked, and that counts for more than any earnings report**
_October was the first month in a while that spending stalled. Measured against prices, it slipped. Heading into the holidays, that is the number worth watching._
The steadiest engine in this economy is the American wallet, and in October it eased off the gas. Retail sales rose just 0.2 percent, down from a strong 0.8 percent in September, as shoppers [pulled back on everything from cars to clothing](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9bdeec04-9e0a-43c7-8443-24c56e4008ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Strip out gasoline and the gain was almost nothing. Because prices climbed faster than spending did, Americans actually bought a little less last month than the month before. The timing stings, with the holidays and their bigger bills only weeks away.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7b938d94-f75c-44c5-a7d8-95b2d180f71d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The report landed with a line that should give any household pause. "The cautious consumer is back," wrote one economist who [watches these numbers](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9bdeec04-9e0a-43c7-8443-24c56e4008ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) closely.
The strain is not spread evenly. Gas is cheaper than a month ago, which frees up a little cash, yet a gallon still costs nearly a fifth more than it did a year ago. Autos, furniture, and clothing all slipped as families trimmed the bigger, more optional buys, while the one clear bright spot was online shopping, lifted by an early Amazon sale. What the data describes is not a consumer in trouble. It is a consumer being careful, counting dollars before the most expensive month of the year.
I read a report like this as a caution light, not a crash. People are still working and still spending. They are just doing it with one eye on the price tag.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e384299b-5e56-4a86-8ea1-4213972d6620?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### The Test Comes Back
## **While shoppers hesitated, the market 's biggest question got answered after the bell**
For four days Wall Street sold first and asked later, bracing for one report. After Tuesday's close it arrived, and the company the whole artificial-intelligence trade leans on delivered. The quarter would either calm the week's nerves or deepen them.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2ca624cb-c09d-430f-8e71-2d8bb1d51621?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
▪ Nvidia posted revenue of about $115.8 billion for the quarter, up 103 percent from a year ago and well past what analysts expected, with a [beat on the top and bottom lines](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3fce4523-1090-4f8f-995e-8e86adb631ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and profit of $2.68 a share.
▪ The company guided to roughly $130 billion in sales for the current quarter, above forecasts, and told investors that demand for its next generation of chips is still climbing.
▪ It also announced a $150 billion plan to buy back its own stock, an unusual show of confidence from a company that lost its founding chief executive only days earlier.
▪ The stock, which had slipped during a brutal session, rose about 3 percent in after-hours trading, a first sign the AI selloff that rattled the market all month may be finding a floor.
One quarter does not undo a correction. But after four straight losing sessions and a market desperate for a reason to stop selling, the most-watched number on Wall Street came back strong, and that is a steadier note to end on than the day began.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5135d86e-4c3b-4cd6-86c1-f8efd4053f32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### One Number
**$1.17 trillion** is what Americans now owe on their credit cards, an all-time high and about 5 percent more than a year ago, by [one credit bureau's count](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9bdeec04-9e0a-43c7-8443-24c56e4008ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The reassuring part is that most people are keeping up, as serious late payments have held steady. The catch is that more of this holiday season is going onto cards that carry some of the steepest interest around, and that bill does not land until January.
#### Why I Led Here
I led with the shopper, not the chip, because the health of the American consumer is the ground this whole economy stands on. Roughly two thirds of it is simply people buying things, so when they start to hesitate, that tells me more than any one company's results, however big the headline.
What I watch is the pattern under a single soft month, and the pattern is a careful consumer, not a broken one. People are still working, still spending, just leaning a little harder on credit and waiting for the sale. The stretch from now to New Year will show which way it tips, and I will be reading the receipts, not the rhetoric.

To set up your profile and discover more on Substack, . | | ---|---|--- From Our Partners Democrats Control Congress. What It Means for Your Savings. The votes were counted. It was a landslide. Democrats won control of the House and the Senate. Here is what that means. Starting in January, every bill, judge, and cabinet member the President wants has to pass a Congress controlled by the other party. That door has shut. President Trump's signature tax and spending bill passed with his own party's votes alone. That window has closed. What comes next is a standoff. Congress can send the President bills he will not like and will veto. And nothing moves. That is what J.P. Morgan calls "a period of policy gridlock." The last time a sitting president lost both chambers in a midterm was 2006. In 2007, the new majority opened investigation after investigation into the White House, from the firing of US attorneys to the conduct of the war. And the first test comes fast. The funding deadline is coming on December 11. A government shutdown is not theoretical Now look at your own savings. Your 401k, your IRA, your bank account. Your savings do not have to be caught in the middle. | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- The Cautious Shopper The American shopper just blinked, and that counts for more than any earnings report October was the first month in a while that spending stalled. Measured against prices, it slipped. Heading into the holidays, that is the number worth watching. The steadiest engine in this economy is the American wallet, and in October it eased off the gas. Retail sales rose just 0.2 percent, down from a strong 0.8 percent in September, as shoppers . Strip out gasoline and the gain was almost nothing. Because prices climbed faster than spending did, Americans actually bought a little less last month than the month before. The timing stings, with the holidays and their bigger bills only weeks away. | | ---|---|--- The report landed with a line that should give any household pause. "The cautious consumer is back," wrote one economist who closely. The strain is not spread evenly. Gas is cheaper than a month ago, which frees up a little cash, yet a gallon still costs nearly a fifth more than it did a year ago. Autos, furniture, and clothing all slipped as families trimmed the bigger, more optional buys, while the one clear bright spot was online shopping, lifted by an early Amazon sale. What the data describes is not a consumer in trouble. It is a consumer being careful, counting dollars before the most expensive month of the year. I read a report like this as a caution light, not a crash. People are still working and still spending. subject: A majority is a start, not a finish line
body:

Peter,

For the last two years, Trump and his MAGA allies have dragged this
country backward, handing giveaways to billionaires, attacking rights our
communities fought for, and rolling back decades of progress.

But Democrats have the majority now. The Squad is back in Congress, and we
have a real chance to fix the damage.

Here’s the thing: a majority on its own doesn’t guarantee change.
Washington is full of politicians who’d rather protect the status quo than
take on corporate power. If this majority is going to deliver for working
families, we need fearless champions inside the halls of power and a
movement behind them pushing for bold progressive change.

Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida are exactly those leaders, and the
Squad Victory Fund exists to have their backs and build the movement
behind them.

We believe every person deserves dignity, opportunity, and a voice in our
collective future. That means childcare parents can afford, housing that
lets families put down roots, and healthcare that’s there for everyone who
needs it. And it means a government that answers to the people, not the
ultra-wealthy who’ve had their way for too long.

None of this will come easy. Trump, the MAGA machine, and their
deep-pocketed allies will fight us every step of the way and work to
silence our movement. We won’t let that happen.

The Squad Victory Fund doesn’t take a dime from corporate PACs. We’re
powered by grassroots supporters like you, and that’s what keeps us
accountable to the people and keeps us in this fight.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: My role as Immigration Chair
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261118-6969-footer&t=1001&akid=6969%2E420207%2E0Pi09b ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

At 16 years old, I came to this country alone and scared. I was far from
home and unsure what my future would hold.

It took me 17 years to get my citizenship.

That long and difficult process came with an alphabet soup of visas and
several degrees — and it’s the reality for so many immigrants trying to
build a life here. And now, with the Trump Administration’s cruel attacks
on immigration, the process to obtain citizenship has only become longer
and more difficult.

But all that is about to change. Congress is back in Democratic hands.
Come January, I will be the chair of the committee that shapes whether we
treat immigrants with cruelty or humanity.

And I’m the first immigrant to ever hold this position.

The officials who kidnapped our neighbors? Who illegally detained and
deported children? Who killed people in our streets? I’m going to drag
every one of them before that committee, and we are going to send them to
prison. We are going to restore kindness and humanity to our immigration
system.

The moment I pick up that gavel, Trump’s allies will come after me harder
than ever. They’ll make me a warning to every other progressive who dares
to take on power like this.

I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs or have billionaires on speed
dial. The only thing standing between me and their attacks is a movement
like ours. And with your help,
Peter, we can show that people
power and compassion are stronger than money and cruelty.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261118-1.XYhMWD&refcode=em20261118-6969&amount=3&t=1002&akid=6969%2E420207%2E0Pi09b ]Trump and his MAGA allies will be coming at us with everything they
have. Can you chip in $3 or anything you can to help us
prepare for these attacks and ensure we’re restoring humanity and kindness
to our immigration system?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261118-1.XYhMWD&amount=3&refcode=em20261118-6969&t=1021&akid=6969%2E420207%2E0Pi09b ]Contribute $3

We’ve never been in a better position to lead the way to substantive
change for immigration reform. Now’s our chance to act, and we can’t let
anything get in our way.

Thank you for being in this fight with me,
Peter.

In solidarity,

Pramila Jayapal
