**November 18, 2026**
Licking the dew from leaves as a child is perhaps a memory shared by many. I think of it when I walk into the field in the morning and bring back a few pieces of fruit for breakfast. The beads catch the morning light, and I sometimes feel a tenderness at the thought of having plucked the fruit, as though I have taken the dew from its mission. I do not lick the dew anymore, but sometimes I am tempted.
Water gathers as dew and nourishes the land. We also direct its movement through canals, drainage networks, and other systems of our making. A Florida DEP notice reports that U.S. Sugar discharged an estimated 440 million gallons of stormwater over ten days into the Clewiston District drainage system.
The dewdrops are measured in beads of morning light. The discharge is measured in millions of gallons.
Both invite us to consider something we can easily overlook: water has an origin, a place, and a purpose before we decide what to do with it.
We have become very good at measuring water, moving water, and managing water. But how well do we understand what has been entrusted to our care?
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

clean_body: Before it is measured, there is wonder. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Before it is measured, there is wonder. | | | Nov 18 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- November 18, 2026 Licking the dew from leaves as a child is perhaps a memory shared by many. I think of it when I walk into the field in the morning and bring back a few pieces of fruit for breakfast. The beads catch the morning light, and I sometimes feel a tenderness at the thought of having plucked the fruit, as though I have taken the dew from its mission. I do not lick the dew anymore, but sometimes I am tempted. Water gathers as dew and nourishes the land. We also direct its movement through canals, drainage networks, and other systems of our making. A Florida DEP notice reports that U.S. Sugar discharged an estimated 440 million gallons of stormwater over ten days into the Clewiston District drainage system. The dewdrops are measured in beads of morning light. The discharge is measured in millions of gallons. Both invite us to consider something we can easily overlook: water has an origin, a place, and a purpose before we decide what to do with it. We have become very good at measuring water, moving water, and managing water. But how well do we understand what has been entrusted to our care? Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper. Refuel. Now he’s throwing a full-blown temper tantrum on Truth Social, accusing me and my Democratic colleagues of "extortion" and ordering his Attorney General to investigate us.
[](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019A-HlL92tAcoJxyT0AKcfFNmnxieTzrdg51oMrsSDnpHeicxgqiqzpIIKqql42x67oKtldKtEcROthrKVTyENmJ09hmGkVLpUIXP595IjfnBpDeP2HtIwo0Plc-xhxVG2uM6O-TsxHURixKIseziwUtyaRrrbM3nWakPnNAYD-oqRL_1Q4sfh5U0eaVq3U7TaK9vP3h5yi1m246sFyB_1Z63hSgzThC_hjtLINzY8Qcrz9RvpwKNOQ==&c=Lg2or7BplUrXFByA1vkzuke9lYH7220u56Q86eQzRlqJSeHSVtYYXw==&ch=Ye78trRDPL9vJzxrNmy04uLTK1Jj7jc-nb_y8LAn0bDX6fbjamN9GA==)

He spent years turning the White House into a personal piggy bank, taking pay-to-play ballroom donations, watching Jared Kushner rake in hundreds of millions from foreign powers, and ignoring human rights abuses at our border. He thought he would never have to answer to anyone.
**Then the American voters delivered an absolute rout, swept Democrats into the majority, and handed us the gavel.**
**_Now that constitutional oversight is coming for him, he claims holding corrupt politicians accountable is "illegal"._**
Hear me loud and clear: Demanding accountability is not extortion. It is our constitutional duty.
Trump can try to weaponize the Department of Justice. He can order his Attorney General to issue threats. _But I will never be intimidated by a rattled bully._
The days of uncontained corruption end the moment I take the chair. We are opening the books on the Trump administration, exposing the pay-offs, and bringing the Epstein files into the light of day.
[Trump is weaponizing every weapon he has left to slow us down. To build the strongest movement in history, I need you on the front lines right now. Chip in $5, $15, or $25 right now to show Donald Trump that we aren’t backing down—and that no one is above the law.](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019A-HlL92tAcoJxyT0AKcfFNmnxieTzrdg51oMrsSDnpHeicxgqiqzpIIKqql42x67oKtldKtEcROthrKVTyENmJ09hmGkVLpUIXP595IjfnBpDeP2HtIwo0Plc-xhxVG2uM6O-TsxHURixKIseziwUtyaRrrbM3nWakPnNAYD-oqRL_1Q4sfh5U0eaVq3U7TaK9vP3h5yi1m246sFyB_1Z63hSgzThC_hjtLINzY8Qd4mKzoZWCEXA==&c=Lg2or7BplUrXFByA1vkzuke9lYH7220u56Q86eQzRlqJSeHSVtYYXw==&ch=Ye78trRDPL9vJzxrNmy04uLTK1Jj7jc-nb_y8LAn0bDX6fbjamN9GA==)

In principle, yes -- election fraud is always possible. The real question is whether the data being circulated proves it. This week, a set of statistics has gone viral arguing that James Talarico's win over Ken Paxton was _statistically_ impossible. The numbers are real. The interpretation, in almost every case, _is not_. When you measure them against the right baselines, the "impossible" dissolves -- and what's left is a genuine scandal, _just not the one people think_.
**The Headline Swings Are Real -- But Measured Against the Wrong Baseline**
The most repeated claim is that Texas went from Trump +13.7 in 2024 to Talarico +12.1 in 2026 -- a 25.8-point shift that "can't happen in a midterm."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/13e0277e-d8d8-44e6-9860-89400d6880f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The problem: a presidential race is not the correct baseline for a Senate race. The last Senate race in Texas was Ted Cruz vs. Colin Allred in 2024, which Cruz won by +8.6. Against _that_ baseline, Talarico's win represents a roughly 21-point Senate-to-Senate swing. That is enormous -- likely the largest in modern Texas history -- but it is a different animal from "impossible," and Texas has seen swings in that neighborhood before. Between 2000 and 2002, the Senate margin moved roughly 17 points against the GOP after Kay Bailey Hutchison's blowout. Large candidate-driven and environment-driven swings between consecutive Senate races are a real feature of American elections.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/afa9c172-21f7-4332-a0f3-c145240dc189?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now consider the "28 counties flipped" claim, including Tarrant, Collin, Denton, Williamson and Hidalgo. Two of those five didn't actually flip at the Senate level. Per the certified 2024 counts:
\- Allred already carried Tarrant (+0.15)
\- Allred already carried Williamson (+1.46)
\- Allred carried Hidalgo by +6.6
The flip list only works if you compare to the presidential race. That comparison inflates the shift.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cc412365-88e2-49f9-9e5b-08cc3e300ea6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And what about "every one of 254 counties moved toward Democrats" and "none flipped the other way"? These are not fingerprints of tampering. They are mechanical properties of a large uniform swing. Real ballot stuffing is geographically lumpy -- it surfaces as statistical outliers, precincts where vote counts exceed all plausible bounds. A flat 15-to-25-point shift across every county, including ones run by GOP election officials in Collin and Denton, is what a national wave combined with a uniquely polarizing nominee produces. Uniformity is evidence of a uniform cause.
**The Border Numbers Dissolve Against 2018**
The most dramatic claim: Starr County moved 71.8 points, Zapata 63.1, Maverick 59.5. "Impossible to have swings that big during a Midterms."
The Starr figure checks out arithmetically -- Talarico +55.8 (13,082 votes) against Trump's 2024 +16 margin is your 71.8. But decompose it against the right benchmarks:
\- Against Cruz's 2024 margin in Starr (+2.2: Cruz 49.84%, Allred 47.64%), the swing is about 58 points.
\- Against Beto O'Rourke's 2018 result in Starr (roughly 86%, about +72), Talarico ran roughly 16 points below the Democratic ceiling. Starr's biggest Democratic margin in modern history belongs to 2018, not 2026. If ballots were being fabricated in Starr, the Democratic share would blow past the 2018 ceiling -- instead it sits below it.
The same pattern holds down the Valley:
\- Cameron: Talarico +38.5 versus Allred's +4.3 in 2024
\- Hidalgo: Talarico +46.5 versus Allred's +6.6 in 2024
More importantly, turnout held. Hidalgo cast 202,520 Senate votes in 2026 versus 211,090 in the presidential year, and the Texas Tribune reported that South Texas early voting *exceeded* 2024 levels. A stuffing signature is inflated vote counts in targeted precincts. A reversion signature is turnout staying high while margins return to pre-2024 norms. The data show the latter.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b3d1a64f-08a1-4d03-ada0-e79fc448ff32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There's also a scale problem. Starr's entire 2026 vote is 13,082 ballots. Every border county combined is a rounding error in a roughly 10-million-vote statewide race. Whatever happened there moved the statewide margin by a fraction of a point. This election was decided in Harris, Dallas, Tarrant, Collin and the suburbs -- where the Houston Chronicle found Paxton's margins falling 10+ points versus both Cruz 2018 and Trump 2024 in Montgomery, Waller, Liberty and Brazoria.
**The Administrative Items Are Real -- And They Cut the Other Way**
The viral list includes several administrative facts. They are genuine. None of them demonstrates fraud, and most point in the opposite direction.
"2.9M registrations without citizenship verification." This describes how every state registers voters under federal motor-voter/NVRA law -- attestation under penalty of perjury, not documentary proof, for federal elections. Registration is not a ballot: Texas requires photo ID at the polls and per-county ballot reconciliation. Texas Newsroom fact checks (KERA, Houston Public Media) examined these viral registration claims this week and concluded the cited federal data do not demonstrate fraud. And the government that administered those rolls from 2022 to 2024 -- with four years to purge phantoms -- was Republican.
The 500K DPS portal error is real. The TEAM registration system malfunctioned, and the Secretary of State has ordered an audit of it (per the Tribune/Votebeat). But read it correctly: roughly 500,000 lawful applicants were left off the rolls, and the state cleared the backlog before the deadline. That is under-registration repaired -- the opposite of stuffing. It is also a self-inflicted GOP administrative scandal about disenfranchisement risk, not fraud.
15,000 address updates four days out. Statutory cutoff-day processing. An address update creates zero votes.
1.76M voters on the suspense list. Texas's own list-maintenance category, years old. Those voters can still vote with ID, and their ballots are reconciled against ballots issued.
97 counties with more registrations than adult citizens. A long-standing artifact of stale rolls plus Census ACS survey estimates. Even if true, extra registrations cannot produce extra ballots where ballot accounting is enforced.
**The Vote-Record Talking Point Proves the Wrong Thing**
"Talarico got more votes than any Democrat presidential candidate, more than any Republican governor, more than any Republican presidential nominee except Trump."
This is a statement about _record turnout_ -- CBS reported record midterm ballots in Dallas, Tarrant and Collin -- plus population growth, plus a sweep so complete that Gina Hinojosa beat an incumbent governor. Fabricated ballots show up as turnout spikes in specific precincts, not record turnout across both coalitions' home turf simultaneously.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/46142c69-ce98-4d22-b802-177e30e28803?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Yes, Talarico beat his final polls (CNN +6, NYT +7) by roughly five points. Results exceeding final polls by that margin happens, especially with an unconventional candidate, an opponent under multiple legal clouds, and record engagement. It is not, by itself, an anomaly indicator.
**So -- Could Ballot Stuffing Have Taken Place?**
To flip a 12-point margin on roughly 10 million votes, you need on the order of **600,000** net fabricated ballots. The fingerprints that would betray them are all public or auditable: precinct turnout exceeding plausible bounds, votes-cast-versus-ballots-issued reconciliation failures, duplicate and dead-registration hits, machine logs.
What has actually surfaced in 2026:
\- Paxton's own Attorney General's office announced a handful of individual felon-voting arrests
\- The FBI debunked the "20,000 ballots in a Houston storage locker" post
\- Lead Stories found no "30,000 fraud investigation" exists
\- AFP traced the viral 91.9% graphic to a data-entry error corrected on air
\- The Republican Secretary of State has already ordered the TEAM audit
Nothing in the dataset cited rises above administrative noise, and several pieces of it -- the 2018 border benchmarks, the Tarrant and Williamson 2024 results, the uniformity of the shift, the turnout patterns -- affirmatively cut against the stuffing hypothesis.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6af2e92a-48a2-49d8-b9a3-03ba227225b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But the fair version of the instinct survives. A 21-point Senate-to-Senate swing in the most expensive Senate campaign ever run deserves mechanical verification, not vibes. The audit worth demanding is specific:
1\. County-by-county ballot reconciliation reports
2\. A manual/risk-limiting audit of the Senate race in a random sample of precincts, plus Starr, Hidalgo, Cameron and Collin
3\. Precinct-level turnout forensics on the published returns
4\. Release of the TEAM system audit
If those come back clean, the verdict is that 2024 was the anomaly on the border, not 2026 -- and Paxton was the anomaly everywhere else.
And that points to the real scandal hiding in this list. _The genuine failure here is the state GOP 's own registration software silently discarding half a million lawful applications._ The one provable disenfranchisement event of the 2026 cycle was self-inflicted. If the right wants a coherent election-integrity story, it starts with fixing the machine that lost the registrations -- not with numbers that fall apart the moment you measure them against the right baseline.

The last Senate race in Texas was Ted Cruz vs. Colin Allred in 2024, which Cruz won by +8.6. Against that baseline, Talarico's win represents a roughly 21-point Senate-to-Senate swing. That is enormous -- likely the largest in modern Texas history -- but it is a different animal from "impossible," and Texas has seen swings in that neighborhood before. Between 2000 and 2002, the Senate margin moved roughly 17 points against the GOP after Kay Bailey Hutchison's blowout. Large candidate-driven and environment-driven swings between consecutive Senate races are a real feature of American elections. | | ---|---|--- Now consider the "28 counties flipped" claim, including Tarrant, Collin, Denton, Williamson and Hidalgo. Two of those five didn't actually flip at the Senate level. Per the certified 2024 counts: \- Allred already carried Tarrant (+0.15) \- Allred already carried Williamson (+1.46) \- Allred carried Hidalgo by +6.6 The flip list only works if you compare to the presidential race. That comparison inflates the shift. | | ---|---|--- And what about "every one of 254 counties moved toward Democrats" and "none flipped the other way"? These are not fingerprints of tampering. They are mechanical properties of a large uniform swing. Real ballot stuffing is geographically lumpy -- it surfaces as statistical outliers, precincts where vote counts exceed all plausible bounds. Friend, Yesterday, I told you we had a _big announcement_ coming.**Today,_I’m proud to share it with you first:_** **I am officially running for _Tennessee Senate District 31_ in the upcoming special election.** On the heels of our historic run for Governor— _the closest Tennessee gubernatorial race in more than a century_ — _**our fight is far from over.**_ With _six legislative seats flipped_ across the state and _the strongest Democratic showing_ in decades, **_the mandate is clear:_** __**Tennesseans are ready for change.**__ With Senator Brent Taylor _resigning_ to assume his seat in Congress, _**a special election is expected in early 2027**_ —giving our community an immediate, _once-in-a-generation_ opportunity to _flip this seat_ , chip away at one-party rule, and _take on the entrenched corruption in Nashville._ _**We know how to win. **_Our campaign will be built on a proven record of expanding competitive reach right here in Shelby County. In my first run for office in House District 83, w _hich makes up a portion of Senate District 31,_ we built a grassroots operation that _captured 47 percent of the vote_ and put a longtime GOP stronghold _firmly in play._ Then on November 3rd, _we scaled that coalition across the entire Senate district_ , capturing _45 percent_ of the vote and demonstrating that _**Senate District 31 is squarely within reach for a Democratic win for the first time in 50 years**._ I am also honored to have the partnership and endorsement of former Democratic nominee _**David Weatherspoon**_ — _whom I am proud to support for the interim appointment ahead of the special election_ —as _we unite our community to deliver l_** _ower everyday costs, affordable healthcare, and fully funded public schools for working families. _** _**And make no mistake: I plan to take the fight to the supermajority and Marsha Blackburn while I serve as Senator, and again in four years.**_ **Special elections move fast— _and our Day One momentum starts right now._** To build a winning field operation in Shelby County from day one, we need to hit the ground running immediately. clean_body: | Friend, Yesterday, I told you we had a big announcement coming.Today,I’m proud to share it with you first: I am officially running for Tennessee Senate District 31 in the upcoming special election. On the heels of our historic run for Governor— the closest Tennessee gubernatorial race in more than a century — our fight is far from over. With six legislative seats flipped across the state and the strongest Democratic showing in decades, the mandate is clear: Tennesseans are ready for change. With Senator Brent Taylor resigning to assume his seat in Congress, a special election is expected in early 2027 —giving our community an immediate, once-in-a-generation opportunity to flip this seat , chip away at one-party rule, and take on the entrenched corruption in Nashville. We know how to win. Our campaign will be built on a proven record of expanding competitive reach right here in Shelby County. In my first run for office in House District 83, w hich makes up a portion of Senate District 31, we built a grassroots operation that captured 47 percent of the vote and put a longtime GOP stronghold firmly in play. Then on November 3rd, we scaled that coalition across the entire Senate district , capturing 45 percent of the vote and demonstrating that Senate District 31 is squarely within reach for a Democratic win for the first time in 50 years. I am also honored to have the partnership and endorsement of former Democratic nominee David Weatherspoon — whom I am proud to support for the interim appointment ahead of the special election —as we unite our community to deliver l ower everyday costs, affordable healthcare, and fully funded public schools for working families. And make no mistake: I plan to take the fight to the supermajority and Marsha Blackburn while I serve as Senator, and again in four years. Special elections move fast— and our Day One momentum starts right now. With Democrats holding a supermajority in Hartford, Governor Ned Lamont's request for resignations from his commissioners presents an interesting opportunity: bringing Republicans into an administration where meaningful political opposition in the legislature is increasingly limited.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..U84FbunRjG5PBrPMxn4rbkonWFM9LKzTIia103SKoMc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=225519227)

Frankly, appointing Republicans to executive positions may be one of the few practical ways to introduce some political balance into Connecticut's government over the next four years.
And Lamont has done it before.
In 2020, he appointed former Republican gubernatorial candidate and longtime Danbury Mayor Mark Boughton as commissioner of the Department of Revenue Services. Boughton had challenged the Democratic establishment, yet Lamont recognized his experience and brought him into the administration.
**Could history repeat itself with Ryan Fazio?**
Fazio, Lamont's Republican challenger in 2026, has been outspoken about Connecticut's high energy costs, taxes, economic stagnation and affordability.
_**Let 's be realistic. Lamont is hardly going to put Fazio in charge of energy policy, given their fundamental disagreements over Connecticut's energy direction.**_
But economic development? That is a different conversation.
Fazio's background in finance, private-sector experience and legislative work could bring a different perspective to the Department of Economic and Community Development, particularly when Connecticut continues to struggle with business competitiveness, economic growth and the departure of residents and capital.
Of course, there is no indication that either Lamont or Fazio is considering such an appointment.
But with Republicans holding only a small minority of legislative seats, the governor has an opportunity to bring opposing perspectives directly into the executive branch.
And there may even be a political advantage for Lamont.
**At the very least, it would give the governor a few Republican scapegoats when things go wrong.**
After all, when Democrats control the governor's office and enjoy overwhelming legislative majorities, it becomes increasingly difficult to blame Republicans for Connecticut's problems.
Put a few Republicans in charge of agencies, however, and suddenly there are members of the opposing party sharing responsibility for the administration's performance.
That may sound cynical, but politics has always involved sharing both credit and blame.
The more serious opportunity is to bring different ideas into the administration, especially on economic development, fiscal management and government efficiency.
Commissioners ultimately answer to the governor, so Republican appointments would not create an independent check on executive power. But they could provide an additional voice in policy discussions that might otherwise take place almost entirely within one party.
The Boughton appointment demonstrated that Lamont is willing to cross party lines when he sees value in doing so.
Now, entering his third term, he has an opportunity to do it again.
**If Connecticut 's legislative supermajority leaves little room for political balance in Hartford, perhaps the governor can create some within his own administration.**
And if nothing else, he'll finally have a few Republicans around to blame.

body:
We want to make sure we hear your thoughts on next year’s Member Card design! [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10349%2E22930333%2EIVmHCo)
---
Derek, **2027 DNC Member Cards are almost here! But before we start printing and mailing them (you can reserve yours[**here**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-membercard.1omOxh&refcode=em_20261118_10349_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10349%2E22930333%2EIVmHCo)), we want to make sure we have your input on which design you like the best.** Whether you’ve chipped in this year, volunteered your time and energy to help elect Democrats, or just been keeping up to date with the DNC’s work to elect Democrats up and down the ballot, _we’re grateful to have you on our team_. Our 2027 DNC Member Cards will be an important reminder of your integral role on our grassroots team, and of the work we have ahead of us in the upcoming two years. With the 2026 midterms in the rearview, we’re beginning to look ahead. **First order of business: Choosing a design for our 2027 Member Cards.** [**This is what we have on file for you right now, can you confirm that it’s accurate?**](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261118_10349_fr&t=7&akid=10349%2E22930333%2EIVmHCo) **_2027 DNC Member Card Voting Record**_ **NAME:** Derek Willis
**2027 MEMBER CARD VOTER:** NO, NOT YET ❌
**SUGGESTED ACTION:** VOTE ON YOUR FAVORITE DESIGN **[VOTE NOW](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261118_10349_fr&t=10&akid=10349%2E22930333%2EIVmHCo)** None of the major victories that Democrats won this year — from Democrats flipping the House and Senate to winning down-ballot races across the country — would’ve been possible without the help of our generous grassroots supporters. We’re so excited to share these Member Cards with you as a reminder that we can win _big_ when we all stand together. [**Please take a few seconds to share your thoughts on which design you’d like to see on your Member Card today >>](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261118_10349_fr&t=12&akid=10349%2E22930333%2EIVmHCo)** **[VOTE NOW](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261118_10349_fr&t=15&akid=10349%2E22930333%2EIVmHCo)** Thank you, The Democrats

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

# **Mamdani names new leftist judges, reappoints controversial "Judge Let-em-Go"**
Mayor Zohran Mamdani appointed 10 new city and family court judges, **[most of them far-left ideologues](https://substack.com/redirect/2bdfe7a7-1979-4236-8f8d-5dcc8f51e742?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and at least six with public defender backgrounds, and reappointed six others, including Manhattan Judge Valentina Morales, nicknamed "Judge Let-em-Go" for repeatedly releasing violent offenders without bail.

* **Mamdani defended the selections as meeting "the highest standards of fairness, integrity and accountability,"** with all nominees vetted by the Mayor's Advisory Committee on the Judiciary ahead of a scheduled public hearing Tuesday.
* **This after Mamdani disbanded the NYPD 's Strategic Response Group**, a special unit that handles violent protests in the city, and replaced them with an unarmed civilian-led alternative unit.

Queens Judge Jennifer Saint-Preux, also reappointed, similarly declined to hold a suspect with nearly 150 prior arrests without bail. Mamdani defended the selections as meeting "the highest standards of fairness, integrity and accountability," with all nominees vetted by the Mayor's Advisory Committee on the Judiciary ahead of a scheduled public hearing Tuesday. This after Mamdani disbanded the NYPD 's Strategic Response Group, a special unit that handles violent protests in the city, and replaced them with an unarmed civilian-led alternative unit. Randy George, to permanently lead the service, sending the nomination to the Senate Armed Services Committee this week. LaNeve, a former senior aide to Hegseth confirmed as vice chief in January, has authored blunt strategic guidance documents like "The Army Azimuth" and "How the Army Fights," emphasizing lethality, discipline, and preparing for high-intensity conflicts against adversaries like Russia or China. The 36-year infantry veteran has commanded major units including the 82nd Airborne Division and Eighth Army in Korea. The White House also nominated Lt. Gen. Marcus Evans to replace him as vice chief, with confirmation efforts facing a tight timeline before Democrats take Senate control in January. body:
Bless their hearts.

[Katie Britt for Alabama]
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

Friend,

They said I’d never make it. That I should stay quiet, sit still,
and stop trying.

But I’ve never been interested in playing by anybody’s rules but
my own.

I’m Katie Britt. A Christian, a conservative, a mom of two, and the
youngest Republican woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate. I didn’t
run for office to win popularity points. I ran to fight for families
like yours, Friend.

From day one, they saw me as just some small-town Alabama girl. Easy
to ignore and even easier to push aside.

But what they didn’t count on is the kind of _backbone_, _grit_, and
_fire_ women like me are made of.

The truth is, I’ve had to fight TWICE AS HARD to earn a seat at the
table. And the moment I got there, the Left wasted no time trying to
tear me down.

They didn’t expect a woman like me to show up and challenge
everything they stand for. They thought I’d sit down, smile, and
play nice. BUT THAT’S NOT WHO I AM, _AND IT NEVER WILL BE._

I’ve had to prove myself in _every_ room I walk into. I’ve had to
work longer hours, ask harder questions, and out-hustle the
establishment just to be taken seriously. And still, every day, they
try to undermine me, discredit me, and push me aside.

Why? Because I don’t play their games. I don’t fall in line. And I
won’t apologize for my values, my faith, or my love for this
country.

The Left is trying to undermine the values we hold dear, AND THEY’D
LOVE NOTHING MORE THAN TO SEE ME BACK DOWN.

But here’s the thing:

I’m not going anywhere.

I won’t apologize, I won’t play nice, and I won’t be backing
down.

They are terrified of strong, unapologetic conservative women, and
they should be.

If you believe in fighting harder than anyone else just to be heard.
If you believe in standing strong when the odds are against you, then
I need you with me.
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

Join the fight
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

This fight isn’t easy. It’s never been easy. But with your
support, we’ll keep pushing forward, together. And we’ll prove
that no one can ignore a woman with a backbone like mine.

Because if we don’t stand up today, the next generation will be
forced to fight the same battles I have — fighting just to have
their voices heard.

_AND I REFUSE TO LET THAT BE THEIR LEGACY, FRIEND._

[Katie Britt]
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

Katie Britt

U.S. Senator, Alabama

# Palestine
* **Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians across Gaza:** Israeli strikes killed three Palestinians and wounded others on Wednesday in separate attacks on Deir al-Balah, Al-Maghraqa, and Sheikh Ajlin, three neighborhoods southwest of Gaza City.
* Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed seven Palestinians, including one who succumbed to earlier injuries, and wounded 15 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* Israeli forces shot and killed a six-year-old Palestinian boy, Eyas Al-Namnam, near his displaced family's tent east of Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, on Tuesday.
* Eyas had woken up and was doing homework when his mother asked him to go to his aunt's nearby tent. "Three shots were fired at him," his brother, Abdul Karim Al-Namnam, told Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed. "Two bullets struck the ground and one hit him in the chest." **Watch the dispatch from Ahmed[here](https://substack.com/redirect/7b94d8de-53ad-4370-9832-cbd94e4b8216?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,710 killed and 176,131 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,658 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 6,000, while 850 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli forces launch first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since "ceasefire":** The Israeli military said on Wednesday that it had launched a "concentrated operation" in three areas of central Gaza near the "yellow line," west of the Israeli military zone established under the October 2025 ceasefire agreement. The military said that the operation was intended to eliminate "threats" to its forces. It closed parts of Salah al-Din Road, a main thoroughfare that runs north-south along the length of the enclave. Israeli military vehicles and bulldozers had begun advancing toward Salah al-Din Road from Al-Maghraqa, in central Gaza, Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah reported.
* **Israel restricts medical evacuations, Gaza Health Ministry says; over 21,000 patients await treatment abroad:** Israel continues to restrict medical evacuations, Gaza's Health Ministry said. Only 22 people, including patients and caregivers, were permitted to leave Gaza on Tuesday, although more than 21,000 people requiring medical care await evacuation. The October 2025 ceasefire provisions permit up to 150 people to leave for treatment every week.
* In October, the UN planned to stop receiving Palestinians returning from Egypt to Gaza in mid-November, citing security risks and repeated Israeli arrests, a senior Palestinian source involved in negotiations [told](https://substack.com/redirect/19f7b5f2-3e0c-4de2-a0c9-42fde5bb2308?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Drop Site News. The source warned that the decision could disrupt the entire Rafah crossing operation. The ceasefire agreement requires that equal numbers of Palestinians enter and leave Gaza, potentially blocking further medical evacuations.

* **Israel orders land seizure in Tulkarm and Nur Shams refugee camps:** An Israeli military order to seize land in the Tulkarm and Nur Shams refugee camps in the West Bank threatens to prevent thousands of forcibly displaced Palestinians from returning and rebuilding their homes, the Popular Committee for Tulkarm Camp Services [said](https://substack.com/redirect/07ae8df8-60df-416c-94b7-ae8bb4a2b1d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday. Israeli forces have maintained a siege of the two camps since January 2025. Soldiers have blocked residents from entering the camps, while demolishing and bulldozing the areas.
* **Israel extends detention of Gaza hospital director Hussam Abu Safiya another six months without charge:** On Wednesday, an Israeli court [extended](https://substack.com/redirect/d6b0e14b-9591-4f35-9192-2e73348b6515?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the detention of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, former director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza, for another six months. His lawyers and human-rights groups say that Israeli authorities have beaten him, deprived him of sleep, held him in solitary confinement, and degraded his health.
* The court rejected his request for release, his lawyer said, ruling that he "poses a threat to the State of Israel." Abu Safiya questioned the renewal of his detention, saying that he was being punished for fulfilling his professional duty as a doctor.
* **U.S.-backed Board of Peace says Gaza ceasefire risks collapse:** On Tuesday, the U.S.-backed Board of Peace [told](https://substack.com/redirect/b156633a-fd1b-4c3f-bb90-006ebd3fb5ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the UN Security Council that the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire could collapse. In a report, the Board of Peace faulted both Israel and Hamas for failing to fully implement the ceasefire agreement. Hamas agreed in July to decommission its "heavy" weaponry and transfer governance to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected the plan, refusing to withdraw its military forces from Gaza until Hamas is dismantled.
* "Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said. Since the so-called ceasefire took effect, Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,600 Palestinians, including at least 330 children and 164 women in Gaza.
* In a rare rebuke, the Board of Peace blamed Israel for delaying the formation of a civilian police force in Gaza, and for restricting the entry of essential supplies as Palestinians face "another winter in tents and rubble."

It is the first time Australia has sanctioned a company involved in settlement construction. Palestinian advocacy groups and the Greens political party called for broader sanctions, including against the Israeli government and settlement exports.
* **Hind Rajab Foundation seeks U.S. prosecution of former Israeli defense minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and genocide:** The Hind Rajab Foundation filed a request with the U.S. Justice Department on Tuesday seeking the prosecution of former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes in Gaza and Lebanon, and genocide in Gaza. He is scheduled to appear at an annual summit hosted by MirYam Institute, a pro-Israel organization, in New York City on Wednesday. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Gallant in November 2024 on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity.

# U.S. News
* **Hakeem Jeffries wins speaker nomination, commits to aggressive agenda on immigration, healthcare ahead of vote:** On Wednesday, Rep. **Hakeem Jeffries**(D-N.Y.) won the nomination for Speaker of the House, overcoming objections from some left-wing Democrats. Much of the opposition came from newly elected Democrats who are aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America. His critics within the party objected to his strong support for Israel, and his opposition to Medicare for All.
* On Tuesday, Jeffries announced his support for a broadly progressive Democratic agenda. "We're going to move the Dream and Promise Act" in the next Congressional session, he [said](https://substack.com/redirect/114b39f7-4ed7-48db-be97-502c9278096c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The American Dream and Promise Act, introduced by Rep. **Sylvia Garcia** (D-Texas), would grant legal permanent residency to undocumented immigrants who arrived in the U.S. as children, and to people shielded from deportation through Temporary Protected Status. Her discharge petition, which would avoid GOP obstruction, has 217 signatures, just one short of forcing a vote. A Democratic Congress could pass the legislation, but its codification would require President Trump's signature. Following the midterms, Trump said that he might "work a deal" to protect some people who have lived in the U.S. for 10-plus years and who do not have a criminal record.
* Also on Tuesday, Jeffries [called](https://substack.com/redirect/5cb5e7b2-210c-4998-af9a-e8e39dd4348b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for an aggressive Democratic health care agenda, including lowering the Medicare eligibility age and adding dental, vision, and hearing benefits to the plan. "And we should cover all the kids in the United States of America," he said. His remarks go well beyond earlier promises, in September, to undo Trump's Medicaid cuts and restore expired Affordable Care Act tax credits. Sen. **Bernie Sanders** (I-Vt.) said that Jeffries appears to be "essentially supporting the first year" of Sanders' proposed Medicare for All plan, which would begin by lowering the eligibility age to 55.
* **NSA reports outage of classified comms system:** An internal National Security Agency communications system was [down](https://substack.com/redirect/24210e44-55d1-465f-a6c0-1330ac2e6474?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday. The outage affected NSA Net, a system for classified communications. The cause is not known, but a former Pentagon official told the Washington Post that the outage delayed employees' work at Fort Meade, in Maryland, and elsewhere. The NSA said that the agency "experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," adding that "mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational." The outage does not appear to have affected core intelligence-gathering systems.
* **DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin defends use of government plane to attend college football game: Markwayne Mullin** , secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/03bedb1d-2a46-451a-9db8-61276b9694dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his flight on a government plane to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, for a college football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas on Saturday. Circuit panel voted 2-1 on Tuesday to [prevent](https://substack.com/redirect/0784dda8-5dbc-4b2e-a71e-bd6421398bd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the War Department from expelling 27 transgender troops from the military. * **Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempt to assassinate U.S. politician; he says Iran backed the plot:** On Monday, a Pakistani businessman, **Asif Merchant** , was [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/a1f60fb3-bed1-45f2-be0c-2bf3405bc9f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to 27 years in prison after he was convicted of trying to kill a U.S. politician in 2024. * **Mary Peltola wins Senate race in Alaska, bringing Dem majority to 56 seats:** Democrat**Mary Peltola** [defeated](https://substack.com/redirect/8efe47c0-2c7a-44d5-b91c-9bf1a50895b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Republican Sen. **Dan Sullivan** in Alaska's Senate race, becoming Alaska's first Native American senator and winning in a state that Trump won by 13 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. The DOJ opened a formal investigation of the incident, which has stalled in the courts. But Republican governor-elect **Mike Dunleavy** has said that Alaska could withhold Peltola's election certification while the investigation continues.
* **NYT: IRS pursuing criminal investigations of left-wing groups:** The Internal Revenue Service has [opened](https://substack.com/redirect/6861ebcc-15cb-4bb7-8428-26e262d56849?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least four criminal investigations into left-wing groups, the New York Times reported, citing an internal memo. The task force referred at least four tax-exempt groups to civil auditors. The IRS officials were assigned to nine grand juries, and used facial recognition and tattoo-analysis databases to investigate protesters arrested at Delaney Hall, an immigrant detention center in Newark, New Jersey.
* **White House abandons FDA nominee:** The White House [rescinded](https://substack.com/redirect/d6c282ef-7302-4e8e-855a-5f140b20dd74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its nomination of **Heidi Overton** to lead the Food and Drug Administration ahead of a Senate vote scheduled for Wednesday. The move comes after pushback from Democratic and Republican senators. **Bill Cassidy** , chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions committee, said on Sunday that he had "questions" about her nomination. Overton, deputy director of the White House Domestic Policy Council, has faced numerous criticisms, including over an executive order to alter the childhood vaccine schedule and to break up the measles vaccine. The FDA has operated without a permanent commissioner since **Marty Makary** resigned from the post in May.
* **DOJ misconduct complaints rise 54% under second Trump administration:** Professional misconduct complaints against DOJ personnel [rose](https://substack.com/redirect/d53eb887-e244-414f-94fe-9ea6a01d804f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 54% under Trump's second term, relative to those filed during the Biden administration. The Office of Professional Responsibility received 2,081 complaints last fiscal year, up from 1,346 in 2024. The report also noted a net decline of 10,345 department employees between January 2025 and May 2026.
* **Massachusetts town passes BDS measure:** The City Council of Somerville, Massachusetts, [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/6745faf8-f9c1-4010-8d06-c1adf8efec6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 10-1 on Tuesday to restrict city contracts and investments in companies linked to abuses in Palestine. Somerville is the fifth city in Massachusetts, and the 30th in the U.S., to adopt a measure in line with the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement, and the first to name Israel and Palestine explicitly in its operative language. The ordinance uses two databases maintained by the United Nations and the American Friends Service Committee to identify companies deemed complicit in abuses.

# Other International News
* **Brazilian federal police investigating Vance donor network for election interference:** Brazilian police are [inquiring](https://substack.com/redirect/826aca3c-730f-48b3-9103-7feabe695318?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) into whether the Rockbridge Network, the donor network co-founded by Vice President JD Vance, illegally intervened in Brazil's election to aid Flavio Bolsonaro, the Washington Post reported Tuesday. The probe opened days after Supreme Court Justice Flavio Dino ordered an inquiry into possible use of American resources in Bolsonaro's campaign, which is illegal under Brazilian law. Rockbridge denies involvement in the elections and says Brazilians used its name in documents without permission.
* **Pentagon policy secretary tells Europeans not to exclude American weapons firms from deals ahead of troop review:** Elbridge Colby, the Pentagon's policy chief, [cautioned](https://substack.com/redirect/b6b55861-8cba-493c-a00e-2f2eb218363d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) NATO's European members Tuesday in Brussels against shutting American companies out of arms contracts as they boost defense spending, saying "American companies make the best weaponry in the world" and arguing that a secure Europe needs hardware like the F-35. He said the U.S. is not insisting on American-only production and wants a "pragmatic, balanced relationship," while stressing that Washington will "allocate our military where it's most needed for Americans" in an upcoming troop review that will cover the roughly 80,000 U.S. troops in Europe.
* **Boat strike survivors sue Trump administration:** Ecuadorian fishermen who survived a U.S. military drone strike on their vessel have [filed a federal lawsuit](https://substack.com/redirect/cee3dfcb-e295-430e-a056-03d6331930bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against the Trump administration. The March attack sank their boat, left crew members with severe burns, and led to their arbitrary detention in El Salvador. The lawsuit seeks damages and an order halting the administration's campaign of strikes against boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. Drop Site News contributor Camila Lourdes Galarza reported on the [fishermen's accounts](https://substack.com/redirect/de27a059-b55f-43a4-80ff-4a7027fd98ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the attack and alleged abduction and torture, alongside testimony from survivors of another strike. A [follow-up investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/e6c53d9e-4dea-4959-84d6-226ccc1274d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reported that the prosecutor investigating the attacks was murdered and documented evidence of U.S. Coast Guard activity prior to the attack.
* **U.S. soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia is transferred to U.S. military custody:** A senior U.S. soldier [assigned](https://substack.com/redirect/5b2a1703-13eb-4bb9-8680-4ea0a42dc2e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to NATO who was arrested in the UK last week on suspicion of spying for Russia was transferred to U.S. military custody, the UK's Counter Terrorism Policing announced Tuesday. The 41-year-old was arrested on November 10 near Gloucester. The case is believed to be the first time a U.S. soldier has been suspected of spying for a foreign government while in the UK.
* **Mexico 's Sheinbaum tells China's Xi she wants deeper economic cooperation: **Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum [said](https://substack.com/redirect/d69474f9-5a10-4b2a-bc8e-aa3b2b369d2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday that Mexico is interested in strengthening cooperation with China in technology, agriculture, water resources, health, and tourism. The two leaders met in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Chinese state media reported that Xi urged the two countries to "treat each other with sincerity, deepen political mutual trust," promote friendly cooperation and strengthen strategic alignment.
* **Peru 's Fujimori seeks China's help on El Niño, says Beijing pledged $22.5 million in aid:** Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori [appealed](https://substack.com/redirect/bb9a2a36-bba1-4415-bf02-e6a5cbed4a37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for China's "goodwill" and support at a Tuesday meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, ahead of the APEC summit, and said Beijing pledged $22.5 million to help Peru cope with El Niño. Scientists say warmer ocean temperatures tied to El Niño are disrupting marine ecosystems off Peru's coast, threatening the fishing industry, and putting more than 1 million people in climate-vulnerable regions at risk.
* **Clashes between police and garment workers in Bangladesh escalate:** Bangladeshi police [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/a44da4e4-11d5-4bcf-a399-73a268871b98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tear gas and stun grenades at thousands of garment workers protesting a postponed wage board meeting on Tuesday. The protesters reportedly hurled bricks, torched vehicles, and blocked the main highway between Dhaka and Mymensingh after a key wage board meeting was postponed. About 500 of the country's 4,500 garment factories are shut, AFP reported, in an industry that earns $38 billion a year and employs more than four million people. Bangladesh is the world's second-biggest garment exporter.
* **Over 146,000 take to French streets as public-sector workers demand pay raises amid rising cost of living:** France's Interior Ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/1aa7b009-326b-4935-91f0-8be6bcf0035f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 146,000 people joined Tuesday's protests by public sector workers, estimating 28,000 in Paris alone, while the General Confederation of Labor put the nationwide turnout at just over 500,000. School pupils and university students struck in solidarity with the public sector workers, the third such strike since September. Unions say public servants have lost 16 percent of their purchasing power since 2017 and want the pay scale point used to calculate basic salary unfrozen, but the government has ruled out a general pay rise for a fourth consecutive year in its draft budget.
* **Mozambique opposition leader goes on trial:** Mozambique's main opposition leader, Venancio Mondlane, went on [trial](https://substack.com/redirect/e52841e1-909a-4e98-97cd-a55ab7cfe6fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday at the Supreme Court in Maputo on charges of inciting terrorism and civil disobedience over the unrest that followed the country's 2024 vote. Mondlane denies all charges and calls the proceedings politically motivated. A civil society monitoring group says more than 300 people were killed in the protests, the largest ever against the ruling Frelimo party, which has governed since independence in 1975. The opposition says President Daniel Chapo and Frelimo won through vote-rigging, and Western observers said the vote was not free and fair.
* **Trump announces critical-minerals agreements with Quad partners India, Australia and Japan at Manila meeting:** President Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f3c50bb4-3b51-4fca-ba5c-deff5c27ae26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) leaders of the Quad, which also includes Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, reached agreements to secure supply chains for critical minerals and prevent "coercion by any single foreign supplier." Trump did not single out China, which dominates the global market for rare-earth elements, but said he plans to "catch" China's production of rare earths within 10 months. The agreement also notes concerns about "economic coercion," given China's predominance in the market. China has effectively cut off key critical-mineral exports to Japan for nearly a year.
