This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. strikes Iran 's Qeshm Island; Iran widens Gulf attacks to Kuwait: U.S. fighter jets airstrikes on a missile-launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday, a U.S. military official told Reuters. The official said that the attack followed Iranian strikes on American personnel and assets. Early Wednesday, the Iranian military that it launched drones targeting U.S. Patriot air defense systems and missile and drone launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. It is the first Iranian attack on the country in more than two months. Kuwait's military reported a wave of incoming drones. In Bahrain, missile alerts sounded twice before dawn on Wednesday as air defenses fired and explosions were heard, with authorities blaming Iran for the attack. Iran has claimed responsibility for three attacks on U.S. assets in Bahrain over the past week. Iranian Army Chief Amir Hatami that further U.S. attacks on Iran would be met with a more forceful response "without geographical restrictions." UAE oil vessel attacked in Hormuz, one crew member missing and 11 injured: A vessel of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's shipping arm, ADNOC Logistics & Services, was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening, the Emirati state-owned company . One crew member remains missing, while 11 others were injured. All other crew members were safely evacuated, the company said. Three vessels struck naval mines in Hormuz on Tuesday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said, including a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and a liquefied petroleum gas carrier. Iran says U.S. "dirty bomb" claims echo Iraq war propaganda; Rubio says no imminent threat: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday that he does not believe there is an imminent threat to Washington, D.C. His comment follows a CNN report, citing U.S. intelligence assessments, that suggested that Iran may be planning to target senior Trump administration officials with a "dirty bomb" or a chemical weapon. "I don't think there is any imminent threat," Rubio told reporters. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi the claims "RUBBISH" and accused U.S. media of reviving the propaganda tactics that justified the 2003 U.S. invasion of Iraq. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf similarly the reports as the "same false flags, same war mongering, new logos." U.S. Navy says Iran war is straining resources, requiring use of previously expired munitions: The war with Iran is "stressing our naval resources," Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao on Tuesday during his Senate confirmation hearing. The Navy has begun using previously expired munitions to stem the shortages, he said. He also said that 17 Navy destroyers were supporting the U.S. blockade of Iranian ships at an estimated cost of $32.5 million a day. Iran says it downed U.S. drone near Hormuz: Iran's military claimed on Wednesday that it shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz. AI models repeatedly identify civilians, Iranian school as military targets, study finds: Advanced AI models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and xAI, repeatedly identified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers, and civilian infrastructure as military targets in simulated scenarios, Bloomberg . The models frequently identified as a military target the school in Minab, Iran, where the U.S. military killed at least 156 people, 120 of them children, in a strike earlier this year. In an earlier investigation, Bloomberg that the Minab school had been placed on a U.S. military target list after being classified as part of an IRGC naval facility. The targeting process included input from Palantir's Maven AI system. Earlier this year, Drop Site News published an in-depth account of the U.S. attack on Minab, including testimony from first responders, witnesses, and survivors. Read the full report. Palestine Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians across Gaza: Israeli strikes killed three Palestinians and wounded others on Wednesday in separate attacks on Deir al-Balah, Al-Maghraqa, and Sheikh Ajlin, three neighborhoods southwest of Gaza City. Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed seven Palestinians, including one who succumbed to earlier injuries, and wounded 15 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Israeli forces shot and killed a six-year-old Palestinian boy, Eyas Al-Namnam, near his displaced family's tent east of Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, on Tuesday. Eyas had woken up and was doing homework when his mother asked him to go to his aunt's nearby tent. "Three shots were fired at him," his brother, Abdul Karim Al-Namnam, told Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed. "Two bullets struck the ground and one hit him in the chest." Watch the dispatch from Ahmed. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,710 killed and 176,131 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,658 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 6,000, while 850 bodies have been recovered. Israeli forces launch first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since "ceasefire": The Israeli military said on Wednesday that it had launched a "concentrated operation" in three areas of central Gaza near the "yellow line," west of the Israeli military zone established under the October 2025 ceasefire agreement. The military said that the operation was intended to eliminate "threats" to its forces. It closed parts of Salah al-Din Road, a main thoroughfare that runs north-south along the length of the enclave. Israeli military vehicles and bulldozers had begun advancing toward Salah al-Din Road from Al-Maghraqa, in central Gaza, Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah reported. Israel restricts medical evacuations, Gaza Health Ministry says; over 21,000 patients await treatment abroad: Israel continues to restrict medical evacuations, Gaza's Health Ministry said. Only 22 people, including patients and caregivers, were permitted to leave Gaza on Tuesday, although more than 21,000 people requiring medical care await evacuation. The October 2025 ceasefire provisions permit up to 150 people to leave for treatment every week. In October, the UN planned to stop receiving Palestinians returning from Egypt to Gaza in mid-November, citing security risks and repeated Israeli arrests, a senior Palestinian source involved in negotiations Drop Site News. The source warned that the decision could disrupt the entire Rafah crossing operation. The ceasefire agreement requires that equal numbers of Palestinians enter and leave Gaza, potentially blocking further medical evacuations. Israeli forces detain 26 Palestinians across occupied West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces a house in Beit Awwa, west of Hebron, on Wednesday, according to WAFA. In Idhna, soldiers demolished an agricultural facility and uprooted olive trees. Across the governorate, soldiers arrested five Palestinians. Tulkarm: Israeli forces 14 Palestinians, including a woman, and damaged Palestinian property during raids on homes in Tulkarm city and Bal'a. Jenin: An Israeli settler olive-harvesting equipment from a Palestinian family in Arraba, south of Jenin, before summoning Israeli soldiers to the area. The soldiers subsequently raided the family's homes, assaulted residents, threw stun grenades inside houses, destroyed surveillance cameras, and arrested two family members. Qalqilya: Israeli soldiers five Palestinians, including Palestine TV cameraman Mohammad Inaya, during raids on homes across the city. Israel orders land seizure in Tulkarm and Nur Shams refugee camps: An Israeli military order to seize land in the Tulkarm and Nur Shams refugee camps in the West Bank threatens to prevent thousands of forcibly displaced Palestinians from returning and rebuilding their homes, the Popular Committee for Tulkarm Camp Services on Tuesday. Israeli forces have maintained a siege of the two camps since January 2025. Soldiers have blocked residents from entering the camps, while demolishing and bulldozing the areas. Israel extends detention of Gaza hospital director Hussam Abu Safiya another six months without charge: On Wednesday, an Israeli court the detention of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, former director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza, for another six months. Israeli forces detained him nearly two years ago, on December 27, 2024. Since then, Abu Safiya, 53, has been imprisoned without charge or trial. His lawyers and human-rights groups say that Israeli authorities have beaten him, deprived him of sleep, held him in solitary confinement, and degraded his health. The court rejected his request for release, his lawyer said, ruling that he "poses a threat to the State of Israel." Abu Safiya questioned the renewal of his detention, saying that he was being punished for fulfilling his professional duty as a doctor. U.S.-backed Board of Peace says Gaza ceasefire risks collapse: On Tuesday, the U.S.-backed Board of Peace the UN Security Council that the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire could collapse. In a report, the Board of Peace faulted both Israel and Hamas for failing to fully implement the ceasefire agreement. Hamas agreed in July to decommission its "heavy" weaponry and transfer governance to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected the plan, refusing to withdraw its military forces from Gaza until Hamas is dismantled. "Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said. Since the so-called ceasefire took effect, Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,600 Palestinians, including at least 330 children and 164 women in Gaza. In a rare rebuke, the Board of Peace blamed Israel for delaying the formation of a civilian police force in Gaza, and for restricting the entry of essential supplies as Palestinians face "another winter in tents and rubble." Australia sanctions Israeli settler leader Daniella Weiss and construction firm over West Bank settlements: Australia sanctions on Wednesday against three individuals and four organizations involved in illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank. Those sanctioned include the settler leader Daniella Weiss; Weiss's Nachala settler movement; and Eyal Hari Yehuda, a construction company that has aided settlement expansion. It is the first time Australia has sanctioned a company involved in settlement construction. Palestinian advocacy groups and the Greens political party called for broader sanctions, including against the Israeli government and settlement exports. Hind Rajab Foundation seeks U.S. prosecution of former Israeli defense minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and genocide: The Hind Rajab Foundation filed a request with the U.S. Justice Department on Tuesday seeking the prosecution of former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes in Gaza and Lebanon, and genocide in Gaza. He is scheduled to appear at an annual summit hosted by MirYam Institute, a pro-Israel organization, in New York City on Wednesday. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Gallant in November 2024 on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity. Yemen Saudi airstrikes kill 15 at factory in Hodeidah, Yemen: Saudi airstrikes on a factory in Hodeidah, Yemen, killed at least 15 people and wounded 13 others, including factory workers and rescue personnel, according to the Sana'a-based Health Ministry. The ministry said that Saudi jets struck the factory a second time after aid workers and journalists arrived on the scene, seriously wounding four members of a Yemen TV crew. released by Al-Masirah TV showed thick black smoke and flames engulfing the factory following the reported strikes. Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed 60 Ansarallah targets across Yemen, intercepted missile near Riyadh: The Saudi-led coalition that it carried out strikes against 60 Ansarallah military targets across the Yemeni governorates of Sana'a, Hodeidah, Amran, and Saada on Wednesday. Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Malki said that the strikes destroyed tunnels and underground facilities that Ansarallah used to store and produce ballistic missiles. Saudi coalition forces also intercepted and destroyed a missile launched by Ansarallah toward the Riyadh area in Saudi Arabia, Al-Malki said. U.S. News Hakeem Jeffries wins speaker nomination, commits to aggressive agenda on immigration, healthcare ahead of vote: On Wednesday, Rep. Hakeem Jeffries(D-N.Y.) won the nomination for Speaker of the House, overcoming objections from some left-wing Democrats. Much of the opposition came from newly elected Democrats who are aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America. His critics within the party objected to his strong support for Israel, and his opposition to Medicare for All. On Tuesday, Jeffries announced his support for a broadly progressive Democratic agenda. "We're going to move the Dream and Promise Act" in the next Congressional session, he . The American Dream and Promise Act, introduced by Rep. Sylvia Garcia (D-Texas), would grant legal permanent residency to undocumented immigrants who arrived in the U.S. as children, and to people shielded from deportation through Temporary Protected Status. Her discharge petition, which would avoid GOP obstruction, has 217 signatures, just one short of forcing a vote. A Democratic Congress could pass the legislation, but its codification would require President Trump's signature. Following the midterms, Trump said that he might "work a deal" to protect some people who have lived in the U.S. for 10-plus years and who do not have a criminal record. Also on Tuesday, Jeffries for an aggressive Democratic health care agenda, including lowering the Medicare eligibility age and adding dental, vision, and hearing benefits to the plan. "And we should cover all the kids in the United States of America," he said. His remarks go well beyond earlier promises, in September, to undo Trump's Medicaid cuts and restore expired Affordable Care Act tax credits. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) said that Jeffries appears to be "essentially supporting the first year" of Sanders' proposed Medicare for All plan, which would begin by lowering the eligibility age to 55. NSA reports outage of classified comms system: An internal National Security Agency communications system was on Tuesday. The outage affected NSA Net, a system for classified communications. The cause is not known, but a former Pentagon official told the Washington Post that the outage delayed employees' work at Fort Meade, in Maryland, and elsewhere. The NSA said that the agency "experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," adding that "mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational." The outage does not appear to have affected core intelligence-gathering systems. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin defends use of government plane to attend college football game: Markwayne Mullin , secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, his flight on a government plane to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, for a college football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas on Saturday. He took the flight shortly after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a national ground stoppage. Mullin said that he took the flight after airspace was "completely open for 21 hours." He added that he is required to travel by government plane, and that he personally paid for the trip. Kalshi halts bets predicting Trump statements: Kalshi is halting all bets on President Donald Trump's predicted statements, the Wall Street Journal . The decision comes after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered Kalshi to temporarily stop such bets due to concerns about bet manipulation. Last month, Kalshi's regulatory chief, Sudhir Jain , defended these types of bets as having "true hedging utility." Kalshi has not halted betting on the statements of other Trump administration officials. Earlier this year, Gabriel Perez , Trump's former teleprompter operator, was penalized for using insider information to place bets on the president's speeches. Politico: Hegseth 's personal attorney represents son of Libyan warlord: War Secretary Pete Hegseth 's personal attorney Tim Parlatore has Saddam Haftar , who is chief of staff of the Libyan National Army and the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar , since April, Politico reported. The father and son have been accused of extrajudicial killings and torture in a lawsuit filed by Mohammed Anbees , a Libyan man living in the U.S. The attorney representing the Haftars in the case is Parlatore himself. Pentagon fails annual audit for ninth consecutive year: The Pentagon its annual audit for the ninth consecutive year. The audit found that many of its financial-management systems are either outdated or otherwise inadequate. The audit assessed nearly $5 trillion of its assets and involved about 1,500 auditors. War Secretary Hegseth had set a goal of a clean audit by 2028. He has said that the department is using tools from Palantir and Elon Musk 's xAI to "automate financial reconciliations and documentation." Federal appeals court stops Pentagon 's attempt to expel 27 transgender troops from military: A D.C. Circuit panel voted 2-1 on Tuesday to the War Department from expelling 27 transgender troops from the military. The decision will allow transgender troops to remain in their posts, but it does not grant the entree of new transgender recruits. The same court panel ruled in June that the Trump administration's ban on transgender troops was unlawful. The administration has petitioned the Supreme Court to take up the case. Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempt to assassinate U.S. politician; he says Iran backed the plot: On Monday, a Pakistani businessman, Asif Merchant , was to 27 years in prison after he was convicted of trying to kill a U.S. politician in 2024. Possible targets included Donald Trump, Joe Biden , and Nikki Haley , according to trial testimony. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard urged Merchant to kill one of the targets, he said, adding that the IRGC assigned a handler to him. Iran has denied trying to kill U.S. officials. Merchant was caught after paying $5,000 in cash to undercover FBI agents posing as hit men. He was arrested in Texas in July 2024. Mary Peltola wins Senate race in Alaska, bringing Dem majority to 56 seats: DemocratMary Peltola Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, becoming Alaska's first Native American senator and winning in a state that Trump won by 13 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Her win brings the Democratic Senate majority to 56 seats. The Peltola-Sullivan race was controversial: The Justice Department accused Peltola's camp of getting a spoiler candidate onto the ballot, whose name is also Dan Sullivan. The DOJ opened a formal investigation of the incident, which has stalled in the courts. But Republican governor-elect Mike Dunleavy has said that Alaska could withhold Peltola's election certification while the investigation continues. NYT: IRS pursuing criminal investigations of left-wing groups: The Internal Revenue Service has at least four criminal investigations into left-wing groups, the New York Times reported, citing an internal memo. The memo shows that a dozen IRS officials are detailed to a federal task force under President Trump's 2025 order to investigate antifascists and groups espousing "extremism on migration, race and gender." The task force referred at least four tax-exempt groups to civil auditors. The IRS officials were assigned to nine grand juries, and used facial recognition and tattoo-analysis databases to investigate protesters arrested at Delaney Hall, an immigrant detention center in Newark, New Jersey. White House abandons FDA nominee: The White House its nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration ahead of a Senate vote scheduled for Wednesday. The move comes after pushback from Democratic and Republican senators. Bill Cassidy , chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions committee, said on Sunday that he had "questions" about her nomination. Overton, deputy director of the White House Domestic Policy Council, has faced numerous criticisms, including over an executive order to alter the childhood vaccine schedule and to break up the measles vaccine. The FDA has operated without a permanent commissioner since Marty Makary resigned from the post in May. DOJ misconduct complaints rise 54% under second Trump administration: Professional misconduct complaints against DOJ personnel 54% under Trump's second term, relative to those filed during the Biden administration. The Office of Professional Responsibility received 2,081 complaints last fiscal year, up from 1,346 in 2024. The report also noted a net decline of 10,345 department employees between January 2025 and May 2026. Massachusetts town passes BDS measure: The City Council of Somerville, Massachusetts, 10-1 on Tuesday to restrict city contracts and investments in companies linked to abuses in Palestine. Somerville is the fifth city in Massachusetts, and the 30th in the U.S., to adopt a measure in line with the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement, and the first to name Israel and Palestine explicitly in its operative language. The ordinance uses two databases maintained by the United Nations and the American Friends Service Committee to identify companies deemed complicit in abuses. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Brazilian federal police investigating Vance donor network for election interference: Brazilian police are into whether the Rockbridge Network, the donor network co-founded by Vice President JD Vance, illegally intervened in Brazil's election to aid Flavio Bolsonaro, the Washington Post reported Tuesday. The probe opened days after Supreme Court Justice Flavio Dino ordered an inquiry into possible use of American resources in Bolsonaro's campaign, which is illegal under Brazilian law. Rockbridge denies involvement in the elections and says Brazilians used its name in documents without permission. Pentagon policy secretary tells Europeans not to exclude American weapons firms from deals ahead of troop review: Elbridge Colby, the Pentagon's policy chief, NATO's European members Tuesday in Brussels against shutting American companies out of arms contracts as they boost defense spending, saying "American companies make the best weaponry in the world" and arguing that a secure Europe needs hardware like the F-35. He said the U.S. is not insisting on American-only production and wants a "pragmatic, balanced relationship," while stressing that Washington will "allocate our military where it's most needed for Americans" in an upcoming troop review that will cover the roughly 80,000 U.S. troops in Europe. Boat strike survivors sue Trump administration: Ecuadorian fishermen who survived a U.S. military drone strike on their vessel have against the Trump administration. The March attack sank their boat, left crew members with severe burns, and led to their arbitrary detention in El Salvador. The lawsuit seeks damages and an order halting the administration's campaign of strikes against boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. Drop Site News contributor Camila Lourdes Galarza reported on the of the attack and alleged abduction and torture, alongside testimony from survivors of another strike. A reported that the prosecutor investigating the attacks was murdered and documented evidence of U.S. Coast Guard activity prior to the attack. U.S. soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia is transferred to U.S. military custody: A senior U.S. soldier to NATO who was arrested in the UK last week on suspicion of spying for Russia was transferred to U.S. military custody, the UK's Counter Terrorism Policing announced Tuesday. The 41-year-old was arrested on November 10 near Gloucester. The case is believed to be the first time a U.S. soldier has been suspected of spying for a foreign government while in the UK. Mexico 's Sheinbaum tells China's Xi she wants deeper economic cooperation: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum in a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday that Mexico is interested in strengthening cooperation with China in technology, agriculture, water resources, health, and tourism. The two leaders met in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Chinese state media reported that Xi urged the two countries to "treat each other with sincerity, deepen political mutual trust," promote friendly cooperation and strengthen strategic alignment. Peru 's Fujimori seeks China's help on El Niño, says Beijing pledged $22.5 million in aid: Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori for China's "goodwill" and support at a Tuesday meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, ahead of the APEC summit, and said Beijing pledged $22.5 million to help Peru cope with El Niño. Scientists say warmer ocean temperatures tied to El Niño are disrupting marine ecosystems off Peru's coast, threatening the fishing industry, and putting more than 1 million people in climate-vulnerable regions at risk. Clashes between police and garment workers in Bangladesh escalate: Bangladeshi police tear gas and stun grenades at thousands of garment workers protesting a postponed wage board meeting on Tuesday. The protesters reportedly hurled bricks, torched vehicles, and blocked the main highway between Dhaka and Mymensingh after a key wage board meeting was postponed. About 500 of the country's 4,500 garment factories are shut, AFP reported, in an industry that earns $38 billion a year and employs more than four million people. Bangladesh is the world's second-biggest garment exporter. Over 146,000 take to French streets as public-sector workers demand pay raises amid rising cost of living: France's Interior Ministry 146,000 people joined Tuesday's protests by public sector workers, estimating 28,000 in Paris alone, while the General Confederation of Labor put the nationwide turnout at just over 500,000. School pupils and university students struck in solidarity with the public sector workers, the third such strike since September. Unions say public servants have lost 16 percent of their purchasing power since 2017 and want the pay scale point used to calculate basic salary unfrozen, but the government has ruled out a general pay rise for a fourth consecutive year in its draft budget. Mozambique opposition leader goes on trial: Mozambique's main opposition leader, Venancio Mondlane, went on Tuesday at the Supreme Court in Maputo on charges of inciting terrorism and civil disobedience over the unrest that followed the country's 2024 vote. Mondlane denies all charges and calls the proceedings politically motivated. A civil society monitoring group says more than 300 people were killed in the protests, the largest ever against the ruling Frelimo party, which has governed since independence in 1975. The opposition says President Daniel Chapo and Frelimo won through vote-rigging, and Western observers said the vote was not free and fair. Trump announces critical-minerals agreements with Quad partners India, Australia and Japan at Manila meeting: President Trump leaders of the Quad, which also includes Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, reached agreements to secure supply chains for critical minerals and prevent "coercion by any single foreign supplier." Trump did not single out China, which dominates the global market for rare-earth elements, but said he plans to "catch" China's production of rare earths within 10 months. The agreement also notes concerns about "economic coercion," given China's predominance in the market. body:
Chuck Hubbard can unseat the second most-powerful Republican in the House, but now he needs our help. | Folks, it’s Chuck Hubbard HQ.

November 3rd was an incredible night for Democrats – but right now, one of the most important races of all is coming down to provisional ballots in North Carolina, **where local journalist Chuck Hubbard has pulled ahead of the second most-powerful Republican in the House by just _331 votes._**

This is one of the closest House races in the entire country, and it could also be one of the most important.

As Chair of the Rules Committee, Virginia Foxx directly blocked the House from voting on Trump’s tariffs and the release of the Epstein files. When Elon Musk and DOGE ransacked our federal government last year, she stood by and cheered them on. She’s made a name for herself yelling at reporters to shut up and screaming at staff for using the wrong elevator. And for twenty years, she’s stepped on the backs of working people in order to climb the ladder in Washington, DC, all while making millions playing the stock market.

Just 331 votes could end her political career and the decades of nastiness – **but not without your help.** She’s not going to give up easily, so it’s up to us to defend this victory.

**For the first time in decades, North Carolina’s Fifth District can be represented by a Democrat.** Chuck Hubbard is ready to roll up his sleeves and get to work fighting corruption, lowering costs, and bringing decency back to his district, but as Virginia Foxx and the GOP challenge every single vote, we need to be ready to make sure voters are heard.

### News
**Alex Fairly guest column: GOP donor: Texas isn’t blue. It’s tired of Donald Trump — Our party has to demand better character in our leaders.**
_Republicans lost ground across every demographic: gender, race, age, religion and party affiliation. Texas fared worse because Sen.-elect James Talarico was a good candidate and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was a bad one, writes Alex Fairly. Pictured here, Paxton supporters hug after the candidate addressed the crowd during an election night watch party in Dallas, on Nov. 3._
Since [Election Day when the “blue tsunami”](https://link.mail.beehiiv.) swept through Texas, my phone has been busy with calls from elected officials, major donors, grassroots organizers, campaign consultants, think-tank leaders and people across Texas. Almost all are reciting the same familiar rallying cry: “We have to fight. The battle to win Texas back starts now.”
In between these calls and meetings, I have taken time to be quiet, pray and take an honest look at what really happened on Election Day.
I invested heavily in conservative races in Texas this past cycle and was closely involved in several statewide races. [I believe in low taxes, limited government and individual liberty](https://link.mail.beehiiv.) with every fiber of my being. I have fought hard to advance a principled conservative agenda in this state.
My commitment to this state and our values isn’t just political; it’s also personal. With my family, I support the Hill Institute at West Texas A&M; University to advance the timeless values of character, personal responsibility and virtuous citizenship. When making the gift to establish that institute, I said something I believe more urgently today than ever: “The way we live matters. The way we live together matters. Character is the indispensable foundation of an effective citizen in a constitutional republic.”
So let’s be honest about what happened on election night. America didn’t wake up and decide it wanted California-style progressive government. America — and Texas — stood up and shouted with stunning clarity: We are tired of Donald Trump.
There was a laundry list of reasons: cost of living, immigration enforcement, the Iran war, corruption — they all played a role.
**The Numbers Tell the Story**
The election wasn’t a soft erosion years in the making. Republicans lost ground across every demographic: gender, race, age, religion and party affiliation.
Texas fared even worse because James Talarico was a good candidate, and Ken Paxton was a bad one. Most Texans didn’t vote against Greg Abbott or for Gina Hinojosa. Their votes were a rebuke against Donald Trump. Americans of every race, gender, socioeconomic group and religion told us they were tired of him. They made a conscious, sweeping decision to reject our president.
Trump has built a political culture centered on himself, vengeance, threats and arrogance. His trademark is bullying and public humiliation of anyone who dares to disagree — Republican and Democrat alike.
These same qualities have infiltrated Texas, and Election Day was a wave of consensus saying: This is not who we are. This is not who we want to be. This is not what we stand for.
If conservatives in Texas are going to rebuild, two changes must happen.
**Stop the Cannibalism**
For years, a certain faction of Texas Republicans have spent enormous energy destroying other Republicans who don’t pass their arbitrary purity tests. We have treated policy friction like treason and recruited politicians whose primary skill is attacking colleagues and spewing divisiveness.
Trump’s [reaction](https://link.mail.beehiiv.) following Gov. Abbott’s gracious concession speech is a case in point. That kind of behavior has become the norm under Trump and is poisoning our party from the top down.
If we continue to excoriate anyone in our own ranks who doesn’t look, talk or vote exactly like us on every issue, we will continue to lose elections. Coalition-building requires hearty debate, discipline and common decency, not purity purges.
**Demand Virtue in Our Leaders**
The Republican Party must find a leader who understands that true strength requires humility and selflessness.
Of course, they must be strong, courageous and willing to take tough stands, but Texas and America need leadership of intelligence and virtue. Education, governance and civic life must take account of permanent values.
We need leaders who admit what they don’t know and are humble enough to surround themselves with principled counsel. We need leaders who possess the character to treat our allies and political opponents as fellow humans who deserve respect, even when the disagreement is profound and we don’t receive the same in response.
I believe Texas remains a conservative state at its core. But Texans have grown tired of the chaos, the vitriol and the grandstanding. Until Republicans reject the politics of ego and return to disciplined, humble and principled public service, the ground we stand on will keep eroding.
_Alex Fairly is an Amarillo businessman and political donor._

### State Government & Legislature
**Paxton drops CAIR lawsuit as Hinojosa pledges to rescind terrorist designation**
Attorney General Ken Paxton dropped the February lawsuit seeking to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) as a foreign terrorist and transnational criminal organization under Gov. Greg Abbott’s 2025 proclamation. The move follows Paxton’s Senate loss and Abbott’s defeat. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has said she will rescind the designation upon taking office. CAIR welcomed the development.
Sources: [USA Today](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [FOX 4 Dallas-Fort Worth](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Bills target data-center tax breaks as local giveaways top $1 billion**
A Texas Tribune analysis found cities and counties have granted at least $1 billion in local property-tax rebates to data centers, often with few or no job requirements. State sales-tax exemptions are projected to cost billions. Senate Bill 293 (Sen. Joan Huffman, R-Houston, with broad bipartisan support) and companion House bills would repeal the exemptions. Tarrant County separately moved to bar new data-center abatements.
Sources: [KXAN / Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Fort Worth Report](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Texas Policy Research](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Political momentum for adult-use marijuana, but Senate remains a hurdle**
With Democrats holding the House and statewide offices, lawmakers have pre-filed bills to legalize recreational marijuana for adults 21+, allowing limited possession, home cultivation, and regulated sales. Advocates see a clearer path than in prior sessions, though Republican control of the Senate remains a major obstacle.
Sources: [Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [NORML](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Houston Public Media](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**One in three Texas students leaves college without a degree**
A new study finds that one in three Texas students leaves college without a degree. Those who left and did not return within a year accumulated roughly $1 billion in student debt over the past five years.
Source: [Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Democrats file hundreds of bills as session approaches**
In the first week of pre-filing for the 2027 session, House Democrats filed more than 700 bills, including measures to expand Medicaid, repeal school vouchers, loosen immigration enforcement cooperation, and implement gun restrictions. Republicans retain control of the Senate.
Sources: [The Center Square](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Pleasanton Express](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)

### Local Austin & Central Texas
**Overnight I-35 lane closures continue this week**
TxDOT has scheduled multiple overnight lane reductions and rolling closures on I-35 through the Austin area for lighting, barrier, and bridge work, including stretches between Parmer Lane and Howard Lane and near Riverside Drive.
Sources: [MySA](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Austin Patch](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Austin City Council briefed on Muny / Brackenridge agreement**
Council members received a briefing on proposed amendments to the 1989 Brackenridge Development Agreement governing UT-owned land around Lions Municipal Golf Course. A vote is expected in early December. Advocates are also pushing to protect the nearby Brackenridge Field Laboratory.
Sources: [KXAN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [FOX 7 Austin](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Catholic Charities has federal funding restored**
Catholic Charities in the Austin area saw previously suspended federal funding restored. Separately, FAA officials are reviewing Austin flight paths amid rising commercial and general aviation traffic.
Source: [KXAN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Georgetown explores arts investments**
City staff presented findings from an arts and culture strategic plan, outlining potential improvements including a 9th Street art walk and upgrades to the Georgetown Arts Center.
Source: [KXAN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Travis County acquires nearly 1,000 acres of historic ranch land**
Travis County completed the purchase of 952 acres of Southwest Stallion Ranch for open space, natural resources, and public recreation.
Source: [KXAN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
|

### Texans in Washington / National
**Analysis of Democratic gains in Texas**
National coverage continues to examine the scale of Republican losses in Texas, including the sweep of statewide offices and the flip of the Texas House. Some observers note that even Sen. Ted Cruz may have been vulnerable had he been on the ballot.
Source: [Washington Examiner](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin faces congressional questions**
Mullin appeared before Congress amid questions related to recent flight disruptions and other issues.
Source: [KSAT / 1st Headlines](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)
**House Democrats file measures targeting immigration and other policies**
Texas House Democrats have pre-filed bills to repeal or limit state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and to reverse other Abbott-era policies.

Since swept through Texas, my phone has been busy with calls from elected officials, major donors, grassroots organizers, campaign consultants, think-tank leaders and people across Texas. ### Top News
**Alex Fairly guest column: GOP donor: Texas isn 't blue. It's tired of Donald Trump -- Our party has to demand better character in our leaders.**
_Republicans lost ground across every demographic: gender, race, age, religion and party affiliation. Texas fared worse because Sen.-elect James Talarico was a good candidate and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was a bad one, writes Alex Fairly. Pictured here, Paxton supporters hug after the candidate addressed the crowd during an election night watch party in Dallas, on Nov. 3._
Since [Election Day when the "blue tsunami"](https://substack.com/redirect/e18f8eb8-7466-403b-81d6-488b8c9e2804?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) swept through Texas, my phone has been busy with calls from elected officials, major donors, grassroots organizers, campaign consultants, think-tank leaders and people across Texas. Almost all are reciting the same familiar rallying cry: "We have to fight. The battle to win Texas back starts now."
In between these calls and meetings, I have taken time to be quiet, pray and take an honest look at what really happened on Election Day.
I invested heavily in conservative races in Texas this past cycle and was closely involved in several statewide races. [I believe in low taxes, limited government and individual liberty](https://substack.com/redirect/ae0d2d02-8d68-4a12-be6f-620fd236cf60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with every fiber of my being. I have fought hard to advance a principled conservative agenda in this state.
My commitment to this state and our values isn't just political; it's also personal. With my family, I support the Hill Institute at West Texas A&M University to advance the timeless values of character, personal responsibility and virtuous citizenship. When making the gift to establish that institute, I said something I believe more urgently today than ever: "The way we live matters. The way we live together matters. Character is the indispensable foundation of an effective citizen in a constitutional republic."
So let's be honest about what happened on election night. America didn't wake up and decide it wanted California-style progressive government. America -- and Texas -- stood up and shouted with stunning clarity: We are tired of Donald Trump.
There was a laundry list of reasons: cost of living, immigration enforcement, the Iran war, corruption -- they all played a role.
**The Numbers Tell the Story**
The election wasn't a soft erosion years in the making. Republicans lost ground across every demographic: gender, race, age, religion and party affiliation.
Texas fared even worse because James Talarico was a good candidate, and Ken Paxton was a bad one. Most Texans didn't vote against Greg Abbott or for Gina Hinojosa. Their votes were a rebuke against Donald Trump. Americans of every race, gender, socioeconomic group and religion told us they were tired of him. They made a conscious, sweeping decision to reject our president.
Trump has built a political culture centered on himself, vengeance, threats and arrogance. His trademark is bullying and public humiliation of anyone who dares to disagree -- Republican and Democrat alike.
These same qualities have infiltrated Texas, and Election Day was a wave of consensus saying: This is not who we are. This is not who we want to be. This is not what we stand for.
If conservatives in Texas are going to rebuild, two changes must happen.
**Stop the Cannibalism**
For years, a certain faction of Texas Republicans have spent enormous energy destroying other Republicans who don't pass their arbitrary purity tests. We have treated policy friction like treason and recruited politicians whose primary skill is attacking colleagues and spewing divisiveness.
Trump's [reaction](https://substack.com/redirect/0ea905b1-292e-4616-97e9-f2dc41f0ec8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) following Gov. Abbott's gracious concession speech is a case in point. That kind of behavior has become the norm under Trump and is poisoning our party from the top down.
If we continue to excoriate anyone in our own ranks who doesn't look, talk or vote exactly like us on every issue, we will continue to lose elections. Coalition-building requires hearty debate, discipline and common decency, not purity purges.
**Demand Virtue in Our Leaders**
The Republican Party must find a leader who understands that true strength requires humility and selflessness.
Of course, they must be strong, courageous and willing to take tough stands, but Texas and America need leadership of intelligence and virtue. Education, governance and civic life must take account of permanent values.
We need leaders who admit what they don't know and are humble enough to surround themselves with principled counsel. We need leaders who possess the character to treat our allies and political opponents as fellow humans who deserve respect, even when the disagreement is profound and we don't receive the same in response.
I believe Texas remains a conservative state at its core. But Texans have grown tired of the chaos, the vitriol and the grandstanding. Until Republicans reject the politics of ego and return to disciplined, humble and principled public service, the ground we stand on will keep eroding.
_Alex Fairly is an Amarillo businessman and political donor._

### State Government & Legislature
**Paxton drops CAIR lawsuit as Hinojosa pledges to rescind terrorist designation**
Attorney General Ken Paxton dropped the February lawsuit seeking to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) as a foreign terrorist and transnational criminal organization under Gov. Greg Abbott's 2025 proclamation. The move follows Paxton's Senate loss and Abbott's defeat. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has said she will rescind the designation upon taking office. CAIR welcomed the development.
Sources: [USA Today](https://substack.com/redirect/dcb9a18c-da09-4861-b2eb-e60e33a4c2cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [FOX 4 Dallas-Fort Worth](https://substack.com/redirect/a35a6014-cc5d-457a-8b1c-c092e2a47f43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Bills target data-center tax breaks as local giveaways top $1 billion**
A Texas Tribune analysis found cities and counties have granted at least $1 billion in local property-tax rebates to data centers, often with few or no job requirements. State sales-tax exemptions are projected to cost billions. Senate Bill 293 (Sen. Joan Huffman, R-Houston, with broad bipartisan support) and companion House bills would repeal the exemptions. Tarrant County separately moved to bar new data-center abatements.
Sources: [KXAN / Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/e5733afb-25cb-4fb8-ad9f-e800e9280520?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Fort Worth Report](https://substack.com/redirect/650cb1d4-1a96-4287-92ee-ef3e5b680112?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Texas Policy Research](https://substack.com/redirect/399222de-994d-44cf-9c19-59be185f233d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Political momentum for adult-use marijuana, but Senate remains a hurdle**
With Democrats holding the House and statewide offices, lawmakers have pre-filed bills to legalize recreational marijuana for adults 21+, allowing limited possession, home cultivation, and regulated sales. Advocates see a clearer path than in prior sessions, though Republican control of the Senate remains a major obstacle.
Sources: [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/cfa894ce-c76d-4027-91d2-b3988ffe467a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [NORML](https://substack.com/redirect/920f42ad-656e-43eb-8ccc-63e7884a34de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Houston Public Media](https://substack.com/redirect/13fc87f0-01d6-4b27-aad3-697cc70e1603?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**One in three Texas students leaves college without a degree**
A new study finds that one in three Texas students leaves college without a degree. Those who left and did not return within a year accumulated roughly $1 billion in student debt over the past five years.
Source: [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/d987b771-ed04-4fa7-8b7a-4bfa114ca2c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Democrats file hundreds of bills as session approaches**
In the first week of pre-filing for the 2027 session, House Democrats filed more than 700 bills, including measures to expand Medicaid, repeal school vouchers, loosen immigration enforcement cooperation, and implement gun restrictions. Republicans retain control of the Senate.
Sources: [The Center Square](https://substack.com/redirect/631a4ab0-a924-42f6-bcbd-e5cf9d35779a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Pleasanton Express](https://substack.com/redirect/ff57e059-9921-432f-be5f-ca72346679b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Local Austin & Central Texas
**Overnight I-35 lane closures continue this week**
TxDOT has scheduled multiple overnight lane reductions and rolling closures on I-35 through the Austin area for lighting, barrier, and bridge work, including stretches between Parmer Lane and Howard Lane and near Riverside Drive.
Sources: [MySA](https://substack.com/redirect/0415ee32-fb74-4e9d-a4b6-22d000df2c7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Austin Patch](https://substack.com/redirect/b3f5fdd9-eee2-437c-8ec5-0a5a24252c06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Austin City Council briefed on Muny / Brackenridge agreement**
Council members received a briefing on proposed amendments to the 1989 Brackenridge Development Agreement governing UT-owned land around Lions Municipal Golf Course. A vote is expected in early December. Advocates are also pushing to protect the nearby Brackenridge Field Laboratory.
Sources: [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/a2d66dcf-a1f0-4c1c-89e9-dddf349a3f4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [FOX 7 Austin](https://substack.com/redirect/2ad2d019-6ea4-4c9b-8774-658f36d0ea5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Catholic Charities has federal funding restored**
Catholic Charities in the Austin area saw previously suspended federal funding restored. Separately, FAA officials are reviewing Austin flight paths amid rising commercial and general aviation traffic.
Source: [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/ec51b173-43fb-4607-b90e-a1f2b5266718?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Georgetown explores arts investments**
City staff presented findings from an arts and culture strategic plan, outlining potential improvements including a 9th Street art walk and upgrades to the Georgetown Arts Center.
Source: [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/ec51b173-43fb-4607-b90e-a1f2b5266718?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Travis County acquires nearly 1,000 acres of historic ranch land**
Travis County completed the purchase of 952 acres of Southwest Stallion Ranch for open space, natural resources, and public recreation.
Source: [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/a2d66dcf-a1f0-4c1c-89e9-dddf349a3f4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Texans in Washington / National
**Analysis of Democratic gains in Texas**
National coverage continues to examine the scale of Republican losses in Texas, including the sweep of statewide offices and the flip of the Texas House. Some observers note that even Sen. Ted Cruz may have been vulnerable had he been on the ballot.
Source: [Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/0452c38a-34ce-4426-96cf-afb25cc208c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin faces congressional questions**
Mullin appeared before Congress amid questions related to recent flight disruptions and other issues.
Source: [KSAT / 1st Headlines](https://substack.com/redirect/52db46a8-4a49-4226-9432-ab2e9354fa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**House Democrats file measures targeting immigration and other policies**
Texas House Democrats have pre-filed bills to repeal or limit state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and to reverse other Abbott-era policies.
Source: [The Center Square](https://substack.com/redirect/631a4ab0-a924-42f6-bcbd-e5cf9d35779a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Business & Economy
**Data centers dominate fiscal and infrastructure discussion**
Beyond the tax-break story, local governments are tightening rules and lawmakers from both parties are advancing limits or repeals. A separate report flags potential water-supply strain from data centers. Business leaders remain cautiously optimistic about AI, energy, and infrastructure investment despite the political shift.

Top News Alex Fairly guest column: GOP donor: Texas isn 't blue. It's tired of Donald Trump -- Our party has to demand better character in our leaders. Republicans lost ground across every demographic: gender, race, age, religion and party affiliation. Texas fared worse because Sen.-elect James Talarico was a good candidate and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was a bad one, writes Alex Fairly. Pictured here, Paxton supporters hug after the candidate addressed the crowd during an election night watch party in Dallas, on Nov. 3. Since swept through Texas, my phone has been busy with calls from elected officials, major donors, grassroots organizers, campaign consultants, think-tank leaders and people across Texas. Almost all are reciting the same familiar rallying cry: "We have to fight. The battle to win Texas back starts now." In between these calls and meetings, I have taken time to be quiet, pray and take an honest look at what really happened on Election Day. I invested heavily in conservative races in Texas this past cycle and was closely involved in several statewide races. with every fiber of my being. I have fought hard to advance a principled conservative agenda in this state. My commitment to this state and our values isn't just political; it's also personal. With my family, I support the Hill Institute at West Texas A&M University to advance the timeless values of character, personal responsibility and virtuous citizenship. When making the gift to establish that institute, I said something I believe more urgently today than ever: "The way we live matters. The way we live together matters. Character is the indispensable foundation of an effective citizen in a constitutional republic." So let's be honest about what happened on election night. America didn't wake up and decide it wanted California-style progressive government. America -- and Texas -- stood up and shouted with stunning clarity: We are tired of Donald Trump. There was a laundry list of reasons: cost of living, immigration enforcement, the Iran war, corruption -- they all played a role. The Numbers Tell the Story The election wasn't a soft erosion years in the making. Republicans lost ground across every demographic: gender, race, age, religion and party affiliation. Texas fared even worse because James Talarico was a good candidate, and Ken Paxton was a bad one. Most Texans didn't vote against Greg Abbott or for Gina Hinojosa. Their votes were a rebuke against Donald Trump. Americans of every race, gender, socioeconomic group and religion told us they were tired of him. They made a conscious, sweeping decision to reject our president. Trump has built a political culture centered on himself, vengeance, threats and arrogance. His trademark is bullying and public humiliation of anyone who dares to disagree -- Republican and Democrat alike. These same qualities have infiltrated Texas, and Election Day was a wave of consensus saying: This is not who we are. This is not who we want to be. This is not what we stand for. If conservatives in Texas are going to rebuild, two changes must happen. Stop the Cannibalism For years, a certain faction of Texas Republicans have spent enormous energy destroying other Republicans who don't pass their arbitrary purity tests. We have treated policy friction like treason and recruited politicians whose primary skill is attacking colleagues and spewing divisiveness. Trump's following Gov. Abbott's gracious concession speech is a case in point. That kind of behavior has become the norm under Trump and is poisoning our party from the top down. If we continue to excoriate anyone in our own ranks who doesn't look, talk or vote exactly like us on every issue, we will continue to lose elections. Coalition-building requires hearty debate, discipline and common decency, not purity purges. Demand Virtue in Our Leaders The Republican Party must find a leader who understands that true strength requires humility and selflessness. Of course, they must be strong, courageous and willing to take tough stands, but Texas and America need leadership of intelligence and virtue. Education, governance and civic life must take account of permanent values. We need leaders who admit what they don't know and are humble enough to surround themselves with principled counsel. We need leaders who possess the character to treat our allies and political opponents as fellow humans who deserve respect, even when the disagreement is profound and we don't receive the same in response. I believe Texas remains a conservative state at its core. But Texans have grown tired of the chaos, the vitriol and the grandstanding. Until Republicans reject the politics of ego and return to disciplined, humble and principled public service, the ground we stand on will keep eroding. Good morning, my fellow Angry Democrats. I had a meeting this morning, so we're getting a little bit of a late start. If you want the full newsletter and the daily podcast, [become a paid subscriber for $5 a month](https://substack.com/redirect/e245d88d-1ff9-42fc-b24e-c23da57615d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That five bucks helps me keep following what happens at Cleveland City Hall after everybody else moves on to Washington. Already subscribed? Here's how to listen on [Apple Podcasts](https://substack.com/redirect/05b10dc6-a31b-42ea-b30e-9f5f7a0754d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or [Spotify](https://substack.com/redirect/077c8077-2168-44bf-b8ad-a3f809f3ae6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Jf3Ptg_3DC0nlPWvXI912HMb-OQii-fckrJ1uOixg7Y?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=225524374)
Today, Cleveland is raising your electric bill, the county library had to take its app offline, and Ohio lawmakers are looking at three abortion bills before they head out the door. Then there's Bernie Sanders. I want healthcare for everybody. I also want my own party to answer a perfectly fair question: **How are we going to pay for it?**
But first, who's meeting today?
* * *
### Today's government watchlist
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e03315bd-20b2-47e3-8fad-9117f8e8b4a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
All times Eastern. I recorded at about 10:30 this morning, so the first meeting was already on the calendar behind me. The county and state keep their meeting information online if you want to go back and see what you missed.
* **10 a.m.** Cuyahoga County Public Works, Procurement and Contracting Committee, county headquarters on East Ninth.
* **11 a.m.** Ohio House General Government Committee.
* **11:30 a.m.** [Ohio House Ways and Means Committee](https://substack.com/redirect/39c3409b-aa8c-41a9-9531-ee77eb78ed48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **1 p.m.** Cuyahoga County Health, Human Services and Aging Committee.
* **1:30 p.m.** Ohio Senate session.
* **2 p.m.** Ohio House session. [Statehouse session calendar](https://substack.com/redirect/901654d1-b7d4-4a52-a2a1-6452a971cdc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **5 p.m.** Cleveland Commission on Black Women and Girls, **Room 514 at City Hall**. The [city's meeting notice](https://substack.com/redirect/0c31aa1b-2897-4ba7-9b73-0e25538dd84f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) also has the Teams information if you want to attend from home.

In Washington, House Democrats are voting on who will lead their incoming majority. More on that below. [Ohio House of Representatives](https://substack.com/redirect/39c3409b-aa8c-41a9-9531-ee77eb78ed48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Cleveland and Cuyahoga County | Now it's your library card
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dd8aa274-8f9b-4219-be70-07f69fcd9cd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You expect to hear about a bank getting hit. You probably weren't thinking about your library card. Cuyahoga County Public Library took its app offline after a security incident involving two vendors that provide customer-account services. The library says borrowing histories and plain-text passwords weren't accessed. [cleveland19.com](https://substack.com/redirect/4e2d1bd1-856f-410f-8bce-35d31cd6be7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
What I keep thinking about is how many systems seem to be going down around the same time. I don't buy "everybody's just rolling out patches" as an explanation for everything. Are countries probing us to see what goes down and how quickly we get it back? Maybe. A guy on my Facebook offered another possibility: a lot of this stuff runs on old technology, and now some dude sitting in his apartment has a pretty capable AI model on his laptop. You don't need a foreign government for that. I don't know who did this one.
And look, if somebody _is_ attacking these systems and the disruption lasts hours instead of weeks, I'll give the defense some credit. The water's still running. The grid's still up. The other team may have moved the ball, but somebody's sacked the quarterback a couple times, too.
* * *
### Cleveland Public Power is raising rates. Collinwood wants to know what it's getting.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d2dc47d7-cc8a-45b4-8d59-72266f663113?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Peter, In a new piece for the [Sanders Institute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143658542/660955685/-319826822?cat=economy-economic-justice&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDMyMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTFjMTkyNTctNmVlMy1mMTExLTkxZjMtMDAwZDNhNTMzOTc4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hzMQS5rFAWnXZmc-aPXVdALlCbuKaelufPmPzpL--M8=&emci=62adb5ec-6be3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=91c19257-6ee3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=9848080), I lay out a choice facing our country: continue an economy rigged for billionaires, or build one that finally works for working people. Today, 60% of Americans live paycheck to paycheck. Families are struggling to afford health care, housing, childcare, and groceries. Meanwhile, billionaire wealth grew 21% in 2025 alone. Your answers are confidential.** Dear Fellow American, This summer, the national co-chair of the Democratic Socialists of America was asked on national TV whether her group wants to abolish the U.S. Senate. Her answer: “True.” Abolish ICE? “Absolutely.” Abolish America’s borders? “As a long-term plan, yep.” They aren’t hiding it anymore. And this is more than talk. DSA-backed candidates won Democratic primaries for Congress and the U.S. Senate. The DSA’s official national program calls on members to “draft a new constitution, and create a democratic socialist republic.” DSA wants to destroy the constitution, and force socialism on every American. That’s why The Heritage Foundation is asking concerned Americans in every state to weigh in. **Will you take the National Survey on Socialism?** **Take the 3-Minute Survey:** **[https://secured.heritage.org/national-survey-on-socialism/](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckd3qnDAQxZ8m3in50KgXudhWpAvdllJoL0NMphowiSTRZd--uN3tA_zvhjlzzvCb-X2TN2VX6-dvyoHQh5UxyfsCEUx4hD1l5U3wKWirVpskxZSXhJSkk0pne4CsVWGENpzRAgRp-wZTzGhdLAK47tqpbnnH4A8lpOc9nzBuGzZNXUv7woozjhDSEV43pK8wVtiQqSe41j2ZFKrxvhmVIVU6-ATxUOdO6304q-ArHVyxiiXnLSF2QXREdEyg9wimWiDarGaoQpwRHf3TodYy7fGARxl8-cZyp5GNe3ZSK7cpO3vEhv_qPwOi_BxIYY8aEBu2GNIGOls_vyQHxu4OsQGcsuurqYPP4DNiw4mKG3n59P3r9ecX-aMtP_-6lu8TFFGY7W7X1SbeohrPZ8aTL3_wLYegfwMAAP__1kmf-Q)** Your answers will help Heritage’s policy experts understand where Americans stand. | | Picture two faucets. One is non-hydro renewable energy. Right now it's a trickle, about 19% of our electricity. The other is fossil fuels, about 60% of the electricity we consume, and it's running full blast. We need to turn the renewable faucet up and turn the fossil faucet way down. **The permitting bill the Senate is considering, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, does the opposite.** **First, the good part.** There are real reforms in this bill to speed up the development of transmission lines that move solar and wind power from where it's produced to where it's needed.**I strongly support that.** More cheaper, cleaner energy online is something I'll always fight for. **But those gains aren't guaranteed.** Trump has already said he won't approve wind permits, even after this bill passes. And now for the bad stuff. The bill opens the fossil fuels faucet wide open:
* It makes it easier to build data centers powered by behind-the-meter natural gas plants.
* It restricts states' ability to raise clean water concerns about gas pipelines.
* It could let Trump issue unlimited permits far into the future, and "certainty" provisions mean they can never be revoked.
* It makes it easy to replace existing pipelines with larger ones, moving huge amounts of fracked gas to the Gulf for export.

**And this bill has never had a single hearing, in the House or the Senate.** It shortens timelines so grassroots groups can't raise concerns, strips tools states use to fight new data centers and detention centers, and undermines Tribal sovereignty. No wonder Trump and his billionaire buddies are full steam ahead. When Stephen Miller says passing this bill is his top priority, maybe we should pause and hold a hearing. **This is a bad deal. Permitting reform is needed, but not at great cost to our environment. Friends, I may have been in Washington for the past couple of weeks, but I haven’t lost sight of the priorities we created together back home. Our incoming class is having important conversations about our plans to root out corruption and lower costs. Last week, [50 of us joined forces](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.IrwCNRMzSkXvFsTjBP9k2KM7DR27f7kRbOsPWp5uBdiVM4hb17dExZxNK3Vi-lgz8FJ7JYD5V9fDhhXGdNyyq4QjjTgvdVCPz3y3IMIE-DiolfDS58-Q6dTWTOpmmY6tTMGvY63inMUmekF8dfiE3mWPVBIGOApyHJ6Wmp0o1JpN1GxKn8HZl-0MdkB1e3LjFPOjxdPp_9RtDKY4Z2-OUdgpisRJToXPVz_JMVvwV8u2cP_Qg9U-TiCju4N8kfC8viWvp3ARtkJSx4pmCR7qa8qkS7dmjNCUKdLb54ksvJdnXcIArfb3TOhuQKvrbSJAqnewApWGonjtsPHagYwJDNWxhsOr8b7uIw3KO1he77_I_3GK5e-rrLVXwJgdLoto879XNPV_x9gwazle3owgFg/4vu/9_heuDfzQMmgHrsZjPhZDA/h0/h001.viJF8qV4Ipp8x5L7D0XOuL7ol46pqMt8oRh9TOchvgA) in urging Democratic leadership to adopt a rule banning congressional stock trading. Because for far too long, Washington politicians have been enriching themselves at the expense of everyday Americans. I ran for office to end that corruption and bring down costs for working families like mine. Banning congressional stock trading is the first step, but we cannot stop there. We must enact term limits to ensure that members of Congress are focused on the next generation, not the next election. And we must also reject corporate PAC money and fight to get big money out of politics by overturning _Citizens United_. It’s long past time for our elected officials to serve the people, not corporations and special interests. Our work here is just getting started.
With gratitude and fire,
Cait Conley

I took it easy on your inbox over the last few weeks because of the heavy bombardment from candidates as they entered the homestretch.
Which means I've got a backlog of good news.
Below is the latest installment of _50 chessboards_ \- my periodic attempt to convey a broader sweep of all the fights we're in, rather than my usual focus on one or two big ones.
In reality, we have about 10,000 active cases, so even the _50 chessboards_ metaphor is a little light, but at least it conveys that we've got a lot more going on than you usually hear about from me.
Diving in:
* **Wedding photography case:** We won our lawsuit against the wedding photography company that swindled over 200 couples. The judge ordered the owners to hand over the wedding photos they still have, pay back the couples all money owed, and pay civil penalties on top of that because of their egregious behavior. They're also now banned from selling photography or video services. _(Note: When I took my kids to the State Fair, three separate people stopped me to thank us for taking this case. How these couples were treated really bothers people, as it should.)_
* **Gas tax:** As you know, the state legislature paused it until Nov. 30th, but I wanted to make sure the savings actually get passed on to drivers. The tax is paid first by the gas station when it buys its inventory, so making sure they pass that savings along to customers is really important. We launched N.C. Fuel Check so drivers can report stations they believe are pocketing the tax savings instead. We got many, many reports from drivers, and we have now followed up on over 50 gas stations.
* _**Attorney General vs. Dollar General:**_**** After an investigation, we found that Dollar General is often charging customers more at the register than the price says on the shelf. Basically a bait-and-switch. When state inspectors checked 10 stores, they found nearly 400 pricing errors. Given that our state has over 1,000 Dollar General stores and over one million North Carolinians shop at one each week, this is a major issue that deserves our attention. So we've taken them to court. I think we've got a strong case, especially considering some of the internal documents the investigation turned up that show the company seems to have known what was happening and did nothing about it. Here's a **[video](https://substack.com/redirect/33c8eae2-b400-4d0f-b260-469c9de8ebd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I did about our case, which I filmed from inside a Dollar General store:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b67b9dd9-4eb2-40c0-ad54-d364a908fe13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Criminal convictions:** A lot of our criminal work is handling appeals after a prosecutor gets a conviction in their district. In the last few weeks, we've won dozens of cases, upholding convictions in murder cases in Gaston, Pender, Wilson, and Guilford counties, attempted murder in Rockingham County, a rape case in Pitt County, a sex offense case in Wake County, and a child sex offense case in McDowell County.
* **Fake nurse:** In Burlington, a nursing home hired someone to work as a nurse despite that person having no nursing license, training or experience. The facility then billed Medicaid for several months of her work. Can't do that. After we got involved, the facility agreed to pay the state back.
* **Food assistance:** Last year, we won a big SNAP (food assistance) case making sure people had food over the Thanksgiving holiday season. Well, we just won another. The Dept. of Agriculture, which runs the SNAP program, had said that new eligibility rules had to be implemented in as little as 24 hours, or it could eventually cost us $425m in funding. We argued it was logistically impossible to meet their deadlines, and the court agreed, stating that we had been put "in an impossible situation to timely implement" the new rules. You didn't hear much about this case, but if we had lost, the effect on our state could have been catastrophic for the 1.4m people (and 600k kids) who rely on SNAP. I'm really proud of our work on this one.
* **Prescription drugs:** I know you'll be shocked to hear this, but there's been some illegal pricing when it comes to prescription drugs. We found that many of these companies conspired to raise the price of generics. Part of our work here has resulted in a refund process for folks who were overcharged. You can see if you're eligible at [AGGenericDrugs.com](https://substack.com/redirect/e67c98e5-9631-402e-a86c-9796e22f95fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Baby formula:** We alleged that Abbott knowingly sold formula with a high risk of contamination from unclean facilities and didn't disclose it to the FDA. Now Abbott will have to make payments to our state Medicaid and food assistance programs to pay the taxpayers back for their conduct. There are also class action lawsuits on behalf of consumers.
* **Auto loans:** We alleged that one of the country's largest auto lenders, Credit Acceptance Corporation, deliberately made loans to buyers it knew couldn't afford the monthly payment, basically making it part of their business model. As you'd expect, a lot of those buyers lost their cars. Part of the consequences for this company involves sending money back to those borrowers and wiping out some of their debt.
* **Robocalls:** Our war continues. We're fighting this one on a number of fronts, being as aggressive as possible. That means trying to get a national response from the FCC. So last week, we led attorneys general from nearly every state in asking the FCC to issue a new set of rules that would make robocalls much easier to track and block. And we're looking for ways to fix the laws to stop the calls in the first place.
* **Amazon scheme:** We sued Amazon over what we allege was a massive scheme to secretly manipulate its advertising auctions. Here's how it's supposed to work: You bid $1 for an ad spot, the next-highest bidder offers 50 cents, so you win at 51 cents. Amazon told sellers that's how the auction worked, then allegedly inserted its own higher bid after the fact to make the winner pay more, adding up to over $20b in overcharges. Those advertising costs get built into the prices people pay for groceries, clothes, school supplies, and everything else sold on Amazon.
* **Durham water pollution:** This one started with an anonymous tip about chemical dumping at a facility in Durham. We sued the company, Brenntag, after testing found contamination flowing toward a creek which eventually reaches Jordan Lake. We got a court order mandating that the company stop the discharge and clean up the mess.
* **Rent prices:** We're suing RealPage, a software company that we believe used private data to help major apartment complex owners coordinate with each other to drive up the rent. We alleged that landlords used it to set rents on about a third of the one- and two-bedroom apartments in the Charlotte, Raleigh, and Durham areas, which means it affected tens of thousands of families in our state. The good news is that RealPage tried to have our case thrown out, but the judge ruled against them. We're moving forward.
* **Head Start:** We pushed back on a new federal effort that could severely undermine Head Start, the preschool program for low-income families. Our position is that the administration is trying to make changes that conflict with the law Congress actually passed and would worsen outcomes for children.
* **Meta:** A few months ago, we got a $490m settlement for North Carolina from Meta, the owner of Facebook and Instagram. The first payment of $41m has now arrived and the next one is coming in January. We are making recommendations on how it should be spent (the legislature makes the final call), and we believe the focus should be on young people, since that's why we took Meta to court in the first place. In addition to the money, the larger agreement also requires new protections for young users, including stronger parental controls and default limits on how kids use the platforms.

Looking at this update, you'll see cases that cover food, rent, energy, healthcare, big tech, child care, transportation, clean water, and public safety - _and there are 10,000 more I didn 't mention._
So we're staying busy, and I'll keep you posted.
Best,
Jeff

Hi team,
Remember when pundits were writing Nevada off as trending red? We showed them.
Even when Joe Lombardo stockpiled millions in his warchest for reelection and heavily outspent Democrats, we were resourceful and focused on delivering our message to the voters.
**We could not do this without your support, with you on our side we made history — what The Indy is calling**** _“Nevada Democrats’ best election ever.”_******
This is what we won together:
* We elected Aaron Ford, Nevada’s first ever Black Governor, the first Black Governor west of the Mississippi.
* We elected Democrats to all statewide constitutional offices for the first time since 1962: Sandra Jauregui for Lt. Governor, Francisco “Cisco” Aguilar for Secretary of State, Dr. Tya Mathis-Coleman for State Treasurer (the first Black woman elected to statewide office in Nevada!), Michael MacDougall for State Controller, and Nicole Cannizzaro for Attorney General.
* We flipped an R+14 district with the first ever Democrat, Teresa Benitez-Thompson, to win NV-02.
* We elected a supermajority in the state Assembly, by more than 30 seats for the first time since 1977.
* We won control of the Washoe County Commission for the first time ever.

Now we have to do the job the voters demanded — pass legislation that will address the cost of living and save Nevadans’ wallets. If we want to keep winning, we have to make sure Nevadans know how we’re fighting for their families every day, not just a few weeks out from Election Day. _That requires resources, but our reserves are low after going all out to secure these legendary wins._
**[Your support helped us win before, now power our next big wins. 2028 is already underway, all paths to victory flow through Nevada, but our warchest is emptied out.
