clean_body: | | | | Hi team, Remember when pundits were writing Nevada off as trending red? We showed them. Even when Joe Lombardo stockpiled millions in his warchest for reelection and heavily outspent Democrats, we were resourceful and focused on delivering our message to the voters. We could not do this without your support, with you on our side we made history — what The Indy is calling “Nevada Democrats’ best election ever.”** This is what we won together: We elected Aaron Ford, Nevada’s first ever Black Governor, the first Black Governor west of the Mississippi. We elected Democrats to all statewide constitutional offices for the first time since 1962: Sandra Jauregui for Lt. Governor, Francisco “Cisco” Aguilar for Secretary of State, Dr. Tya Mathis-Coleman for State Treasurer (the first Black woman elected to statewide office in Nevada!), Michael MacDougall for State Controller, and Nicole Cannizzaro for Attorney General. We flipped an R+14 district with the first ever Democrat, Teresa Benitez-Thompson, to win NV-02. We elected a supermajority in the state Assembly, by more than 30 seats for the first time since 1977. We won control of the Washoe County Commission for the first time ever. Now we have to do the job the voters demanded — pass legislation that will address the cost of living and save Nevadans’ wallets. If we want to keep winning, we have to make sure Nevadans know how we’re fighting for their families every day, not just a few weeks out from Election Day. Peter, When I ran for Congress, I promised to represent the needs of my home district and working families across Illinois, and now that I’m heading back to Washington with Democrats in the majority, I want to make sure I start the new year by listening. Everywhere I go in Central and Northwestern Illinois, I hear about the cost of groceries, gas, health care, and prescription drugs. I hear about the future of our family farms and the real worry that rural hospitals will get squeezed. I hear concern about the war in Iran, about tariffs hitting our manufacturers and farmers, and about how quickly artificial intelligence and data centers are showing up in our communities. Those are just the conversations I’ve had _so far_. So I want to ask you directly: is there something I’m overlooking? What’s bugging you, and what can I do to help? [**Please take a moment to fill out this survey and tell me what Congress’ priorities should be in 2027? Your feedback matters a great deal to me, and it will help shape where I focus my time from day one.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143665299/660979991/-1487955014?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDZmZGQ5Ni03Y2UzLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wcADIIUNJqvUDhZMxIJ64BYMJWukRte91BeBG1cpiJY=&emci=e373bb90-7ce3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=d46fdd96-7ce3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=18052858) | [Take the Survey](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143665300/660979992/-1487955014?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDZmZGQ5Ni03Y2UzLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wcADIIUNJqvUDhZMxIJ64BYMJWukRte91BeBG1cpiJY=&emci=e373bb90-7ce3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=d46fdd96-7ce3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=18052858)

body:
I want to hear from you. | |
Peter, I'm in Washington, DC for freshman orientation, and it's been a trip. I'm meeting my new colleagues, finding the best cup of coffee and already starting to have conversations about the progress I promised to deliver. I ran for Congress to lower the cost of living, protect access to health care, and stand up to Donald Trump and his administration when they threaten our communities and our fundamental rights. I'm not waiting until I'm sworn in to get to work. I told you I wanted an open-door policy, and I meant it. I want to hear from you often. What's the first thing you want me to fight for? Reply and tell me. Here's what's at the top of my list:
Housing you can afford
Health care you can count on
LGBTQ equality
Protecting immigrant families
AI regulation
Accountability for this administration
A government that works for people – not powerful interests There's no time to waste. I'm ready to hit the ground running. What else needs to be on this list? Write back and let me know what you’re thinking. We’re in this together. Thank you for being part of this movement. We built something truly special with this campaign and now, it’s time to deliver. \- Scott

| Here’s everything I did to earn a menacing letter from Trump’s DOJ.
---
Derek, this morning a Trump-appointed U.S. attorney sent me a letter on Justice Department letterhead, and it reads just like a threat. _It is meant that way, too._ Aaron Reitz is a MAGA loyalist who promised to investigate the people investigating Trump, and today he made good on it — citing federal criminal statutes, demanding I preserve my records, and warning of “significant legal consequences” if I don’t. **[Attacks like this will not deter me from investigating corruption in the Trump Administration. Will you chip in $10 to show you have my back and keep me in the Senate?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8046?t=9&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_111826_attorneyrr&akid=10945%2E5257348%2EmNHmp-)** | | [DONATE→](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8046?t=11&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_111826_attorneyrr&akid=10945%2E5257348%2EmNHmp-)

In addition to sending this tweet, here is everything I did to earn this menacing letter from the Department of Justice:
I demanded to know who paid for Trump’s $900 million ballroom. Who funded Freedom 250. What’s really behind the ABC and CBS settlements, and the pro bono deal Kirkland & Ellis cut with the White House.
These are the questions any oversight committee would ask, and the questions the American people have every right to have answered. Because this administration’s corruption has driven up costs for every American family.
DOJ’s letter calls these donors “private Americans,” but a billionaire who writes a check to the president is not simply a private citizen minding his own business.
And one more thing this Trump enabler at DOJ didn’t like. He didn’t like my calling him “bat shit crazy.” But no self-respecting, rule of law abiding prosecutor would put their name on such meritless drivel.
Reitz already sent the same letter to Senator Blumenthal, to Senator Warren, and to Senator Slotkin, and the message to the rest of Senate Democrats is unmistakable: the Justice Department exists to protect the people paying Trump — and asking where the money came from will be treated as a criminal act.
I won’t back down. I won’t be intimidated.
Millions of Americans rejected this corruption at the ballot box two weeks ago. They gave us the majority to ask hard questions and follow the money until we find out who is buying access to our government and what those individuals are getting in return.
**That’s why I need you to have my back right now.**

These are the questions any oversight committee would ask, and the questions the American people have every right to have answered. Because this administration’s corruption has driven up costs for every American family. DOJ’s letter calls these donors “private Americans,” but a billionaire who writes a check to the president is not simply a private citizen minding his own business. And one more thing this Trump enabler at DOJ didn’t like. He didn’t like my calling him “bat shit crazy.” But no self-respecting, rule of law abiding prosecutor would put their name on such meritless drivel. Reitz already sent the same letter to Senator Blumenthal, to Senator Warren, and to Senator Slotkin, and the message to the rest of Senate Democrats is unmistakable: the Justice Department exists to protect the people paying Trump — and asking where the money came from will be treated as a criminal act. I won’t back down. I won’t be intimidated. Millions of Americans rejected this corruption at the ballot box two weeks ago. They gave us the majority to ask hard questions and follow the money until we find out who is buying access to our government and what those individuals are getting in return. # [Nvidia doubles revenue to $116B as board PERMENANTLY rejects Huang](https://substack.com/redirect/f28f65f6-bfbf-45c0-989d-d4cc890387a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia **[reported third-quarter revenue](https://substack.com/redirect/7a54ae5d-ed63-4f75-9a72-f429e19d66eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, while chairman Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate founder Jensen Huang after he offered to return.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f28f65f6-bfbf-45c0-989d-d4cc890387a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revenue and data center** : Third-quarter sales reached $115.84 billion with data-center revenue near $107.6 billion to $108 billion, beating estimates around $109 billion.
* **Guidance and growth** : The company guided current-quarter revenue to $130 billion at the midpoint and[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9a941bcb-e918-4c9c-93b1-bd4d5d7537f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[lifted next-year revenue growth outlook to 75%](https://substack.com/redirect/9a941bcb-e918-4c9c-93b1-bd4d5d7537f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from 70%.
* **Leadership decision** : Jones said the board **[unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and is not considering reinstatement,](https://substack.com/redirect/d0cc3d62-cc39-4102-9361-cd03ee8cf948?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while interim CEO Colette Kress said "We've got this."
* **Probes and China** : The SEC is investigating Nvidia's disclosures; the company stopped shipping Hopper-series chips to China, and **[Huang is scheduled to appear before House panels on Dec. 1.](https://substack.com/redirect/d0cc3d62-cc39-4102-9361-cd03ee8cf948?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

# [Anthropic prices $1.4T IPO today in ultimate AI boom test](https://substack.com/redirect/f28f65f6-bfbf-45c0-989d-d4cc890387a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Anthropic **[expects to price its initial public offering on Nov. 18](https://substack.com/redirect/52116d6f-088f-47eb-b2ef-8af45d2bdd63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for trading as ANT on Nov. 19, with a range of $70 to $78 for 825 million shares implying a fully diluted valuation near $1.4 trillion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f28f65f6-bfbf-45c0-989d-d4cc890387a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Share offering size** : The company is offering **[825 million Class A shares at $70](https://substack.com/redirect/f0ef2b51-736e-4f83-8254-a916ae73ed4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f0ef2b51-736e-4f83-8254-a916ae73ed4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[to $78,](https://substack.com/redirect/f0ef2b51-736e-4f83-8254-a916ae73ed4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f0ef2b51-736e-4f83-8254-a916ae73ed4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)plus a concurrent $26 billion private placement from **[Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and other tech firms.](https://substack.com/redirect/f244897e-ba8f-40f6-aa1e-d15d5a5f2176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Valuation range** : At the top of the range the fully diluted value approaches $1.4 trillion, with reports of strong demand and possible pricing above the range.
* **Timing and ticker** : Pricing is expected this evening with first trade Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.
* **AI market context** : The debut follows Nvidia's strong results amid leadership turmoil and **[tests investor appetite for the AI trade after recent volatility.](https://substack.com/redirect/52116d6f-088f-47eb-b2ef-8af45d2bdd63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

# [Waller: Fed may need 50bp shock hike as inflation spreads](https://substack.com/redirect/f28f65f6-bfbf-45c0-989d-d4cc890387a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Fed Governor Christopher Waller **[told CNBC](https://substack.com/redirect/534dc13c-5346-4f90-a659-62c5a9cd49f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** inflation is **["spreading out"](https://substack.com/redirect/5f297aba-df6c-4d70-ba4e-20974474be41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and heading the wrong way, saying a half-point rate hike at the December meeting may be needed to "shock people."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f28f65f6-bfbf-45c0-989d-d4cc890387a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Inflation concerns** : Waller said most readings are above 3% and inflation has reignited, driven by energy spikes and tariffs after earlier events.
* **Hike path** : He backed a 50 basis point move in December or a 25 basis point hike with a clear signal for January, after last year's three quarter-point cuts.
* **Policy stance** : Waller argued current policy is not sufficient and more aggressive actions are required to bring inflation down.
* **Market reaction** : **[Futures had been pricing a quarter-point December hike;](https://substack.com/redirect/15b6f486-a771-49a4-995b-9db77ac41086?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/15b6f486-a771-49a4-995b-9db77ac41086?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)minutes are due later Wednesday.

U.S. stocks fell Tuesday as the S&P 500 broke its 200-day moving average and **[technicians warned of a double-top pattern,](https://substack.com/redirect/11954631-213e-490b-91c3-d8b54d7aa510?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** then futures rose Wednesday after Nvidia's results.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f28f65f6-bfbf-45c0-989d-d4cc890387a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tuesday selloff** : The Dow dropped as much as 1.8% or nearly 1,000 points, the S&P 500 fell about 1.3-1.6%, and the Nasdaq declined up to 2%, with more than 80% of S&P stocks lower.
* **Technical signals** : The S&P 500 **[undercut its 200-day average; 61.4%](https://substack.com/redirect/1eddff50-c435-4ade-b223-2a8155cac659?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of Nasdaq 100 stocks are already down 20% or more.
* **AI doubts** : **[Doubts about the AI boom](https://substack.com/redirect/c783a278-534d-449e-9015-8d645ded6285?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and another system outage weighed on sentiment ahead of Nvidia earnings.
* **Wednesday bounce** : Futures rose after Nvidia's beat and raised guidance, with **[attention turning to Anthropic's IPO.](https://substack.com/redirect/d2ca286b-0a8a-447f-ba9e-505345ac4766?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Fund our deputies. No new committee

| | | | | |

| STOP DEFUNDING OUR DEPUTIES $125 million shortfall · Over 600 fewer deputies at risk

**A MESSAGE FROM SHERIFF CHAD BIANCO.**

Friends,

Thank you to everyone who called and emailed your Supervisor over the last couple of weeks. The Board is hearing you. **We're not done. We have until January to make our voices heard.**

Our message is simple:
* **Fund our Sheriff's Department.**
* **Do not create another "oversight" committee.**

---
| | | | | |

We already have federal, state and local oversight. Another committee won't make your neighborhood safer. It just spends more of your money and hands more control to politicians, all while making the jobs of our deputies harder.
**Call your Supervisor. Email your Supervisor.** Be respectful, be assertive, and keep it short: fund our deputies, and no ad hoc committee. **Then share this with your Facebook friends and neighbors.**
The Board needs to hear from all of us, not just the activists who already pressured the Board to **defund the Sheriff’s Department by $125 million.**

body:
Let’s take a look at how far we’ve come and where we must go.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143667598/660986694/-453679381?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjU0YjAwMDRjLTgyZTMtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=n5QSsoW_us1aFHRGnSTZUwmw5tEUvq3NV4SNGEYchLQ=&emci=cb826654-c7e2-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=54b0004c-82e3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=8431045)
---
_Formerly All On The Line_

Peter,
Coming out of a historically consequential midterm election, let’s take a look back at how far we’ve come in the last two years, where we need to be in the next two months, and where we can get ourselves two years from now.
**In 2026, despite an unprecedented mid-decade gerrymandering crisis across the country, and despite an onslaught of attempts to restrict access to the ballot, Americans were able to make their voices heard.**
**That wasn’t an accident.** People like you made it happen. People like you said no to extreme gerrymanders that threatened to silence their votes. People like you got involved with Redistricting Action — getting out the vote, joining volunteer trainings, testifying, speaking out to lawmakers, writing letters to the editor, pushing back against voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act, recruiting friends to join the fight, and making grassroots donations when possible to power this work.
**The fair maps movement played a critical role in preventing anti-democracy forces from rigging the midterm elections** — just like we played a critical, years-long role in establishing the foundation for fair maps.
_**Where We Were Two Years Ago**_
In 2024, voters went to the polls under one of the fairest national congressional maps in a generation. Our movement had made real progress, but that progress inspired fierce backlash from anti-democracy forces.
Extremist politicians didn’t want to compete on a level playing field. So last summer, they kicked off a national redistricting crisis, scrambling to draw new maps that would give them a partisan advantage in the 2026 midterms.
The Supreme Court then supercharged the crisis by gutting critical Voting Rights Act protections in the spring of 2026, clearing the way for last-minute changes to maps that undermined fair representation for Black and brown voters.
**But the fair maps movement rose up to meet these challenges head-on.** Ordinary Americans took time out of their busy schedules to contact their lawmakers, show up to protests, and make their voices heard.
People stood up and spoke out in Indiana, South Carolina, and Georgia to successfully put public pressure on their state legislatures — and they helped block new gerrymanders.
Utahns won a years-long fight to enforce redistricting reforms and ensure they had a fair map. Ohioans forced lawmakers to abandon an extreme redraw and agree to a compromise map.
Missourians took a new gerrymander to court, gathered thousands of signatures to stop it from being used this fall, and rejected it once and for all on Election Day.
And volunteers across the country reached out to voters in states with key elections — where fair maps and voting rights were at stake — to make sure more people had the information they needed in order to vote.
_**Over the Next Two Months**_
Before leaving office and losing power, lame-duck lawmakers could rush to draw new gerrymanders. They’d be counting on our movement to be tired after the elections, to be complacent in the glow of previous pro-democracy victories, and to have taken our eyes off the ball.
We’re going to prove them wrong. Whenever and wherever new attacks on democracy rear their heads, we will be ready to mobilize activists like you to fight back, just like our movement helped prevent gerrymanders across key states in the past two years.
_**Over the Next Two Years**_
**The work must continue. We must continue to build our grassroots power — and seize every opportunity to advance significant pro-democracy reforms at the state and federal level. It won’t pay off overnight, but ultimately we will succeed. Gerrymandering’s days are numbered.**
[**It depends on people like you deciding to keep up the fight to ensure the survival of our democracy. If you can, make a donation today and let’s keep up this work.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143667601/660986699/-1059218283?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_FairMaps_email_20261118-AOTL-Tier1-FairMaps_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261118-AOTL-Tier1-FairMaps_&utm_campaign=FairMaps&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjU0YjAwMDRjLTgyZTMtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=n5QSsoW_us1aFHRGnSTZUwmw5tEUvq3NV4SNGEYchLQ=)

clean_body: Let’s take a look at how far we’ve come and where we must go. | Formerly All On The Line Peter, Coming out of a historically consequential midterm election, let’s take a look back at how far we’ve come in the last two years, where we need to be in the next two months, and where we can get ourselves two years from now. In 2026, despite an unprecedented mid-decade gerrymandering crisis across the country, and despite an onslaught of attempts to restrict access to the ballot, Americans were able to make their voices heard. That wasn’t an accident. People like you made it happen. People like you said no to extreme gerrymanders that threatened to silence their votes. People like you got involved with Redistricting Action — getting out the vote, joining volunteer trainings, testifying, speaking out to lawmakers, writing letters to the editor, pushing back against voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act, recruiting friends to join the fight, and making grassroots donations when possible to power this work. The fair maps movement played a critical role in preventing anti-democracy forces from rigging the midterm elections — just like we played a critical, years-long role in establishing the foundation for fair maps. Where We Were Two Years Ago In 2024, voters went to the polls under one of the fairest national congressional maps in a generation. Our movement had made real progress, but that progress inspired fierce backlash from anti-democracy forces. Extremist politicians didn’t want to compete on a level playing field. So last summer, they kicked off a national redistricting crisis, scrambling to draw new maps that would give them a partisan advantage in the 2026 midterms. The Supreme Court then supercharged the crisis by gutting critical Voting Rights Act protections in the spring of 2026, clearing the way for last-minute changes to maps that undermined fair representation for Black and brown voters. But the fair maps movement rose up to meet these challenges head-on. Ordinary Americans took time out of their busy schedules to contact their lawmakers, show up to protests, and make their voices heard. People stood up and spoke out in Indiana, South Carolina, and Georgia to successfully put public pressure on their state legislatures — and they helped block new gerrymanders. Utahns won a years-long fight to enforce redistricting reforms and ensure they had a fair map. Ohioans forced lawmakers to abandon an extreme redraw and agree to a compromise map. Missourians took a new gerrymander to court, gathered thousands of signatures to stop it from being used this fall, and rejected it once and for all on Election Day. And volunteers across the country reached out to voters in states with key elections — where fair maps and voting rights were at stake — to make sure more people had the information they needed in order to vote. Over the Next Two Months Before leaving office and losing power, lame-duck lawmakers could rush to draw new gerrymanders. They’d be counting on our movement to be tired after the elections, to be complacent in the glow of previous pro-democracy victories, and to have taken our eyes off the ball. We’re going to prove them wrong. Whenever and wherever new attacks on democracy rear their heads, we will be ready to mobilize activists like you to fight back, just like our movement helped prevent gerrymanders across key states in the past two years. Over the Next Two Years The work must continue. We must continue to build our grassroots power — and seize every opportunity to advance significant pro-democracy reforms at the state and federal level. It won’t pay off overnight, but ultimately we will succeed. Folks, it’s Chuck Hubbard. If we haven’t met before, I’m a native of northwestern North Carolina who's spent forty years of my career working in local journalism, and I'm also the Democrat who is currently up by 335 votes against Virginia Foxx, the second most-powerful Republican in the House.
_**This is the closest House race in the entire country, and it could also be one of the most important.**_
As Chair of the Rules Committee, Virginia Foxx directly **blocked the House from voting on Trump’s tariffs and the release of the Epstein files.** When Elon Musk and DOGE ransacked our federal government last year, she stood by and cheered them on. She’s made a name for herself yelling at reporters to shut up and screaming at staff for using the wrong elevator. And for twenty years, she’s stepped on the backs of working people in order to climb the ladder in Washington, DC, all while making millions playing the stock market.
Meanwhile, I spent my career reporting the truth at the local newspaper my grandfather started after WWI. I always made an effort to bring my readers just the facts without any bias. In that same spirit, my team and I are working around the clock to make sure every legal ballot in this race counts, because no matter who they voted for, all of our neighbors deserve to be heard.
For the first time in decades, North Carolina’s Fifth District will be represented by a Democrat. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work to lower costs and fight corruption in Washington – but Republicans are going to do all they can to ensure this doesn’t happen. They’re going to challenge every single vote.
[**Just 335 votes could end Virginia Foxx’s political career and the decades of nastiness – but this week will be the most critical of the campaign. I need your help now to ensure we have the resources required to defend this seat and make sure our neighbors are heard. Can I count on you to chip in a few dollars today? Even just $5, $10, or $25 can help us and Equal Opportunity Now to defend this seat.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143668383/660988409/-1898432515?refcode=261118_hubbard_331&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGVmY2EyZS04M2UzLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TdCW1C6ASya0PU4_2ZhAPHWDVRXKiQv-saGMwvS3RkQ=)

name: Andrew Sypher, Turning Point USA
subject: We’re trying to keep up
body:
I want to give you a picture of what’s really happening right now

| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdCA8BmMXFJFWSCkuipQiJRrsgR0dYMc2d8rbR5vdF7h2_nyj-X6_3-Y35J3P7QceNHLOc8rzJyUq6S-fWwnvRPGKM7SgaylraWZ0hT9o7rDyYw_SrKaiUQ62b8EqsNV91ItdQINq2xXdAAPoVQ99C0a2hvwgKx4fPCmlkVb2YBq0Zmn10ik0nuwKomuv6LFQw2dmT9mFEGPYubDLTUhbtY_3UmIW6puAScCUyV2JGjzJh9K4cAiYypVOPrc6Bj5LfWUUMA22X5d-oNqSVXVHHmtLpGpczbr2JEkTCjXlcCVHswuehLp9__VTaiUBBOirHPNBnq9DqBsdyPur-FwR6nbH5DG_z-j-vFoOj4i8nULdSrwyPh1yPv57fQ0VSg9klUYfP3nfOetBdO32OPF4qCpfzedjhH8BAAD__6E1nYo)
---
| | Friend,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdCA8BmMXFJFWSCkuipQiJRrsgR0dYMc2d8rbR5vdF7h2_nyj-X6_3-Y35J3P7QceNHLOc8rzJyUq6S-fWwnvRPGKM7SgaylraWZ0hT9o7rDyYw_SrKaiUQ62b8EqsNV91ItdQINq2xXdAAPoVQ99C0a2hvwgKx4fPCmlkVb2YBq0Zmn10ik0nuwKomuv6LFQw2dmT9mFEGPYubDLTUhbtY_3UmIW6puAScCUyV2JGjzJh9K4cAiYypVOPrc6Bj5LfWUUMA22X5d-oNqSVXVHHmtLpGpczbr2JEkTCjXlcCVHswuehLp9__VTaiUBBOirHPNBnq9DqBsdyPur-FwR6nbH5DG_z-j-vFoOj4i8nULdSrwyPh1yPv57fQ0VSg9klUYfP3nfOetBdO32OPF4qCpfzedjhH8BAAD__6E1nYo)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdCA8BmMXFJFWSCkuipQiJRrsgR0dYMc2d8rbR5vdF7h2_nyj-X6_3-Y35J3P7QceNHLOc8rzJyUq6S-fWwnvRPGKM7SgaylraWZ0hT9o7rDyYw_SrKaiUQ62b8EqsNV91ItdQINq2xXdAAPoVQ99C0a2hvwgKx4fPCmlkVb2YBq0Zmn10ik0nuwKomuv6LFQw2dmT9mFEGPYubDLTUhbtY_3UmIW6puAScCUyV2JGjzJh9K4cAiYypVOPrc6Bj5LfWUUMA22X5d-oNqSVXVHHmtLpGpczbr2JEkTCjXlcCVHswuehLp9__VTaiUBBOirHPNBnq9DqBsdyPur-FwR6nbH5DG_z-j-vFoOj4i8nULdSrwyPh1yPv57fQ0VSg9klUYfP3nfOetBdO32OPF4qCpfzedjhH8BAAD__6E1nYo)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdCA8BmMXFJFWSCkuipQiJRrsgR0dYMc2d8rbR5vdF7h2_nyj-X6_3-Y35J3P7QceNHLOc8rzJyUq6S-fWwnvRPGKM7SgaylraWZ0hT9o7rDyYw_SrKaiUQ62b8EqsNV91ItdQINq2xXdAAPoVQ99C0a2hvwgKx4fPCmlkVb2YBq0Zmn10ik0nuwKomuv6LFQw2dmT9mFEGPYubDLTUhbtY_3UmIW6puAScCUyV2JGjzJh9K4cAiYypVOPrc6Bj5LfWUUMA22X5d-oNqSVXVHHmtLpGpczbr2JEkTCjXlcCVHswuehLp9__VTaiUBBOirHPNBnq9DqBsdyPur-FwR6nbH5DG_z-j-vFoOj4i8nULdSrwyPh1yPv57fQ0VSg9klUYfP3nfOetBdO32OPF4qCpfzedjhH8BAAD__6E1nYo)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**[Each activism kit costs $25 to pack and ship to a student chapter. Will you put one into a student's hands today?](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdCA8BmMXFJFWSCkuipQiJRrsgR0dYMc2d8rbR5vdF7h2_nyj-X6_3-Y35J3P7QceNHLOc8rzJyUq6S-fWwnvRPGKM7SgaylraWZ0hT9o7rDyYw_SrKaiUQ62b8EqsNV91ItdQINq2xXdAAPoVQ99C0a2hvwgKx4fPCmlkVb2YBq0Zmn10ik0nuwKomuv6LFQw2dmT9mFEGPYubDLTUhbtY_3UmIW6puAScCUyV2JGjzJh9K4cAiYypVOPrc6Bj5LfWUUMA22X5d-oNqSVXVHHmtLpGpczbr2JEkTCjXlcCVHswuehLp9__VTaiUBBOirHPNBnq9DqBsdyPur-FwR6nbH5DG_z-j-vFoOj4i8nULdSrwyPh1yPv57fQ0VSg9klUYfP3nfOetBdO32OPF4qCpfzedjhH8BAAD__6E1nYo)**
---
[ **Sponsor an Activism Kit**
**Make Your Gift Here**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdCA8BmMXFJFWSCkuipQiJRrsgR0dYMc2d8rbR5vdF7h2_nyj-X6_3-Y35J3P7QceNHLOc8rzJyUq6S-fWwnvRPGKM7SgaylraWZ0hT9o7rDyYw_SrKaiUQ62b8EqsNV91ItdQINq2xXdAAPoVQ99C0a2hvwgKx4fPCmlkVb2YBq0Zmn10ik0nuwKomuv6LFQw2dmT9mFEGPYubDLTUhbtY_3UmIW6puAScCUyV2JGjzJh9K4cAiYypVOPrc6Bj5LfWUUMA22X5d-oNqSVXVHHmtLpGpczbr2JEkTCjXlcCVHswuehLp9__VTaiUBBOirHPNBnq9DqBsdyPur-FwR6nbH5DG_z-j-vFoOj4i8nULdSrwyPh1yPv57fQ0VSg9klUYfP3nfOetBdO32OPF4qCpfzedjhH8BAAD__6E1nYo)
---
Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines.

That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward.

That's how this movement actually scales.

Because the reality is, the demand is here now.

_Palestinian journalist and Drop Site contributor Mujahed Al-Saadi was born and raised in the Jenin refugee camp. A seasoned reporter, he has covered the occupied West Bank since 2012, focusing on Jenin and the surrounding areas._
_In September 2024, he was violently arrested by Israeli authorities from his home and thrown into prison where he was held for nearly two years in administrative detention without charge or trial. You can read his account of his brutal imprisonment[here](https://substack.com/redirect/e9c4fb37-1b2d-4a06-840d-cf6989b45361?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
_During Al-Saadi 's 22 months behind bars, Jenin underwent a violent transformation. The Israeli military launched a massive military operation targeting the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams refugee camps in the northern West Bank, displacing over 30,000 people in the single largest displacement of Palestinians in the territory since 1967._
_After his release in July 2026, Al-Saadi returned to Jenin to find not only his hometown devastated but his ability to work as a journalist almost impossible._
_In this dispatch, Al-Saadi recounts the changes to his work and to Jenin, particularly the destruction of the camp, from the perspective of someone who was locked up and prevented from witnessing it as it was unfolding, and instead was forced to contend with the entirety of the transformation all at once._
_-- Sharif Abdel Kouddous_

The view from Mujahed Al-Saadi's house in the Al-Saada neighborhood west of Jenin city at dawn on August 13, 2026. Jenin refugee camp, with all its residents displaced by the Israeli military, appears as a dark patch in the background. Photo by Mujahed Al Saadi.
_Story by Mujahed Al-Saadi_
JENIN, occupied West Bank--I didn't expect Jenin could change so much in the 22 months I was locked up in the occupation's prisons. When I returned after my release in July, it was as if an earthquake had struck the entire area--not only had the Jenin refugee camp been destroyed, emptied, and occupied, but the landscape of journalism had entirely shifted.
The first time I went back into the field to report, it was overwhelming. There was a different kind of pressure, with the sheer volume of the news and the struggle to verify it, and the difficulty of reaching places the occupation had targeted.
Over the years, I have worked for several local and international news organisations covering different parts of the occupied West Bank, but these past few months have been the most difficult I've experienced as a journalist working in the field for over a decade.
When I donned my press vest for the first time after nearly two years, I had been away from reporting, or even being aware of the news, during one of the most difficult and consequential periods since the occupation of Palestine began.
I would say that working as a journalist in the West Bank today, particularly reporting from the northern cities like Jenin, has become one of the most dangerous jobs in the world.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bb10ed63-6f87-4a00-8d12-164132146c23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Mujahed Al-Saadi reporting from Jenin on September 8, 2024, less than two weeks before his arrest by Israeli forces. Photo courtesy of Mujahed Al-Saadi.
Jenin governorate, where I primarily work, is now carved up into several areas that are divided and difficult to reach because of newly established checkpoints and the construction of new settlements and outposts. Some 14 settlements and Israeli military camps have been established in the towns surrounding the city of Jenin, and trying to access the scenes of incidents has become an ordeal, particularly with the frequent road closures. At these checkpoints, in addition to checking identification documents, people's phones and social media accounts are inspected. Journalistic equipment is frequently destroyed, confiscated, or stolen.
Conditions on the ground in this area have always been extremely dangerous, but since I returned to work, it's clear the risks have increased significantly. The occupation is tightening its grip more and more. Troops open fire without any justification, detain journalists for hours, prevent them from moving freely, and subject them to interrogation.
We also have to be careful about every word we write or every image we publish online. Even just writing about settlements, for example, or the history of Palestine can make you a target of Israeli security forces. This is what has changed over the past two years--it was still risky before, but there was greater freedom to report and express opinions.
Just accessing information has become almost impossible and relaying it dangerous. Reaching the places targeted by the occupation, such as bedouin and rural communities around Jenin and the people whose stories we try to tell, is difficult with all the closures. It is then a risk simply to share information or detail the repeated attacks against them. A journalist can even be detained simply for having certain media in their possession, let alone for publishing it.
Two years ago, I could work and move around the governorate relatively normally. Today, if I want to write an article or film a story about the plight of the Jenin refugee camp, for example, and the people that once called it home, I may need more than two days just to coordinate with those families, who have been displaced to villages surrounding the city, with occupation forces stationed between these villages and in some neighborhoods on the outskirts of the city.
Satellite imagery of Jenin refugee camp recorded before and after the Israeli military's assault on the camp dubbed "Operation Iron Wall." LEFT: Jenin refugee camp on October 24, 2024. RIGHT: Jenin refugee camp on November 14, 2026, after most of the camp's residents were forcibly displaced, hundreds of homes destroyed or heavily damaged, and alleys and roads bulldozed and widened. Images courtesy of Planet Labs PBC.
Jenin--both the city and the refugee camp within it--have been transformed. The city is no longer the "Mother of Gardens," as it was once known. The refugee camp, a tight-knit community of families who had lived there for decades, has been emptied, its residents scattered, once again facing displacement, homelessness, and oppression.
The city and the camp had already been living through a particularly harsh security situation in the years before, with repeated Israeli incursions, armed clashes, and systematic damage to roads and civilian infrastructure. At the same time, internal tensions with the Palestinian Authority (PA) were escalating. On December 5, 2024, the PA launched a large-scale [military campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/3a9e8a40-1083-4ebc-85c0-e8db57eee3d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Jenin dubbed "Operation Homeland Protection," which it claimed was to maintain security and establish the rule of law. The devastating campaign continued until January 21, 2025.
The entire governorate was affected, and the local economy was hit hard. In July 2024, the Palestinian Ministry of Economy reported that some 53% of companies and businesses in the governorate had been affected amid a sharp decline in demand and production capacity. Some were forced to shut down completely, others partially.
But the biggest turning point came on January 21, 2025, just hours after PA forces withdrew from the camp, when Israeli forces launched a massive assault on the camp, which later expanded to the Tulkarem and Nur Shams refugee camps. "Operation Iron Wall" forcibly displaced 33,000 Palestinians from their homes in the three camps and destroyed or severely damaged homes, roads, water and sewage systems, telecommunication networks, and other civilian infrastructure. The basic necessities of life were no longer there. Israeli forces remain in the camps and have prevented residents from returning.
The security situation inside Jenin camp used to be shaped by the presence of multiple armed groups, tensions between the PA and these factions, and repeated Israeli military operations. When I returned to Jenin, the entire security equation had completely changed.
In 2024, despite the damage and destruction caused by repeated Israeli incursions, the camp was still alive and densely crowded with residents spilling out of streets, alleyways, homes, and public gathering places. By 2026, the camp was empty--large parts of its landscape had been transformed by bulldozing, home demolitions, the construction of new roads, and the removal of entire sections of the built environment. At night, the camp is now a patch of darkness surrounded by the other lit areas of the city--a swathe of land emptied of life.
Over 600 days of displacement have taken a heavy toll on the camp's former residents: their hearts have grown old, their bodies have aged, and economic hardship has exhausted them. The camp has been changed, and the people who once lived there have too.
But the changes are not limited to the camp itself. An Israeli military base and observation post has been established in the Al-Jabriyat neighborhood in the heart of the city, an area classified as Area A under the Oslo Accords that technically should fall under full control of the PA. Occupation forces deployed throughout the city have turned Jenin upside down.
The economy has been devastated. The camp, once an integral part of the city's economic and social fabric, has been cut off. Movement restrictions have disrupted access to workplaces, markets, and agricultural land, while the loss of income has left affected families increasingly dependent on humanitarian aid that arrives only intermittently.
During the two years of my imprisonment it wasn't just the security and economy of Jenin refugee camp that had changed, but the very place itself. A crowded camp where conflict once erupted between multiple parties has become an empty landscape with traces of war and displacement in its streets, homes, and infrastructure. The camp is no longer what it once was, and neither are we.

A seasoned reporter, he has covered the occupied West Bank since 2012, focusing on Jenin and the surrounding areas. In September 2024, he was violently arrested by Israeli authorities from his home and thrown into prison where he was held for nearly two years in administrative detention without charge or trial. You can read his account of his brutal imprisonment. During Al-Saadi 's 22 months behind bars, Jenin underwent a violent transformation. The Israeli military launched a massive military operation targeting the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams refugee camps in the northern West Bank, displacing over 30,000 people in the single largest displacement of Palestinians in the territory since 1967. After his release in July 2026, Al-Saadi returned to Jenin to find not only his hometown devastated but his ability to work as a journalist almost impossible. When I returned after my release in July, it was as if an earthquake had struck the entire area--not only had the Jenin refugee camp been destroyed, emptied, and occupied, but the landscape of journalism had entirely shifted. body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTQxMDU3MTIS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU4MDA5NDM2OAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
DEVELOPING... the Supreme Court has just given approval for the Trump
administration to continue building its border wall in Big Bend National Park in
Texas, waiving laws focused on environmental protections. The move clears the way for bulldozing and construction in some of the most
pristine parts of the national park. Even Republicans in the state are urging
the administration not to move forward. With just weeks before a new Congress takes office, Trump is trying to advance
some of his worst policies while he still has a MAGA Republican majority in the
House and Senate. We need the opposition to be swift and fierce, but we need your help: The best thing you can do to help right now is to renew your LCV membership for just $15 to help stop Trump’s corrupt land grabs >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/z9e0fz7e~ RENEW YOUR LCV MEMBERSHIP >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/w_ywTK3~ Here’s the thing: the border wall in Big Bend isn’t just bad for the environment
— it’s wildly unpopular. Ranchers, conservationists, environmental
organizations, and local landowners have all banded together to oppose the
project. And time and time again, when Trump feels serious pressure, he backs
down. We need him to feel that pressure now — and stop the bulldozers from destroying
any more of this irreplaceable landscape.Your LCV membership helps build that pressure, hold elected leaders accountable,
and push for pro-environment policies at every level of government. Every dollar truly makes a big difference, so we’re asking: Save Big Bend. Renew your membership today. $15 is all it takes >> https://links.messages.lcv. RENEW YOUR LCV MEMBERSHIP >> https://links.messages.lcv. Thank you for everything you do for people and our planet, Peter. Sincerely, Chris Brooks

What did Democrats do well? What could we have done better? We're counting on _you_ for this critical feedback so we're in the best possible position to keep the Senate majority blue.

Please, it's absolutely critical we hear from as many people as possible ‐‐ **[share your thoughts about the midterms with the DSCC right now so we can start building our strategy for 2028. subject: Right-wing billionaires control the media. The list is staggering.
body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1007&refcode=20261118_Mission_T1&akid=333%2E344797%2E_TvgyO ]COURIER Newsroom

Peter,

The media landscape has changed dramatically since Trump returned to the
White House.

Here’s the reality most Americans don’t fully see:

A small group of Trump-backing, billionaire-aligned corporations now
controls the vast majority of what Americans see, hear, search, and
consume as news. Cable networks. Social media platforms. Search engines.
AI tools. Streaming services. Everything.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/14724?t=1003&refcode=20261118_Mission_T1&akid=333%2E344797%2E_TvgyO ]With over 11 million followers and newsrooms in 20 states, COURIER is
one of the fastest-growing media networks in the country. We are fiercely
independent — and we rely on grassroots support, not sucking up to Trump
or a billionaire boardroom, to make our reporting freely available to
anyone who needs it.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/14724?t=1004&refcode=20261118_Mission_T1&akid=333%2E344797%2E_TvgyO ]Donate

Here’s what the new, right-wing-dominated media ecosystem looks like:

* Larry and David Ellison are top Trump donors who control massive
entertainment and distribution platforms through Paramount, CBS News,
Pluto TV, TikTok — and now CNN too.
* Mark Zuckerberg gave $1 million to Trump’s inaugural fund and has been
a dinner guest at Mar-a-Lago. He controls the entire Meta ecosystem —
Facebook, Instagram, Threads, WhatsApp, and Messenger — platforms that
continue to algorithmically reward outrage, disinformation, and
right-wing political content.
* The Sinclair family controls one of the largest local TV affiliate
networks in the country. Conservative backers, they push coordinated
right-wing talking points across CBS, NBC, ABC, Fox, and CW local
stations nationwide.
* Jeff Bezos owns Amazon, The Washington Post, Prime Video, Twitch, and
Wondery. He has spent much of Trump’s second term aligning his
business empire with the Trump administration.
* Elon Musk, who led the destruction of the federal government under
DOGE, owns X. He has used the platform to actively boost Trump,
reinstate extremist accounts, and turn it into a MAGA megaphone.

We could go on and on. But here’s the point.

Too many legacy outlets are still pretending every issue has “both sides,”
even as Trump and his billionaire media allies erode democracy to push a
far-right agenda.

For billionaire owners, that kind of coverage is about access and profits
over any obligation to the public.

Stories that challenge power don’t get banned — they get buried under
cowardly journalism.

That’s why COURIER exists.

Our mission is to keep courage and truth alive in these dangerous times.
We exist to:

* Confront MAGA propaganda head-on
* Call authoritarian threats what they are
* Build a media infrastructure strong enough to win the information war
as we enter the final two years of Trump's term

Since 2025, COURIER has surged in reach and impact across the digital
spaces where the right wing has long dominated. Millions are turning to
our reporting because they know we’re telling the truth others won’t. But
this kind of journalism only survives with the support of readers like
you.

name: Scott Peters
subject: We made them a promise
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott Peters for Congress
body:
I'm pushing for a vote to protect our Afghan allies. Join me.
---
| | Hey Peter, **Afghans who risked their lives alongside American troops are now facing deportation to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan.** These are people who served as interpreters, protected our servicemembers, and helped Americans do their jobs in dangerous places. We promised to stand by them. Sending them back to face retaliation breaks that promise. **This is personal to me.** In August 2021, as Kabul fell, San Diego Navy veteran Shawn VanDiver called me about an Afghan friend surrounded by the Taliban. His friend made it out. That call helped spark what became #AfghanEvac, a coalition that has worked ever since to protect our Afghan allies. On Veterans Day, I joined veterans and Afghan allies at the Capitol to press Congress to act. Now we need to turn that pressure into a vote. I cosponsor the bipartisan Afghanistan TPS Act, which would restore temporary protection from deportation for eligible Afghans through July 2029, with full background and security checks. I've also signed a discharge petition to force a House vote. name: Governor-elect Aaron Ford
subject: Vote Forward is doing critical work for our democracy. Here’s how you can get involved
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
Election season is over. But talking with voters doesn’t have to stop here.
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1282%2E127862%2EilYAAR)
Hi there,
Governor-Elect Aaron Ford here. I’m reaching out to you about an important program that our partners at Swing Left and their nonpartisan affiliate organization, Vote Forward, are running in 2027 that will create opportunities for volunteers to engage communities and build trust in democracy year-round.
Elections offer a unique opportunity for candidates to talk deeply with voters. But that work of listening to constituents doesn’t need to end on Election Day.
**To help bridge that gap, Vote Forward is launching year-round nonpartisan canvassing, aimed at listening to voters and connecting them with their elected representatives.**
Through door-to-door and high-traffic (community events) canvassing, volunteers will:
* Have open-ended, deep-listening conversations to learn what’s going on in people’s lives.
* Connect people to their elected representatives to solve their challenges.
* Help new voters register and understand how to participate in our democracy.
* Explain how policies and legislation in Washington help or harm voters and their families.

The information and voter insights gathered in these canvasses will be shared with elected representatives to help them stay in touch with their constituents, respond to community concerns, and inform their leadership and communications.
**[If you’re interested in learning more and getting involved, click here to visit Vote Forward today.](https://votefwd.org/join?utm_source=partner&utm_medium=af&utm_campaign=gt-x)**
**[Learn More ››](https://votefwd.org/join?utm_source=partner&utm_medium=af&utm_campaign=gt-x)**
Together, we can rebuild trust in our democracy and build a government that delivers for the people.
— Governor-Elect Aaron Ford

name: Andrew Sypher, Turning Point USA
subject: This might be a sign of something bigger
body:
I want to give you a picture of what’s really happening right now

| | | [](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGOnDAMhp8m3BhNYgjhwKHqCKmH3WuPyCQOWCUJJWH6-hU78wR7s-zf_y9__v0xfSBvHJdPDDTYJ09HnsrKOfCylpkw8xKTzylQWXlSd6VrKWtpJrSFnzQ1WLnBOg2qokF2fXsH3TayWofWk529JWvAmsbMrgfXgFHGem0NQcXDZSelNErKFvQNoJ-19gYMWvJdJ5r7uTsslG82xUzHE69MjjFdVYo3m0K1DWspexbwQ6hRqDGTPQ-6YSSXyqUQaiznETku9Z44lvrMKNTY9a2f247qnnqoG3JY90RQozfetyRJEwoYczoPS5NNjgQ8fv76lBqkbITSZwlTIMdnEPCggLy9m68VAY8VD4f5z4T273tkMezISxTwKPuZ8YWRc_hC-xYVOi7L6hjc_o-3jbO-WCxXxNfJ5Zufeg7qfwAAAP__M4Gl9A)

| | Friend,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGOnDAMhp8m3BhNYgjhwKHqCKmH3WuPyCQOWCUJJWH6-hU78wR7s-zf_y9__v0xfSBvHJdPDDTYJ09HnsrKOfCylpkw8xKTzylQWXlSd6VrKWtpJrSFnzQ1WLnBOg2qokF2fXsH3TayWofWk529JWvAmsbMrgfXgFHGem0NQcXDZSelNErKFvQNoJ-19gYMWvJdJ5r7uTsslG82xUzHE69MjjFdVYo3m0K1DWspexbwQ6hRqDGTPQ-6YSSXyqUQaiznETku9Z44lvrMKNTY9a2f247qnnqoG3JY90RQozfetyRJEwoYczoPS5NNjgQ8fv76lBqkbITSZwlTIMdnEPCggLy9m68VAY8VD4f5z4T273tkMezISxTwKPuZ8YWRc_hC-xYVOi7L6hjc_o-3jbO-WCxXxNfJ5Zufeg7qfwAAAP__M4Gl9A)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGOnDAMhp8m3BhNYgjhwKHqCKmH3WuPyCQOWCUJJWH6-hU78wR7s-zf_y9__v0xfSBvHJdPDDTYJ09HnsrKOfCylpkw8xKTzylQWXlSd6VrKWtpJrSFnzQ1WLnBOg2qokF2fXsH3TayWofWk529JWvAmsbMrgfXgFHGem0NQcXDZSelNErKFvQNoJ-19gYMWvJdJ5r7uTsslG82xUzHE69MjjFdVYo3m0K1DWspexbwQ6hRqDGTPQ-6YSSXyqUQaiznETku9Z44lvrMKNTY9a2f247qnnqoG3JY90RQozfetyRJEwoYczoPS5NNjgQ8fv76lBqkbITSZwlTIMdnEPCggLy9m68VAY8VD4f5z4T273tkMezISxTwKPuZ8YWRc_hC-xYVOi7L6hjc_o-3jbO-WCxXxNfJ5Zufeg7qfwAAAP__M4Gl9A)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGOnDAMhp8m3BhNYgjhwKHqCKmH3WuPyCQOWCUJJWH6-hU78wR7s-zf_y9__v0xfSBvHJdPDDTYJ09HnsrKOfCylpkw8xKTzylQWXlSd6VrKWtpJrSFnzQ1WLnBOg2qokF2fXsH3TayWofWk529JWvAmsbMrgfXgFHGem0NQcXDZSelNErKFvQNoJ-19gYMWvJdJ5r7uTsslG82xUzHE69MjjFdVYo3m0K1DWspexbwQ6hRqDGTPQ-6YSSXyqUQaiznETku9Z44lvrMKNTY9a2f247qnnqoG3JY90RQozfetyRJEwoYczoPS5NNjgQ8fv76lBqkbITSZwlTIMdnEPCggLy9m68VAY8VD4f5z4T273tkMezISxTwKPuZ8YWRc_hC-xYVOi7L6hjc_o-3jbO-WCxXxNfJ5Zufeg7qfwAAAP__M4Gl9A)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**[Each activism kit costs $25 to pack and ship to a student chapter. Will you put one into a student's hands today?](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGOnDAMhp8m3BhNYgjhwKHqCKmH3WuPyCQOWCUJJWH6-hU78wR7s-zf_y9__v0xfSBvHJdPDDTYJ09HnsrKOfCylpkw8xKTzylQWXlSd6VrKWtpJrSFnzQ1WLnBOg2qokF2fXsH3TayWofWk529JWvAmsbMrgfXgFHGem0NQcXDZSelNErKFvQNoJ-19gYMWvJdJ5r7uTsslG82xUzHE69MjjFdVYo3m0K1DWspexbwQ6hRqDGTPQ-6YSSXyqUQaiznETku9Z44lvrMKNTY9a2f247qnnqoG3JY90RQozfetyRJEwoYczoPS5NNjgQ8fv76lBqkbITSZwlTIMdnEPCggLy9m68VAY8VD4f5z4T273tkMezISxTwKPuZ8YWRc_hC-xYVOi7L6hjc_o-3jbO-WCxXxNfJ5Zufeg7qfwAAAP__M4Gl9A)**

Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines.

That's how this movement actually scales.

clean_body: I want to give you a picture of what’s really happening right now | | | | | Friend, I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible. Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them. They're already claimed. And we don't have extras. By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in. Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it. That's where things stand right now. We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment. And I don't say that lightly. Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down. The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing. Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back. We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there. And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet. That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens. And it's not isolated growth anymore. We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. What's different now is the pace. Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: ✅ Arkansas ✅ Florida ✅ Idaho ✅ Indiana ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Oklahoma ✅ South Carolina ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action. That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly. It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up. Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through. And right now, that's where we're stretched. We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. It turns a student who wants to speak up... into one who actually does. And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here." Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines. That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward. That's how this movement actually scales. Because the reality is, the demand is here now. The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it. And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward. One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you. If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now. Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school. This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it. And we don't take that lightly. I appreciate you taking the time to read this, and for everything you've already done to support this work. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. Friend, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture. But moments like this don't sustain themselves. If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple. We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. If you've already supported Turning Point USA in the past, thank you for carrying this movement forward every single day. If you haven't yet, I'm asking you to step in now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044 Pop Acta Media | Conservative Innovation PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 | _

name: Patty Murray
subject: a Democratic Senate majority 🎉THANK YOU
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY PEOPLE FOR PATTY MURRAY
body:
| | |
---
They just called Alaska for Mary Peltola, Peter. I want to start by saying **thank you.**

There will officially be 56 Senators in the Democratic caucus–that number was practically unthinkable a year ago today. Your support, hard work, donations, and belief in our democracy were absolutely what made that happen.

Republicans made historic cuts to health care so billionaires could get richer. They kicked millions of families and kids off SNAP. Republicans gave ICE millions of dollars for an out-of-control paramilitary that has arrested, detained, and assaulted U.S. citizens. And they stood by while Trump’s corruption reached historic levels, as he started a forever war with Iran, and when he put in place idiotic tariffs that drove up costs across the board.

The election was a clear message from the American people: lower costs, end the corruption, and end the war.

This is a generational shift in what people want America to look like, and I am ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work.

I take the trust you put in Democrats seriously and will hit the ground running to protect the power of the purse, lower costs, and hold Trump accountable for his corruption and cruelty.

But for today, I want to leave you with this:

Trump and Republicans wanted voters to be discouraged. They wanted you to think your voice and your vote didn’t matter. They had the money and the billionaires – Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars alone, for god’s sake.

But the way you turned out at the polls and supported Democrats across the country, you showed them that The People ARE what matter in a democracy.

This grassroots team punched way above its weight and made a big difference.

From the very bottom of my heart–thank you,

Patty Murray

Together with my colleagues Reps. Adelita Grijalva (AZ), Summer Lee (PA), and Melanie Stansbury (NM), I’m leading the effort to stop this dangerous bill that would allow unaccountable, greedy corporations to speed up data center and fracked natural gas pipeline construction.
This bill makes it easier to build fossil fuel infrastructure while undermining clean water and national environmental policy acts. It would also strip away Tribes’ and the general public’s right to give input and sue to stop polluting projects and to protect culturally significant areas.
Too often, we’re seeing local and state elected officials enter into non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with Big Tech over the construction of AI data centers ― hiding potential environmental impacts, harms to public health, and tax break packages for billion-dollar corporations. That’s why I’ve introduced the **_No Secret Deals Act_** to prohibit public officials and government agencies from entering into NDAs and hiding the true impacts of data centers on our communities.
**Growing up in southwest Detroit by the Marathon Oil Refinery and other corporate polluters, I know what it’s like to live in a frontline community treated as a sacrifice zone.** I will not stand by and watch as corporate polluters poison our air and water.

clean_body: I know what it’s like to live in a frontline community treated as a sacrifice zone. | | | Friend, Democrats and Republicans in the Senate are claiming that Congress needs to pass the so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act now, before the new Congress is sworn in in January. But this bill is more than 400 pages of bad ideas and empty promises. It’s a gift to Big Oil and Big Tech, and would super-charge fossil fuel and data center construction in our communities. This week, the Senate cleared the last procedural hurdle and could vote on this bill before Thanksgiving. | Together with my colleagues Reps. Adelita Grijalva (AZ), Summer Lee (PA), and Melanie Stansbury (NM), I’m leading the effort to stop this dangerous bill that would allow unaccountable, greedy corporations to speed up data center and fracked natural gas pipeline construction. This bill makes it easier to build fossil fuel infrastructure while undermining clean water and national environmental policy acts. It would also strip away Tribes’ and the general public’s right to give input and sue to stop polluting projects and to protect culturally significant areas. Too often, we’re seeing local and state elected officials enter into non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with Big Tech over the construction of AI data centers ― hiding potential environmental impacts, harms to public health, and tax break packages for billion-dollar corporations. That’s why I’ve introduced the No Secret Deals Act to prohibit public officials and government agencies from entering into NDAs and hiding the true impacts of data centers on our communities. Growing up in southwest Detroit by the Marathon Oil Refinery and other corporate polluters, I know what it’s like to live in a frontline community treated as a sacrifice zone. I will not stand by and watch as corporate polluters poison our air and water. With you in the fight for better, Rashida Rashida Tlaib for Congress PO Box 32777 Detroit, MI 48232 | Paid for by Rashida Tlaib for Congress | | Sent via . Friend, earlier this month, Donald Trump made a move that sends an unmistakable message about the direction of his administration: **he elevated Stephen Miller to serve as White House Chief of Staff.**
For nearly a decade, Stephen Miller has been one of Donald Trump’s most influential advisors and the primary architect behind some of the administration’s most divisive policies – from family separations at the border to the 2017 travel ban and militarized deportation raids on American streets.
According to reports, Miller is stepping into this role with every intention of doubling down on his aggressive agenda while refusing to compromise with Democrats or cooperate with congressional oversight and subpoenas.
**Elevating someone with a documented history of white nationalist associations, anti-immigrant rhetoric, and open hostility towards our civil rights to the most powerful staff position in the West Wing is deeply alarming.**

And why can't the people running our government give Americans a straight answer? That's exactly the kind of accountability work we're building Endless Urgency to do. * * *
Yesterday, I had a front-row seat to the absolute chaos and stupidity of this administration.
I was on MS NOW in the afternoon to talk about immigration and the 2028 race. Then Sean Duffy, our Secretary of Transportation, decided to go live to explain the meltdown at our airports and whatever the hell happened last week. Within about thirty seconds it was painfully obvious that he had no idea what the fuck he was talking about.
So when the producer asked if I wanted to respond, I was delighted. Because, of course I did.
I want to tell you two things about what I saw.
The first is that Duffy was lying, and he was bad at it. Their story, as far as I can tell, is that the whole thing came down to a router in Arkansas or some crazy shit like that. It didn't sound like an explanation. It sounded like an excuse. My wife put it perfectly. She said something like, "I don't know anything about technology. So what does it say that I understood everything Sean Duffy said and knew it was bullshit the minute it came out of his mouth?"
She's right. You didn't need a computer science degree to hear the BS. You just needed ears.
The second thing is the one I got to call out live on air. Not a lot of you know this, but over the last couple of years I ran an AI tech startup, and we sold it successfully last year. I'm not going to call myself a full-blown AI expert, but I know enough to be dangerous. And when someone who clearly knows nothing about it starts talking, I can smell the bullshit a mile away.
Duffy stood at that podium and said, with a straight face, that this was not an AI issue. It was a "predictive analytics" issue.
As if those are two different things.
Predictive analytics is a subset of artificial intelligence. That's like saying a square isn't a rectangle. The man in charge of America's transportation system, explaining a nationwide failure of America's transportation system, doesn't understand the basic vocabulary of the problem he's supposed to be fixing.
Now, I'm not going to pretend I know exactly what happened. My guess is they pushed some kind of AI technology out the door before it was ready, and it set off a cascade of failures that led to nationwide ground stops and stranded 1.5 million people at airports. Myself included.
And look, I'd like to think the people running this country understand what's going on in it, especially when something breaks and needs to be fixed. But that's not who we have. We have a collection of anti-intellectual, incompetent boobs who were picked by Donald Trump for one reason: he can control them, and they won't stand up to him on his grift.
* * *
#### _**[This is the part that makes me the angriest. Behind every government failure are real people paying the price. Parents missing time with their kids. Families stranded in airports. People losing money, missing important moments, and wondering whether anyone in Washington actually gives a damn. That's why Endless Urgency isn't just about calling out the latest ridiculous thing somebody in the Trump administration says. It's about following the money, asking who benefits, demanding accountability, and fighting for a government that puts ordinary people first. Paid subscribers make that possible. * * *
That matters, because this was a real national emergency. A million and a half people stuck in terminals. People missing weddings. Missing funerals. Missing the chance to sit at the bedside of someone they love while that person is dying. Real disruption to our economy. That's a crisis that requires serious leadership, and we don't have any.
You don't have to be an expert in everything to be a good leader. I don't expect the Transportation Secretary to understand every corner of artificial intelligence. What I do expect is that he surrounds himself with people who do, and listens to them before he steps in front of a camera.
But we don't have one Sean Duffy. We have thousands of them, from the Pentagon to the FBI, because Trump hires people he can control and they purge the qualified civil servants who actually know how this stuff works. Government isn't perfect. There's plenty we should cut and plenty we need to modernize. But these people hate government irrationally, because they need you to believe the reason your life isn't where it should be is that the government is on your back. Not that corrupt billionaires are robbing you blind.
And it's costing you. It cost me. I didn't get to see my son nearly as much as I should have this weekend because of their incompetence, and that ain't right. I also know I got off easy compared to a lot of you who were stuck far longer and missed things you can never get back.
Now Duffy wants $50 million to "fix" America's aviation infrastructure. If I were in Congress, I wouldn't give him a cent. They are frothing at the mouth over this mess, a mess they probably created themselves, intentionally or not, because it's the perfect excuse to push privatization. Watch what happens to that money. It goes to no-bid contracts. To their friends. To their families. To their corporate donors. The problem won't actually get solved. And when Democrats take over and clean it up, Republicans will turn around and claim credit for it anyway, because that's what they always do.
It's a grift on top of a grift. A con on top of a con. And you're the one paying for it, with your time, your money and your energy.
I've had it up to fucking here.
But I also know we'll get through this. In January, Democrats take back the House and the Senate. We get the gavels. We get subpoena power. And we investigate the shit out of these people and expose every last bit of it, because they are very, very bad human beings. America has fully touched the hot stove of what it means to have these bozo Republicans in charge, and that's our opening to show people that government can be a force for good in their lives again.
One more thing before I go. Yesterday at the Shorty Impact Awards, Endless Urgency won Best Newsletter and Best YouTube of the Year. I'm so grateful to everyone I get to work with, and to this community of people who read, watch and engage with what we make. We only get to do this work because of you, so this award belongs to all of you. I love you guys so much.
If you're as fed up as I am, this is where we fight back together. Become a paid subscriber and be part of the community that just won Best Newsletter of the Year.
With urgency,
--Mike
