clean_body: Yesterday, I went on national television to ask some pretty basic questions about the chaos at our airports. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? | | | Nov 18 | | | | | | | | | | | | Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know. Yesterday, I had a front-row seat to the absolute chaos and stupidity of this administration. I was on MS NOW in the afternoon to talk about immigration and the 2028 race. Then Sean Duffy, our Secretary of Transportation, decided to go live to explain the meltdown at our airports and whatever the hell happened last week. Within about thirty seconds it was painfully obvious that he had no idea what the fuck he was talking about. So when the producer asked if I wanted to respond, I was delighted. Because, of course I did. I want to tell you two things about what I saw. The first is that Duffy was lying, and he was bad at it. Their story, as far as I can tell, is that the whole thing came down to a router in Arkansas or some crazy shit like that. It didn't sound like an explanation. It sounded like an excuse. My wife put it perfectly. She said something like, "I don't know anything about technology. So what does it say that I understood everything Sean Duffy said and knew it was bullshit the minute it came out of his mouth?" She's right. You didn't need a computer science degree to hear the BS. You just needed ears. The second thing is the one I got to call out live on air. Not a lot of you know this, but over the last couple of years I ran an AI tech startup, and we sold it successfully last year. I'm not going to call myself a full-blown AI expert, but I know enough to be dangerous. And when someone who clearly knows nothing about it starts talking, I can smell the bullshit a mile away. Duffy stood at that podium and said, with a straight face, that this was not an AI issue. It was a "predictive analytics" issue. As if those are two different things. Predictive analytics is a subset of artificial intelligence. That's like saying a square isn't a rectangle. The man in charge of America's transportation system, explaining a nationwide failure of America's transportation system, doesn't understand the basic vocabulary of the problem he's supposed to be fixing. Now, I'm not going to pretend I know exactly what happened. My guess is they pushed some kind of AI technology out the door before it was ready, and it set off a cascade of failures that led to nationwide ground stops and stranded 1.5 million people at airports. Myself included. And look, I'd like to think the people running this country understand what's going on in it, especially when something breaks and needs to be fixed. But that's not who we have. We have a collection of anti-intellectual, incompetent boobs who were picked by Donald Trump for one reason: he can control them, and they won't stand up to him on his grift. * That matters, because this was a real national emergency. A million and a half people stuck in terminals. People missing weddings. Missing funerals. Missing the chance to sit at the bedside of someone they love while that person is dying. Real disruption to our economy. That's a crisis that requires serious leadership, and we don't have any. You don't have to be an expert in everything to be a good leader. I don't expect the Transportation Secretary to understand every corner of artificial intelligence. What I do expect is that he surrounds himself with people who do, and listens to them before he steps in front of a camera. But we don't have one Sean Duffy. We have thousands of them, from the Pentagon to the FBI, because Trump hires people he can control and they purge the qualified civil servants who actually know how this stuff works. Government isn't perfect. There's plenty we should cut and plenty we need to modernize. But these people hate government irrationally, because they need you to believe the reason your life isn't where it should be is that the government is on your back. Not that corrupt billionaires are robbing you blind. And it's costing you. It cost me. I didn't get to see my son nearly as much as I should have this weekend because of their incompetence, and that ain't right. I also know I got off easy compared to a lot of you who were stuck far longer and missed things you can never get back. Now Duffy wants $50 million to "fix" America's aviation infrastructure. If I were in Congress, I wouldn't give him a cent. They are frothing at the mouth over this mess, a mess they probably created themselves, intentionally or not, because it's the perfect excuse to push privatization. Watch what happens to that money. It goes to no-bid contracts. To their friends. To their families. To their corporate donors. The problem won't actually get solved. And when Democrats take over and clean it up, Republicans will turn around and claim credit for it anyway, because that's what they always do. It's a grift on top of a grift. A con on top of a con. And you're the one paying for it, with your time, your money and your energy. I've had it up to fucking here. But I also know we'll get through this. In January, Democrats take back the House and the Senate. We get the gavels. We get subpoena power. And we investigate the shit out of these people and expose every last bit of it, because they are very, very bad human beings. America has fully touched the hot stove of what it means to have these bozo Republicans in charge, and that's our opening to show people that government can be a force for good in their lives again. One more thing before I go. Yesterday at the Shorty Impact Awards, Endless Urgency won Best Newsletter and Best YouTube of the Year. I'm so grateful to everyone I get to work with, and to this community of people who read, watch and engage with what we make. We only get to do this work because of you, so this award belongs to all of you. I love you guys so much. If you're as fed up as I am, this is where we fight back together. Become a paid subscriber and be part of the community that just won Best Newsletter of the Year. [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek,

In a moment, I’m going to ask you to [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23757?t=1001&akid=958%2E245147%2EUgePxT ]chip in just $1 to support our
work here in Pennsylvania — but first, I want to explain why.

I know what you’re thinking: The election... just happened. What do you need
$1 for?

Here’s the answer: When our Democratic trifecta is sworn into office in
January, that won’t be the conclusion of our hard work,
Derek. It’ll be the beginning.

Hear me on this: Yes, we’re going to raise Pennsylvania’s minimum wage.

We’re going to enshrine abortion rights in our state Constitution.

We’re going to build more housing and fund mass transit in all 67 counties
across Pennsylvania.

But I don’t want to end there — and I know you don’t either.

This will be Pennsylvania’s first Democratic trifecta in over three
decades. And we can’t let this opportunity pass us by. The good people of
Pennsylvania — and hell, folks all across the country — demanded profound
change earlier this month.

No more half-measures. No more fifteen-point plans that never get
finished.

And Derek, I
intend to deliver on those demands. In every way I possibly can.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23757?t=1002&akid=958%2E245147%2EUgePxT ]But I can’t do it alone. Just as this team powered us to a historic
victory on November 3rd, we need to do the same in January once our
historic Democratic majority is officially sworn in. Please, will you rush
just $1 to make sure we make the most of this once-in-a-generation
opportunity here in Pennsylvania?

Thank you so much for your incredible support throughout this campaign. Because of grassroots supporters like you, we have made it to the runoff election for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District. [**Can you split a donation now between me and Blue Amp Action to help flip this seat blue?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/20210?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.11.18_PMoore-Bio_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=5&akid=4021%2E259176%2EU35uTN) My story began right here in Louisiana. I know what it means for a family to struggle. I know what it means to need an opportunity and what can happen when family, teachers, employers, mentors, and a community invest in someone and refuse to count them out.

I have spent my career showing up when our community needs someone to step up. I’m dedicated to fighting for working families, protecting rural hospitals, supporting our schools and teachers, and making sure small towns and rural parishes across LA-05 are never overlooked.

**I didn't get into public service because I was looking for another title. I got involved because I saw people and neighborhoods that needed somebody to show up.** As we head into this crucial final stretch, we need your help to reach every voter across the district. **Runoff elections are won on the ground, and every dollar we raise right now goes directly toward getting out the vote, running ads, and connecting with families across Louisiana's 5th District.**[**Will you split a donation between me and Blue Amp Action today to help power our campaign to victory in the runoff?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/20210?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.11.18_PMoore-Bio_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=6&akid=4021%2E259176%2EU35uTN) _If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Pat Moore and Blue Amp Action will go through immediately:_ | [DONATE $12 >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/20211?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.11.18_PMoore-Bio_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=7&akid=4021%2E259176%2EU35uTN)

name: Swing Left
subject: [Ground Truth Stories Report] What happens when we listen to dissatisfied Republicans?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Voters have given Democrats a chance, not necessarily their trust.
#
Hi there,
Not everyone who voted for a Republican this year was happy about it. In fact, some longtime Republican voters were so disappointed in their party (and Trump) that they were willing to vote for a Democrat. But they weren’t necessarily looking to switch parties. They wanted candidates who would listen to them and take their concerns seriously.
That’s one of the things we learned this year through Ground Truth, Swing Left’s innovative, listening-first voter contact program.
A few days ago, we shared stories from conversations with voters who were persuaded by their interaction with a Ground Truth volunteer. Today, we want to share a few of the stories volunteers heard from voters we call “dissatisfied Republicans”—people who have supported Republican candidates in the past but are questioning whether the party still represents them.
Thanks to this community, Ground Truth volunteers had tens of thousands of real, meaningful, and impactful conversations with voters. Instead of rushing through a script, they took the time to hear people out, and many conversations lasted upwards of 10 minutes.
Here are three of the stories they brought back:
> **A past GOP voter saw no Republican “deserving” of his vote**
> Emmett in Virginia has a lot of family in the military and was frustrated by how the troops were being treated, in addition to the fact that young people can’t build a solid life the way he could. He had voted Republican in the past, but didn’t see a Republican this year who deserved his vote. He wanted candidates “with a backbone.”
> **A longtime Republican called Trump “possibly the worst human being ever”**
> Kathleen in Omaha was a Republican for a long time and still leans conservative. However, she said Republicans have disappointed her by being dishonest and backing Trump. She was discouraged after news of another shooting and was afraid her one vote wouldn’t matter, but felt that everyone had to do their part. At the end of the conversation, she rated herself a 6 out of 10 for voting for a Democrat, with her main asks being integrity and a less divided country.
> **A former Navy clearance holder treats candidates like job interviews**
> Chester in Arizona is a retiree who used to conduct job interviews, and he reads candidate questionnaires as if each candidate were applying for a job. He voted for Trump before and has been very disappointed. He says a candidate has to earn his vote.
Although many of these voters had been longtime Republicans, most weren’t hostile to Democrats at all. They just felt like no one was paying attention to them and the issues they cared about.
Thanks to Ground Truth, we’re not losing what we learn from those conversations. These stories were made available to campaigns and party committees and saved so they can be used by candidates in the next election, too. By supporting this work, you’re helping campaigns reach and understand voters that they might otherwise overlook.
[**If you want to hear more about what we learned and what it means for the elections ahead, join us tomorrow night from 8-9 pm EST for our virtual post-election Inside Update call.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3289?t=23&akid=3453%2E1562180%2EkbYr2r)
**[RSVP Now »](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3289?t=24&akid=3453%2E1562180%2EkbYr2r)**
Thank you for reading. We’ll be back soon to share more stories from the field this year!
— The Swing Left Team

That’s me on the left, with my little brother and parents.
[That little boy could never have guessed that he’d be elected as your House Speaker-designate this morning.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143677687/661014400/1662333047?amount=15&refcode=20261118_em_fr_b2_jeffries_main_v5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzM0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzliMmQxYy1hNWUzLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5rChWudFkLIvcgor2Gv0EF7yVN2bgoowS6XTRGx-3fI=)
Here’s my story: My mom was a social worker and my dad was a substance abuse counselor. They raised us in Brooklyn in a predominantly Black neighborhood and we went to public schools.
They had one expectation for my brother and me: get an advanced degree and use it to serve others.
So I went to law school, and I made the pressing choice to run for office to improve people’s lives.
Today, I’m asking you to make a pressing choice too.
– We can either take our foot off the gas while Trump and extreme Republicans rake in funds from their billionaire donors to block the majority at every turn.
[– Or we can choose to rise up, help Democrats enter the new majority in a historic position of strength and ensure we have the resources to deliver on every last promise we made to the American people.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143677688/661014401/1662333047?amount=15&refcode=20261118_em_fr_b2_jeffries_main_v5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzM0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzliMmQxYy1hNWUzLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5rChWudFkLIvcgor2Gv0EF7yVN2bgoowS6XTRGx-3fI=)
[_Many Democrats spent down to $0 to achieve our victory and reclaim the House in this historic Blue Tsunami. Our urgent priority must now be to replenish our resources and leave no vulnerability for Republicans to exploit. I set an ambitious goal, 1,000 donations before midnight, to help Democrats regain our war chest and head into the new majority with undeniable strength to fend off every single attack Trump and Republicans will deploy to sabotage our work For the People. I’m asking you personally: Will you step up with $15 in this historic moment? >>_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143677689/661014402/1662333047?amount=15&refcode=20261118_em_fr_b2_jeffries_main_v5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzM0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzliMmQxYy1hNWUzLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5rChWudFkLIvcgor2Gv0EF7yVN2bgoowS6XTRGx-3fI=)
Here’s where things stand:
Life is way too expensive.
There are far too many people working hard and playing by the rules, and they can’t thrive and can barely survive.
That’s an unacceptable situation.
Millions of Americans are drowning in this failed Republican economy. The American people rejected MAGA extremism and voted for a Congress that will drive down the high cost of living.
We will fight for affordable gas, groceries, housing and healthcare.
We will fight to root out corruption and hold the crooks accountable.
We will fight to end the era of voter suppression and protect your right to vote.
[_I’m humbly asking: Will you help Democrats enter the new majority in a historic position of strength and ensure we have the resources to deliver on every last promise we made? >>_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143677690/661014403/1662333047?amount=15&refcode=20261118_em_fr_b2_jeffries_main_v5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzM0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzliMmQxYy1hNWUzLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5rChWudFkLIvcgor2Gv0EF7yVN2bgoowS6XTRGx-3fI=)

Veterans Day had me thinking about the people who helped shape the decision I made to put on the uniform. The people who taught me what service, responsibility, and accountability actually mean.
First, my mother, Ivette Palomo. She taught me responsibility and accountability. Two things that sound simple until it is time to live by them.
A.G. Ambrose Jr., U.S. Army, taught me that history is our greatest teacher.
Joe Rincon, U.S. Navy, and Buddy Palmer, U.S. Navy, taught me through their example that you never stop working to improve yourself. Pay attention to the details. Every day. No shortcuts.
And then there is my wife, Tiffany Soriano, who served our country in two branches of the military.
She taught me what it really means to embrace the suck.
Things will go wrong. Sometimes badly. Sometimes you will find yourself standing alone, facing something that is downright unjust. You can complain about it, let it break you, or find a way to keep moving forward.
**Embrace the suck. And do it with a smile.**
That lesson is worth more than I can put into words.
**To all my fellow veterans, thank you for your service. And to those who helped shape mine, thank you for the lessons.**
**Gavriel E. Soriano
U.S. Army**

subject: What should the new Congress prioritize?

body:
Have you had a chance to weigh in? Peter,

I wanted to reach out personally to make sure you've had a chance to fill out my priorities survey.

* **An Israeli analyst described Iran 's pattern as "calibrated escalation"** aimed at raising the costs of the ongoing U.S. blockade rather than sparking full-scale war, as CENTCOM separately tightened enforcement, warning ships accepting cargo transferred at sea from Iran-loaded vessels could be boarded or seized.

# **ABC News puts two journalists on leave over fake Trump Jr. story**
ABC News placed a desk assistant and his editor on paid leave after an Oct. 7 report falsely claimed Donald Trump Jr.'s firm, 1789 Capital, invested $2.5 billion in defense contractor Anduril -- when the actual figure was roughly $50 million; both are reportedly expected to be fired, **[the NY Post reports.](https://substack.com/redirect/af1221cd-6f7c-41b8-a246-c48bcd97a95a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Derek, the first post-midterms FEC deadline is in just 5 days and soon we’ll have to make our fundraising numbers public. We just won the _most historic midterm election in the history of the Democratic Party,_ so it’s critical that we continue growing our momentum as we start to prepare for 2028. **This deadline is our first opportunity to show Republicans that Democrats aren’t finished — we’re just getting started.** We know we’ve asked a lot of this team this year, but if you’re able to spare just $5, it would go a long way when our numbers go public. **Here’s what a $5 donation could power:**
* Ensuring our team of lawyers has the resources they need to take the Trump administration to court — _and win_ — at a moment’s notice.
* **Strengthening Democratic state parties.** Democrats were able to flip seats that Republicans held for years, powered by the DNC investing over $1 million per month directly into state parties, with additional funding going to places like Mississippi, Iowa, and South Carolina this year.
* **Mobilizing and training the next generation.** By 2028, Gen Z and millennial voters could make up more than half of the electorate, and it’s critical that Democrats continue to win over this key group of voters as we set our sights on the White House.

Derek, it may not seem like there’s much work to do right now, but staying consistent and continuing to build on our election-winning infrastructure is the only way we’ll keep securing more Democratic victories in 2027, 2028, and beyond.
